n3fa008537e8a: Electronic doping underpins many semiconductor applications but has remained elusive for lead halide perovskite nanocrystals because their high density and low formation energy of defects easily compensate introduced dopants. Here, we use electrochemical doping as a strategy to avoid doping compensation. Electrochemical injection of electrons or holes into the nanocrystal is compensated by surface-adsorbed electrolyte counterions, therefore not compromising crystal structure. We accomplished ambipolar (n- and p-type) doped CsPbBr3 nanocrystals with charge carrier concentrations ranging from intrinsic up to 4.8 × 1017 cm–3 (corresponding to 0.25 charges per nanocrystal). We show that electrochemical doping is reversible and stable at these free carrier concentrations. The extent of doping and stability are enabled by the use of lecithin, a zwitterionic ligand that strongly binds to the surface of the CsPbBr3 nanocrystals while still allowing ion and electron transfer. Lecithin stabilizes the surface atoms by shifting the potentials for Pb2+ reduction and Br– oxidation outside of the bandgap. The inferred surface-chemistry design rules for stable electrochemical doping can also serve as a guideline for developing CsPbBr3 nanocrystals stable under high free-carrier concentrations in optoelectronic devices, such as light-emitting diodes or electronically triggered quantum light sources.
nf069af42c647: Molecular dynamics simulations provide insight into inhibitor-protein interactions and support rational drug design; however, their accuracy depends on reliable molecular mechanics force field parameters and coarse-grained representations that retain relevant molecular features. Although force field parameter sets for biomacromolecules are well established, the chemical diversity of small-molecule inhibitors often requires the development of system-specific parameters. Here, we present a parametrization framework integrating quantum mechanical optimization, experimental benchmarking, and small-molecule coarse-graining, demonstrated using HIV-1 inhibitors targeting multiple stages of the viral replication cycle. We provide a curated data set of CHARMM-compatible force field parameters for 12 HIV-1 inhibitors and the HIV assembly cofactor inositol hexakisphosphate (IP6), together with geometry-optimized atomic structures and ligand restraint files. The resulting parameters are validated against experimental structural and thermodynamic benchmarks, including lenacapavir binding free energy estimates, through inhibitor-bound complex simulations. We demonstrate applications of the parameter data set by quantifying inhibitor-protein interactions, including the free-energy profile of an integrase strand transfer inhibitor interacting with the viral capsid lattice, and the binding energetics of an allosteric integrase inhibitor. Furthermore, we extend the all-atom inhibitor parameter data set through a novel coarse-graining strategy for small molecules that preserves key electrostatic features. The HIV-1 inhibitor force field parameter data set is a publicly available resource that establishes a unified framework for multiscale modeling of HIV-1 inhibitors and facilitates computational and structural biology studies of drug resistance and inhibitor design. More generally, the framework presented here is broadly applicable to small-molecule parametrization and multiscale simulations in other therapeutic and biomolecular contexts.
nd7dac975691d: Selective water oxidation in the presence of thermodynamically favored competing oxidation reactions remains a major challenge for photocatalytic systems. BiVO4 is one of the most efficient visible-light-responsive photocatalysts for water oxidation and exhibits high activity in Fe3+-mediated water-oxidation systems. However, although accumulated Fe2+ can introduce competing oxidation pathways under strongly acidic Fe3+/Fe2+ redox conditions, effective strategies for suppressing these processes and maintaining selective water oxidation remain largely unexplored. Here, we demonstrate a surface-engineering strategy that overcomes this limitation in BiVO4. Systematic investigation revealed that the poor activity of BiVO4 under strongly acidic Fe3+/Fe2+ conditions arises not only from catalyst degradation but also from competition with Fe2+ oxidation reactions. Surface modification of BiVO4 with W species, originally intended to improve acid durability, not only suppressed catalyst dissolution but also mitigated Fe2+-related performance losses, resulting in a marked enhancement of photocatalytic water oxidation. The activity enhancement correlated with highly dispersed surface W species localized near the outermost region of BiVO4. Notably, the highest activity was obtained before or near the onset of detectable WO3 crystallization, suggesting that the surface state of W species in this temperature range is more closely associated with the enhanced activity than crystalline WO3 domains under strongly acidic Fe3+/Fe2+ conditions. The optimized photocatalyst maintained efficient water oxidation while suppressing Fe2+-related performance losses, achieving an apparent quantum yield of 63% under Fe3+-based conditions and approximately 30% even under strongly acidic and concentrated Fe(ClO4)3 conditions relevant to hybrid water splitting. The optimized photocatalyst maintained selective water oxidation even as Fe2+ accumulated to approximately 100 mM, enabling nearly quantitative Fe3+-to-Fe2+ conversion under strongly acidic conditions. When incorporated into a photocatalysis–electrolysis hybrid system, the enhanced photocatalytic activity was directly translated into approximately 1.5-fold higher water-splitting performance than that of the benchmark H-Fe-Cs-WO3 system. These findings demonstrate that selective water oxidation can be maintained even in the presence of thermodynamically favored competing oxidation reactions through appropriate photocatalyst surface engineering, providing a useful strategy for photocatalysts operating in redox-mediated reaction environments, including photocatalysis–electrolysis hybrid water-splitting systems.
n48bb8642c5df: Impurities exert profound effects on electrocatalytic measurements and interpretations. Trace levels of contaminants introduced through electrolytes, electrodes, gases, or cell materials routinely generate false activity signals, accelerate degradation, and alter product selectivity. This review categorizes impurity effects by functional impact, including misleading activity, compromised stability, and shifted selectivity, and offers strategies to recognize, isolate, and mitigate these influences. We argue that reliable and reproducible electrocatalytic data require an impurity-aware approach, integrating both experimental protocols and systems engineering. By intentional design, impurities can be transformed from hidden liabilities into controlled variables, ensuring that reported advances in electrocatalysis reflect intrinsic catalyst properties and translate into durable energy technologies.
n2cca62a8ea7d: Layered CrSe2 reversibly accommodates approximately one potassium (K) per formula unit, but the structural origin of its rate-dependent capacity remains unresolved. Operando synchrotron X-ray diffraction (SXRD) reveals the sequential P-3m1-R3m-C2/m phase pathway during cycling at different current rates. The P-3m1/R3m transformation exhibits the lattice discontinuity and becomes incomplete when increasing the current rate, as directly observed by operando SXRD. Chemical K deintercalation and state-resolved impedance measurements provide complementary evidence for sluggish kinetics near the fully deintercalated regime. Restricting the upper cutoff voltage will sacrifice some capacity but will improve electrochemical cycling capacity retention. These findings identify a particularly rate-sensitive structural region and show how phase-resolved characterization can guide voltage-window selection for layered potassium-storage electrodes.
n3e0506e90068: Next-generation nanoelectronics require device architectures that integrate high density, multifunctionality, and low power consumption. Antiambipolar transistors (AATs) are promising candidates for multivalued logic and intelligent sensing, yet conventional two-dimensional (2D) AATs suffer from low peak-to-valley current ratios (PVRs) and unidirectional self-driven photoresponse. Here, we report a multifunctional AAT based on a MoS2/Ta2NiS5/MoTe2 double van der Waals heterostructure (vdWH). The device exhibits outstanding antiambipolar transport characteristics, achieving an ultrahigh PVR of 1 × 107 and a peak current of 1.2 μA, surpassing those of most previously reported 2D AATs. By introducing Ta2NiS5 as an intermediate layer, a back-to-back type-I band alignment is established, enabling efficient modulation and reversal of interfacial band bending under different bias conditions. Simultaneously, under 635 nm illumination, the device exhibits a gate-tunable bidirectional photocurrent response, with responsivities of +2.94 and −0.65 A/W at Vgs = +40 and −40 V, respectively. Furthermore, the device is demonstrated in ternary logic inverters, in-sensor image convolution processing, and multimodal information encoding. These results demonstrate the potential of van der Waals heterostructure-based antiambipolar transistors for integrated and reconfigurable optoelectronic systems.
n1aa84545f0a4: Dentin hypersensitivity (DH) is a widespread dental disease characterized by transient and sharp pain affecting routine oral activities, with a reported prevalence that can exceed 70%. While remineralization offers a promising therapeutic strategy to address the anatomical basis of exposed dentinal tubules, achieving long-term efficacy remains challenging due to mechanical abrasion and cariogenic biofilms. Herein, strontium–phenolic network nanoparticles (Sr-EGCG NPs) are developed via a facile, one-pot aqueous process for DH treatment. Unlike conventional transition-metal-based metal-phenolic networks (MPNs), the assembly of Sr-based MPNs is found to be dependent on alkaline conditions, yielding a distinct biscoordinated structure. When applied to exposed dentin, Sr-EGCG NPs exhibit rapid and stable adhesion mediated by abundant galloyl groups, maintaining tubule occlusion ratios exceeding 91.8% after simulated oral challenges, especially surpassing commercial Duraphat in thermocycling (Duraphat: 2.0%), while simultaneously reducing live bacterial coverage by over 97.5% at day 3. Crucially, Sr-EGCG NPs enable bidirectional dentin repair: in situ remineralization (achieving complete mineralized occlusion by day 7 both in vitro and in vivo) and the induction of tertiary dentin formation via the CaSR-mediated MAPK signaling pathway. Overall, this work provides insights into the rational design of Sr-based MPNs and expands the framework for developing biomaterials targeting DH.
n67a6cee626db: Lithographic patterning, which employs the solubility switch of photoresists to convert optical signals into nanostructures on the substrate, constitutes the primary top-down approach for high-precision nanomanufacturing. However, the stochastic defects arising from inhomogeneous reaction sites in photoresists pose a formidable challenge to reconciling the precision of sub-10 nm lithography. In this study, we present a coordinating photoacid generator (cPAG)-driven lithography strategy that has achieved a performance breakthrough through precise spatial control of acid sites. The resulting zirconium-oxo cluster photoresists, operating via cPAG-triggered precoordination and cluster cross-linking, demonstrate a two-orders-of-magnitude decrease in UV exposure dose. Furthermore, electron beam lithography has been demonstrated to achieve a sub-10 nm line width, underscoring its suitability for high-resolution and high-sensitivity applications. This strategy is versatile across cPAGs with diverse structures and is also applicable to other metal oxide photoresist systems, including titanium-oxo and zinc-oxo clusters. This work introduces a cPAG design tailored for cluster-based photoresists and validates their ability to overcome the intrinsic trade-off in resolution, line edge roughness, and sensitivity, providing a framework for developing next-generation photoresists.
n94eb1b6c355f: Quantum dot (QD) supraparticle lasers are promising platforms for microscale light sources and photonic labeling, yet their optical properties are set during assembly. Here, we introduce QD colloidosomes, liquid-core/solid-shell supraparticles that combine whispering-gallery-mode (WGM) optical feedback with stimulus-triggered structural collapse. Intact QD colloidosomes exhibit narrow, cavity-defined emission consistent with WGM-assisted lasing from 4.2 mJ/cm2, with line widths of 2.2–3.7 nm, demonstrating light confinement without a solid core. We identify shell continuity as a critical determinant for WGM feedback and lasing by exploring a morphological continuum of suprastructures comprising solid supraparticles, colloidosomes, and microporous hollow shells. Intact colloidosomes support narrow cavity modes, whereas porous shells remain broadband even at high pump fluence. We show that colloidosomes can be driven to rupture and release payload through well-defined pathways, including meniscus-driven capillary failure, uniform heating, and localized near-infrared activation, thereby configuring their optical response from cavity-defined lasing to broadband emission. These results establish QD colloidosomes as stimuli-responsive microlasers that couple optical-state switching and triggered release within a single self-assembled platform.
n1f7aa94497c7: Engineering lymph node-targeted tolerogenic nanomaterials requires simultaneous antigen–drug coloading and efficient lymphatic transport. However, conventional biocompatible nanoparticles with static architectures often face a size-dependent trade-off: larger particles enable cargo coloading but drain inefficiently to lymph nodes, whereas smaller particles favor lymphatic transport but have limited cargo versatility. Here, a size-transformable, self-dissociating albumin nanocluster inverse vaccine is introduced to address this materials design trade-off. Citrullinated peptide antigens are conjugated to human serum albumin, and rapamycin (RAPA) is coloaded using ball-milling technology to generate 200–300 nm nanoclusters. After subcutaneous injection, the nanoclusters dissociate into sub-10 nm albumin-based units, enabling passive lymphatic transport and accumulation in draining lymph nodes while maintaining coordinated antigen–RAPA codelivery. In vitro mechanistic studies show that the nanoclusters induce a tolerogenic dendritic cell phenotype and promote antigen-specific immune regulation. In a collagen-induced arthritis mouse model, weekly administration attenuates synovial inflammation, humoral autoimmune responses, bone erosion, and cartilage degradation while expanding Foxp3+ regulatory T cells. These findings establish self-dissociation-mediated size transformation as a functional materials strategy for lymph node-targeted antigen-specific immune tolerance and tolerogenic nanomedicine.
nb5c24c07088f: Supramolecular self-assembly can produce a linear or a positive nonlinear CD versus enantiomeric excess (ee) relationship. Negative “racemate rules” behavior is rare. In this work, we report an unusual nonlinear CD-ee dependence in a coassembly system comprising chiral perylene diimide molecules and gold nanoparticles (AuNPs). In contrast to the linear majority-rules behavior observed for pure PDI molecules, the introduction of AuNPs induces a tendency toward heterochiral coaggregation, leading to a negative CD-ee correlation at low temperature (278 K) and a positive correlation at high temperature (318 K). Even both positive and negative CD-ee correlations can coexist and be tuned within a single self-assembling system. Combined molecular dynamics simulations and preassembly control experiments demonstrate that the nanoparticles reshape the chiral recognition pathway of PDI molecules through alkyl chain–chain van der Waals interactions, while the assembly temperature further modulates the majority-rules behavior. This work reveals a mechanism by which nanoparticles act as regulatory units in supramolecular chirality, offering a design strategy for programmable chiral materials.
nf77fe073646b: Great strides have been achieved in lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-mediated mRNA delivery. However, traditional LNPs can induce undesirable side effects such as inflammatory reactions. Oxidative stress damage arising from ionizable lipids within LNPs is regarded as a major underlying cause of these adverse effects. Herein, we propose incorporating endogenous vitamin E (VE) into the tail moiety of commercial ionizable lipids to improve biosafety. Proof-of-concept investigations using SM-102-derived W3 confirm that this endogenous antioxidant modification substantially mitigates the inflammatory toxicity of mRNA-loaded LNPs. Following intravenous administration, W3 LNPs markedly decrease the levels of multiple pro-inflammatory cytokines, demonstrating an improved safety profile compared to SM-102 LNPs. Further analysis reveals that W3 LNPs significantly reduce intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels, alleviate oxidative stress damage, thereby inhibiting the activation of key inflammatory pathways such as NF-κB. Of note, the optimized formulation, sW3 LNPs enable efficient mRNA delivery to the spleen, with stronger antitumor efficacy and higher safety than SM-102 LNPs. In summary, W3 lipid confers minimal inflammatory adverse effects while preserving excellent delivery capability, which indicates that the VE-engineered LNPs possess great potential to serve as powerful and multifunctional platforms for next-generation mRNA therapeutics.
nc274a3c3909c: Lithium (Li) metal batteries have emerged as one of the most promising candidates for next‐generation energy storage systems due to the potentially high energy density. Nevertheless, repeated interfacial breakdown causes a short lifespan and poor safety. Inspired by the role of plant root systems in anchoring soil, an oligomer‐anchored LiZn nanocrystal composite interphase is constructed on the Li metal anode via a simple spray‐coating strategy, simultaneously enhancing the electrochemical stability and thermal safety of Li metal batteries. The LiZn alloy in the composite interphase restructures the interface energy distribution and reduces the local current density, thereby facilitating uniform lateral Li deposition. The oligomer serves as a binder to glue LiZn particles together and preserve the structural integrity of the interphase. A Li||LiNi0.5Co0.2Mn0.3O2 coin cell with the composite interphase exhibits a lifespan of 700 cycles at 1 C with a high cathode loading of 3.06 mAh cm−2. The 1.38 Ah Li||LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 pouch cell achieves a capacity retention of 86% after 200 cycles. When the cycled pouch cells undergo forced thermal runaway, the composite interphase elevates the trigger temperature from 124°C to 191°C. This interphase design provides novel insights to enhance the service lifespan and thermal safety of high energy density batteries.
ne866c971ba96: Interfacial ion and water organization critically influence proton-coupled electrochemical reactions, yet their coupled regulation under high-rate CO2 electroreduction remains poorly understood. Here, we construct a mosaic-and-gap-confined poly(dimethylsiloxane)-modified Bi (Bi-PDMS) interface that reorganizes the catalyst–electrolyte solvation environment. Atomistic simulations indicate altered near-surface cation accessibility and a less persistent extended hydrogen-bond environment, while slow-growth proton-transfer calculations show a substantially larger energetic penalty for selected extended proton-delivery pathways than for local proton transfer to *OCHO. Operando spectroscopy and mass spectrometry measurements further reveal potential-dependent interfacial water restructuring, suppressed hydrogen evolution, and enhanced formate-related pathway response. Bi-PDMS-30 sustains ∼90% formate Faradaic efficiency (FE) at −0.2 A cm− 2 for ∼200 h with substantially reduced surface-deposit accumulation. Together, these results support differentiated interfacial proton delivery within a reorganized ion–water environment as a useful framework for selective and durable CO2-to-formate electrosynthesis.
n5fd394f9c8b3: Non‐radiative energy loss originating from triplet exciton generation and intrinsic energetic disorder severely restricts the efficiency breakthrough of organic solar cells (OSCs). To address this dual bottleneck, herein, two benzodiimide‐based solid additives with distinct photophysical properties, namely fluorescent HPmDI and room‐temperature phosphorescent (RTP) BrPmDI, are developed to simultaneously suppress triplet exciton dissipation and mitigate energetic disorder for high‐efficiency OSCs. Both additives construct favorable intermolecular interactions with the D18 donor and L8‐BO acceptor, optimizing active layer molecular packing, enhancing film crystallinity, and reducing Urbach energy to alleviate intrinsic energetic disorder. Benefiting from the unique long‐lived triplet exciton characteristics of organic RTP BrPmDI, an efficient Dexter energy transfer (DET) pathway is additionally enabled, which effectively inhibits non‐radiative decay channels, including intersystem crossing and charge recombination‐induced triplet exciton formation. Consequently, the optimized D18:L8‐BO‐based OSCs modified with BrPmDI achieve a champion power conversion efficiency of 20.52% with a low non‐radiative energy loss of 0.217 eV, far outperforming the pristine device (19.01% and 0.226 eV) and HPmDI‐modified device (19.70% and 0.219 eV). This work reveals the dual regulatory mechanism of organic RTP additives on triplet exciton dynamics and energetic disorder, providing a facile strategy for the design of high‐efficiency additive materials toward low‐energy‐loss and high‐performance OSCs.
naed4de931479: Perovskite photovoltaics offer a promising route to low‐cost, low‐carbon solar energy, but progress toward largescale deployment is limited by manufacturing scalability, stability, and dependence on scarce materials. We demonstrate fully roll‐to‐roll coated, large‐area back‐contact perovskite photovoltaic modules based on a microgroove architecture that removes the need for transparent conductors such as Indium Tin Oxide (ITO). Devices are continuously manufactured on flexible substrates using scalable embossing, vacuum deposition, solution printing, and encapsulation. Modules with active areas up to 48.2 cm2 achieve record power conversion efficiencies exceeding 12.5 % and are further scaled to panels larger than 1000 cm2. The first comprehensive stability study of fully roll‐to‐roll coated perovskite modules is presented, including ISOS‐compliant accelerated ageing and up to five months of outdoor operation. Nanoscale x‐ray fluorescence tomography identifies key degradation pathways within the microgroove architecture. In addition to scalable fabrication, the architecture enables intrinsic bifaciality, improved angular response, and linear shading tolerance, enhancing real‐world energy yield and supporting sustainable largescale deployment beyond conventional photovoltaics.
nd0b2394516c7: The intrinsic electronic structure of Ru-based catalysts exhibits strong adsorption of oxygen-containing intermediates, which runs counter to the adsorption requirements of the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR), limiting their ability to achieve high activity. In this study, we employed a spatial confinement-pyrolysis strategy to develop a chlorine-doped triatomic Ru catalyst (Ru3ClNC), whose active center consists of a Ru3ON6Cl unit stabilized by both Ru─Ru bonds and Ru─N/O/Cl coordination bonds. Ru3ClNC delivers a high alkaline half-wave potential (E 1/2) of 0.90 V and an acidic E 1/2 of 0.79 V; the assembled zinc-air battery demonstrates excellent performance in terms of energy density and durability. In situ experiments and theoretical calculations have demonstrated the superiority of Ru3ON6Cl as the electrocatalytic ORR active site. The non-planar coordination effects and electronic effects of the Cl atom, in synergy with the triatomic site, disrupt the high symmetry, trigger charge redistribution, and significantly optimize the localized electron density at the active site. Importantly, the rearranged electronic structure breaks the linear scaling relationship in the d-band, enabling the catalyst to simultaneously optimize the rate-determining step of Ru3NC and OH* desorption, thereby enhancing reaction kinetics. This provides a new design concept for Ru-based catalysts to overcome the thermodynamic limitations and thereby improve the ORR activity.
nccc3776d3695: Achieving higher efficiency in organic solar cells requires simultaneous control over energy-level alignment, acceptor aggregation, and active-layer crystallization. Herein, two guest acceptors, S-SMA and AS-SMA, were designed by stepwise replacing the fluorinated terminal group of L8-BO with a weaker electron-withdrawing 2-(3-ethyl-4-oxothiazolidin-2-ylidene)malononitrile (CN-Rh) unit. This terminal-group engineering upshifts the acceptor energy levels, enables cascade the lowest unoccupied molecular energy levels among D18, the guest acceptor, and L8-BO, and regulates blend morphology. In situ spectroscopic analysis reveals that both guest acceptors accelerate the liquid-to-solid transition during film formation and promote tighter molecular packing. Compared with symmetric S-SMA, asymmetric AS-SMA enables a more favorable morphology and device operation, as reflected by suitable domain sizes, suppressed trap-assisted recombination, and more balanced charge transport. Consequently, the ternary D18:L8-BO:AS-SMA device delivers the best overall photovoltaic performance, achieving a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 20.71% with an open-circuit voltage (V OC) of 0.930 V and a fill factor (FF) of 80.62%. These results demonstrate that asymmetric terminal-group engineering is an effective strategy for coordinating energy-level tuning, crystallization kinetics, and morphology optimization in high-performance ternary organic solar cells.
n38366de562d5: Defects in polycrystalline perovskite films induce carrier ion migration and recombination, restricting the efficiency and durability of inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs). Conventional additive strategies based on ammonium salts often provide insufficient defect passivation and poor long-term stability. Herein, (1H-benzo[d]imidazol-2-yl)methanamine hydrochloride (BMHCl) serves as a multifunctional molecule regulator to cooperatively regulate defect evolution and crystallization kinetics through dual-site molecular interactions in inverted PSCs. Benefiting from the coordinated interactions of the protonated amino group (─NH3 +) and electron-rich nitrogen atoms with defective [PbI6]4− octahedra, BMHCl effectively regulates crystallization kinetics, suppresses defect formation, and alleviates residual lattice strain. Consequently, the BMHCl-modified perovskite films exhibit enhanced crystallinity, enlarged grain sizes, optimized vertical orientation, and reduced trap density. These combined microstructural improvements facilitate charge carrier transport while suppressing non-radiative recombination. BMHCl also produces more favorable energy-level alignment and faster interfacial charge extraction. Consequently, the champion PSC achieves the conversion efficiency of 26.50% while demonstrating excellent operational and damp-heat stability, retaining 87.49% and 80.52% of its initial efficiency after 1000 h at 85°C and 800 h at 85°C, 85% relative humidity, respectively. This work demonstrates a practical molecular-interaction strategy for efficient and durable inverted PSCs based on multifunctional, dual-site passivation and crystallization regulation.
n8a1ae8896119: Intrinsic properties of sulfide solid‐state electrolytes (SEs) are crucial for achieving all‐solid‐state batteries (ASSBs) with high safety and high energy density, yet it is challenging to fabricate high‐performance sulfide SE films in a scalable approach. Furthermore, the inevitable side reactions between sulfide SE and lithium metal anodes exacerbate interfacial incompatibility, causing degradation in the cyclic stability. Here, a high‐performance sulfide SE (Li5.4PS4.4Cl0.8Br0.8) was selected as the base phase to compensate for the loss of electrochemical performance during the dry film‐forming process. It was then combined with Polytetrafluoroethylene binder to prepare a high‐ionic‐conductivity composite membrane (HICCM). To mitigate side reactions between HICCM and the anode, a LiF‐rich interfacial layer forms in situ on the lithium metal surface, and the assembled symmetric cell achieves a high critical current density of 1.3 mA cm−2 and stable cycling for 2000 h (0.2 mA cm−2). For electrochemical performance, HICCM exhibits fast ion transport kinetics and electrical insulation, allowing the ASSB configured as FeS2//HICCM//LiF‐Li to achieve an energy density of 416.5 Wh kg−1 at a high loading of 3.4 mAh cm−2. This work demonstrates that by combining HICCM with a stable interface design, ASSBs can achieve longevity and high cell‐level energy density.
naefb806b300d: Solar‐driven interfacial evaporation is an energy‐efficient desalination strategy. However, the existing solar‐driven interfacial evaporators mostly rely on a surface‐localized photothermal layer for heat confinement, which limits evaporation exclusively to the top surface. The internal transfer channels and potential evaporation area remain unexplored, restricting water production rates. Here, a wireless anodization with a composite bipolar electrode has been proposed to prepare completely internal anodized porous Ti with TiO2 nanotube (TNT) arrays, serving for 3D solar‐driven interfacial evaporation. By regulating the reaction area and intensity, the TiO2 nanotubes (TNTs) with tailored size (diameter of 120–170 nm, length of 3–10 µm) have successfully anisotropically grown on the porous Ti substrates, constructing internal interconnected channels. The obtained wireless anodized porous Ti (WAPT) possessed an increased surface area of 7.938 m2·g−1, as well as solar absorbance >80%, superhydrophilicity (totally wetting within 10 s), and low evaporation enthalpy (451.83 kJ·kg−1), making efficient water evaporation with larger evaporation area and lower energy consumption possible. Under one‐sun irradiation, the WAPT showed an evaporation rate of 1.68 kg·m−2·h−1 with no salt crystallization and could maintain over 30 days. By assembling the WAPTs into a 3D interfacial evaporator, cooperated with wind‐driven cold evaporation, the maximum evaporation rate reached 2.412 kg·m−2·h−1. In outdoor conditions (solar intensity of 0.6 kW·m−2 at 12 pm), the water collection rate reached 1.59 kg·m−2·h−1. This work should make possible the development of a high‐performance solar‐driven interfacial evaporator for various applications.
n20c691d35fb7: Li metal anodes, sought after for next‐generation high‐energy batteries, are severely hindered by dendritic growth and an unstable solid electrolyte interphase (SEI). Here, we design a fluorinated 3D artificial SEI with a built‐in vertical Si‐gradient lithiophilicity (3D F‐SiG SEI) via in situ copolymerization of hexafluorobutyl methacrylate and 2,4,6,8‐tetramethyl‐2,4,6,8‐tetraethynylcyclotetrasiloxane. Critically, this crosslinking reaction proceeds exclusively under the catalytic action of the Li metal substrate, ensuring seamless interfacial integration. The resulting porous SEI generates a continuous lithiophilicity gradient that homogenizes Li+ flux, enforces “bottom‐up” pore‐filling deposition, and buffers volume fluctuations. Simultaneously, the F/Si‐rich chemistry promotes in situ formation of a stable LiF‐enriched Si‐based SEI, which reduces the nucleation overpotential and accelerates interfacial kinetics. The modified anode delivers an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.4% in half cells and ultralong cycling stability over 3500 h in symmetric cells. Full cells paired with LiFePO4 and high‐nickel NCM cathodes exhibit superior capacity retention and rate capability even under high mass loading. This work provides a blueprint for simultaneously engineering interfacial deposition, buffering volume fluctuations, and enhancing air stability in practical Li metal anodes.
n0ebc7f20429c: Cobalt-free Li-rich layered oxides (LRMs) hold great promise for next-generation high-energy batteries, yet their practical deployment is severely hindered by irreversible oxygen redox and progressive interfacial degradation. Here, a full-range Li stoichiometry screening across Li1+0.65 x Ni0.35Mn0.65O2+0.65 x (0 ≤ x ≤ 1) was conducted to decouple bulk superlattice evolution from surface chemistry. A structural crossover at x ≈ 0.5 with minimized Li2MnO3 long-range ordering is identified, yet optimal electrochemistry unexpectedly emerges at x = 0.375, governed by a triple synergistic mechanism: finely dispersed Li2MnO3 nanodomains, moderate Li+/Ni2+ antisite pillars, and—most critically— an in situ coherent spinel passivation interphase spontaneously formed during calcination. The optimized LRM0.375 delivers 227.1 mAh g−1 at 0.1C, 161.8 mAh g−1 at 5C, and an ultralow voltage fade of only 1.33 mV cycle−1, with its graphite full cell retaining 78.48% capacity after 500 cycles. Operando XRD, RIXS, and DEMS collectively demonstrate that the spinel surface barrier, rather than bulk superlattice ordering alone, governs anionic redox reversibility and cycling durability. This work challenges the superlattice-centered design paradigm and identifies interfacial spinel passivation as a key stability-governing factor within a triple synergistic mechanism, providing targeted stoichiometric guidelines for designing durable anionic-redox cathodes beyond conventional bulk-structure-focused strategies.
nae8b23e3be8f: Crystalline silicon solar cells are approaching their theoretical Auger efficiency limit, necessitating tandem architectures that transcend the Shockley–Queisser constraint and lower the cost of electricity. Monolithic perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells (PSTSCs) have breached the 35% power conversion efficiency barrier, emerging as the leading candidate to disrupt the photovoltaic landscape. However, translating this laboratory success to terawatt‐scale deployment requires precise control over charge transport and interfacial recombination at the interconnecting layer (ICL). This review examines the material innovations driving this evolution, grounded in a quantitative loss‐budget analysis, with a focus on the ICL and full‐dimensional interface engineering. We first examine the evolving ICL paradigm, from defect‐mediated transport in amorphous silicon to efficient band‐to‐band tunneling in polycrystalline silicon junctions, and the enhanced charge extraction enabled by transparent conductive oxides with self‐assembled monolayers (SAMs), whose Ohmic contact formation we trace through an anchoring‐to‐Fermi‐level‐depinning mechanism. We further dissect breakthroughs mitigating non‐radiative losses on textured silicon substrates, where SAMs and passivation strategies overcome steric hindrance and contact resistance, and where the same pyramid texture governs wide‐bandgap perovskite crystallization and its process‐engineering trade‐offs. Finally, we navigate the “efficiency‐stability‐cost” trilemma, addressing halide‐segregation and ion‐migration suppression under a standardized stability framework, alongside scalable manufacturing toward industrial translation.
ndd516c903dbf: Ti3C2Tx MXene is a promising 2D nanofiller for gas barrier composites. However, controlling the composite's nanoscale structure and ensuring its stability in harsh thermal environments remain significant challenges. This study compares the multilayer properties, morphology, and hydrogen (H2) gas barrier performance of two different MXene‐based layer‐by‐layer (LbL) assemblies, demonstrating the influence of polymer content and complementary positively charged assembling species. LbL assembly effectively promotes brick‐and‐mortar‐like multilayer ordering of MXene in nanoscale thin films, but the method requires positively charged species to electrostatically assemble with negatively charged MXene. Using either reduced graphene oxide (rGO) precomplexed with a polycation (rGO‐PDDA) or positively charged MXene (f‐MXene) functionalized with [3‐(2‐aminoethylamino)‐propyl] trimethoxysilane (AEAPTMS) as the complementary species, the two MXene‐based multilayers show strikingly different behaviors at elevated temperatures. Structural and chemical characterization shows that only the rGO‐PDDA/MXene multilayer maintains electrostatic bonding, leading to improved stability and performance in harsh conditions. In films as thin as 43 nm, the LbL multilayers retain their performance. The rGO‐PDDA/MXene multilayer exhibits low H2 gas permeability (7.13 ± 0.09 × 10−11 m3·m·m−2·atm−1·day−1) even at 400°C. This study offers insightful guidelines for the rational design of MXene‐ or polymer‐based composite films for gas barrier applications in extreme temperatures.
n51e366485701: Sodium‐ion batteries have attracted extensive attention for large‑scale energy storage owing to the abundance and low cost of sodium resources. However, the near‑coplanar structure geometry of polyanionic‐type cathodes causes in‑plane stress and electrostatic barriers, which lead to blocked Na+ transport kinetics and hinder their practical application. Herein, an α‑plane, defined by the transition metal and its coordinating dangling anions, is identified as the critical structural bottleneck for Na+ diffusion. By screening and tuning the dangling anions, a coordination geometry reconstruction is achieved that twists the α‑plane into α1‐ and α2‐planes. This twisting behavior breaks α‑plane restriction and relieves the in‑plane stress, thereby lowering the Na+ migration barrier. Concurrently, the geometry reconstruction enlarges the Na2‑centered polyhedral volume and increases the Na2 site occupancy from 0.56 to 0.62. Thus, the modified cathode delivers a high reversible capacity of 130 mAh g−1 and outstanding rate capability, with 80% retention at 30 C and 83 mAh g−1 at 50 C. It also exhibits excellent wide‐temperature operability (−40°C to 55°C) and stable full‑cell performance. The universality of this strategy is validated on several polyanionic cathodes. This work reveals the α‑plane as a tunable structural parameter, offering a geometry‑electronic synergy paradigm for high‑power polyanionic‐type cathodes.
n469801823aec: Protein nanofibrils assemble hierarchically, yet directing the mesoscale topology that connects fibrillar growth to network mechanics remains challenging. Here, we show that crystalline seed identity redirects regenerated silk fibroin assembly while retaining a common silk II packing motif. Top‐down silk nanocrystals promote core‐arm units with dense cores and radiating fibrillar arms, whereas seed‐free assembly and length‐matched bottom‐up nanofibril seeds yield predominantly linear structures. Cryogenic transmission electron microscopy and spectroscopy reveal preorganized, β‐sheet‐rich fibrillar bundles within the seeds. Time‐resolved imaging supports a mechanism in which these scaffolds accommodate multiple local growth regions, followed mainly by arm elongation. Composition‐dependent morphologies are consistent with precursor allocation among these regions, linking seed abundance to arm length and assembly‐unit density. At matched solids content, core‐arm gels enter the flow regime at lower strains than linear gels while retaining substantial modulus recovery after repeated high‐strain deformation. Idealized network simulations suggest that multivalent cores preserve global connectivity while shorter reconstruction pathways facilitate reversible bridge exchange. These findings establish crystalline seed interfaces as topology‐selecting elements in protein assembly and provide a strategy for constructing thixotropic and injectable protein materials without additional chemical cross‐linking.
n3ac46f96eb5d: Liquid crystal elastomers (LCEs) combine liquid crystal orientational order with the elasticity of polymer networks and respond to thermal, optical, electrical, chemical, and mechanical stimuli. These responses can change not only the shape of an LCE but also its surface morphology and properties. The resulting surface changes can regulate wetting, adhesion, friction, biological contact, and interactions with light, electromagnetic waves, and sound. This review summarizes recent progress in molecular and network design, alignment programming, surface fabrication, and functional layer integration for LCE surfaces and LCE‐driven composite interfaces. The resulting functions are organized into fluid, mechanical, and wave interactions. Guided by the central idea that bulk responses generate deformation while surface states determine interfacial behavior, this review discusses functions controlled by LCE surfaces and examines the conversion of bulk deformation into changes in surface shape and properties. These dynamic surface states enable liquid manipulation, adhesion and friction control, biological and haptic interfaces, optical readout, and wave modulation. Finally, the review discusses challenges and future directions in reliable switching, scalable fabrication, and feedback control. By linking bulk responses to changes in surface and interfacial states, it provides a framework for understanding and designing functional LCE surfaces and LCE‐driven composite interfaces.
n785399bba164: Mechanical programming provides a simple way to tune embedded nonlinear resonators without redesigning the host structure. Here, seven magneto‐elastic piezoelectric resonators are integrated into elastically reconstructed openings of a host beam. The removed stiffness, mass, and inertia are restored. The dynamics of the intact beam are therefore recovered over the investigated frequency range. Programming is performed by changing only the spacing between repulsive magnets. Each resonator can be set independently. This creates uniform, nonuniform, and graded combinations of monostable and bistable states. Experiments and simulations show marked changes in both vibration attenuation and harvested power. Different programs favor different functions. One configuration reaches 1.82 times the reference attenuation bandwidth. Another reaches 1.57 times the reference harvesting performance. Assuming nine admissible states per resonator, the seven‐resonator system spans 97$9^7$ possible configurations. Model‐selected candidates improve both numerical references simultaneously, reaching 1.16 times the attenuation bandwidth and 1.11 times the harvesting metric. The prototype also delivers up to 10.67 μW$\umu{\rm W}$ of total AC load power near resonance. The result is a structurally integrated platform with programmable nonlinear functionality and largely preserved host dynamics.
n2aa639e3ef05: Luminescent sensing relies on the generation, migration, and dissipation of excited‐state energy modulated by analytes. However, the contribution of intraframework energy transfer processes to sensing performance remains insufficiently studied. Owing to the highly tunable structures and designable energy transfer pathways, metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) provide an ideal platform for dissecting detailed processes. Herein, a series of isostructural lanthanide MOFs were constructed from 2,5‐furandicarboxylic / 3,5‐pyridinedicarboxylic acid, enabling independent regulation of metal‐to‐metal and linker‐to‐linker energy transfer. Direct comparison of chemically integrated frameworks and their physical mixtures using bisphenol pollutants as probes reveals that metal‐to‐metal energy transfer dominates sensing performance, while linker‐to‐linker energy transfer contributes marginally. Mechanistic analyses indicate the impacts originate from the different energetic characteristics. Rigid lanthanide energy levels in Eu‐Tb systems create an “energy reservoir” that strongly regulate luminescence responses, whereas highly environment‐sensitive linker states in mixed‐linker systems give rise to self‐compensating energy transfer, resulting in a diminished influence. Moreover, the additional energy transfer pathways introduced by chemical integration can partially compensate for analyte‐induced excited‐state energy loss by releasing the “accumulated energy”, thereby mitigating the overall quenching effect. This work establishes a fundamental relationship between intraframework energy transfer and luminescence recognition performance, providing a general design pattern for sensing materials.
na577ba6418e6: Accurate quantification of glutathione (GSH), a key regulator of intracellular redox homeostasis, and its correlation with the early therapeutic response to cuproptosis‐based treatment in animal models are crucial for developing effective glutathione‐depletion therapeutics, yet in vivo GSH quantification remains challenging. Here, we developed a GSH‐responsive Cu nanoplatform (Cu‐CDs) for early and noninvasive assessment of cuproptosis by exploiting the thiol chemical exchange saturation transfer (CEST) magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) signal of glutathione. In vivo studies in 4T1 tumor‐bearing mice demonstrated that thiol CEST MRI enabled quantitative detection of GSH as low as 0.39 µmol/g in tumors (R2 = 0.944). Notably, no correlation was observed between the levels of GSH and the MRI signals (R2 = 0.302 or 0.117) from the exogenous analog, indicating that assessments using exogenous probes at a single time point were inaccurate. Remarkably, dynamic changes in the thiol CEST signals within only 8 h after administration of the Cu‐CDs strongly correlated with the tumor inhibition rate measured (R2 = 0.993), enabling early prediction of the long‐term cuproptosis therapeutic efficacy. Thus, CEST MRI provides a non‐invasive and quantitative approach for monitoring GSH in vivo, with potential for assessing therapeutic agent accumulation and predicting early therapeutic response of GSH‐related therapies.
n7b5a0a7b8944: Solid‐state lithium metal batteries suffer from poor interfacial stability and dendrite growth, primarily limited by the ion transport kinetics and mechanical properties of composite solid electrolytes (CSE). Inspired by the hierarchical grape cluster, we design a biomimetic electrolyte via electrospinning PAN fiber “pedicel” integrated with mesoporous SiO2‐SO3Li “grape berry” fillers, followed by in‐situ polymerization. This structure establishes long‐range Li+ conduction channels and a robust physical barrier, delivering a high Li+ transference number of 0.65, ionic conductivity of 1.44 × 10−3 S cm−1 at 25°C, and a modulus of 520 MPa. Benefiting from these advantages, the assembled LFP|Li and NCM811|Li cells achieve 88.8% capacity retention after 1000 cycles and 94.3% after 300 cycles, respectively. Moreover, a high‐loading pouch cell realizes an energy density of 414.9 Wh kg−1/797.8 Wh L−1 and withstands harsh abuse tests. Mechanistically, DFT and phase‐field simulations reveal the dual Li+ pathways and TFSI− immobilization enabled by the ‐SO3Li groups. Notably, a physics‐informed neural network (PINN) framework decouples interface activation‐aging kinetics and predicts long‐term impedance evolution. This work provides a biomimetic paradigm and data‐driven methods for the design and interface analysis of high‐performance CSE.
n864c29937140: All-solid-state lithium-sulfur batteries (ASSLSBs) are promising for safe, high-energy storage, but their development is limited by lithium polysulfides (LiPSs) dissolution and shuttle effect in poly(ethylene oxide)-based solid polymer electrolytes, leading to sluggish sulfur conversion and rapid capacity decay. Herein, we report a dual-phase high-entropy sulfide system (HES, FeCoNiCuMoSx) nanoflowers as a multifunctional sulfur host. Owing to lattice distortion and strong d-p orbital coupling, HES exhibits strong chemical affinity toward LiPSs and accelerates sulfur conversion. Importantly, the dual-phase HES enables a dual-pathway sulfur reduction reaction, in which a restrained LiPSs-mediated “liquid”-phase route sustains kinetics, while a dominant “solid-solid” (S to Li2S) pathway fundamentally blocks LiPSs dissolution and shuttling. As a result, the S@HES cathode delivers a high specific capacity of 1319.3 mAh g−1 at 0.1 C and maintains remarkable cycling stability with a low capacity decay rate of only 0.0458% per cycle over 1000 cycles at 1 C, along with stable electrochemical performance over the investigated temperature range of 40°C to 60°C. Furthermore, S@HES-based pouch cells exhibit excellent mechanical flexibility and deliver a high initial capacity of 1365.8 mAh g− 1 with stable cycling performance, collectively underscoring the strong potential of this dual-pathway regulation strategy for practical advanced ASSLSBs.
n0c4976133d79: Developing soft and conformable materials with enhanced charge generation and retention capabilities remains a critical barrier for next‐generation flexible triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs). Here, we report a polarization‐coupled tribo‐negative film fabricated by integrating a room‐temperature ferroelectric nematic liquid crystal (FNLC) material (FNLC‐1571) into an electrospun poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) mat. In contrast to traditional rigid fillers, the optimally engineered ferroelectric nematic phase (NF) of FNLC‐1571 microdomains assists spontaneous soft polar ordering in the nanofibrous PVDF matrix. This facilitates the integration of dipolar interactions with the fluorinated ends of PVDF, thereby synergistically promoting the crystallization of the electroactive β‐phase, enhancing dielectric behavior, modulating surface potential, improving interfacial charge‐trapping ability, and increasing contact area for superior charge generation while maintaining mechanical flexibility. When paired with a polyethylenimine (PEI)‐coated polyamide‐6 (PA‐6) tribo‐positive counter layer, the optimized 1 wt.% FNLC/PVDF‐based TENG delivers stable electrical output under low‐amplitude mechanical periodic contact‐separation excitation (8N, 10 Hz), with a peak‐to‐peak open‐circuit voltage of ∼395 V, a short‐circuit current of ∼40 µA, and a transferred charge of ∼167 nC. Finally, the optimally engineered all‐organic TENG assemblies were employed for various practical applications by demonstrating efficient capacitor charging, LED illumination, accurate biomechanical‐motion sensing, and real‐time IoT‐enabled monitoring through wireless interfacing.
ndee9385244db: Metal‐organic frameworks (MOFs) are widely deployed in catalysis, separation and chemical sensing, yet luminescent MOFs, especially those emitting near‐infrared (NIR) circularly polarized luminescence (CPL), remain largely underexplored. Here, we address this critical gap through a hierarchical dual‐sphere engineering strategy to fabricate luminescent Eu‐Yb‐BTC MOFs, wherein L‐phenylalanine serves as a second‐sphere modulator to construct low‐symmetry chiral microenvironments surrounding lanthanide centers. Subsequent hybridization with Yb‐doped perovskite quantum dots synergistically enhances both quantum‐cutting efficiency and CPL performance, yielding a 170% enhancement in the 980 nm Yb3+ emission, an absolute photoluminescence quantum yield of 154%, and a luminescence dissymmetry factor of ‐1.58 × 10−2. Leveraging its single‐source RED‐NIR dual‐band CPL output, whose inherent polarization selectivity suppresses stray light and ambient background noise to enable more accurate blood oxygen monitoring, we demonstrate a portable blood oxygen sensor with 15 s response and <1.5% measurement error, and further develop an AI‐assisted emotion recognition framework based on dual‐channel photoplethysmography signals. This work establishes a versatile design paradigm for high‐performance chiral luminescent MOFs, opening new avenues for next‐generation wearable biomedical diagnostics and edge‐AI‐enabled healthcare.
nb5e967473731: Freshwater scarcity and intermittent solar irradiation motivate the development of technologies for freshwater production and electricity generation. However, salt accumulation limits the long‐term operation of solar interfacial evaporators. A laser‐architected delignified balsa wood evaporator (DBW/LCC) with a 3D cylindrical array and laser‐carbonized surfaces is fabricated through delignification, laser engraving, and in situ laser carbonization. The array enhances light trapping and exposes additional sidewall area. Vertically aligned hydrophilic channels sustain capillary water supply and, together with the hydrophobic top surface, establish asymmetric wettability. DBW/LCC achieves an average absorptance of 99.46% over 250–2500 nm. The wetted surface exhibits a valley–plateau temperature difference of ∼1.2°C. Thermo–solutal Marangoni circulation may contribute to brine redistribution. The evaporator maintains stable evaporation for 150 h in 20 wt.% brine without visible salt deposition. Under 1 sun, it achieves a mass‐loss rate of 5.09 kg m−2 h−1 normalized to its horizontal projected area, with an apparent evaporation efficiency of 99.85% calculated using an effective enthalpy. Coupled with a thermoelectric module, it generates voltages of 86.3 mV under 1 sun and 79.8 mV at a wind speed of 9.6 m s−1 without illumination. This platform offers a route to decentralized water–electricity cogeneration.
n3590c773ffce: Efficient microwave absorption in the S–C band requires the strength and frequency distribution of resonance‐related magnetic loss to be regulated while sufficient permeability is retained. The key is therefore to balance control of the resonance‐related dynamic magnetic response with preservation of the magnetic contribution from the ferromagnetic matrix. Here, FeCoNiCr0.4Mn0.6 high‐entropy alloy (HEA) powders were subjected to wet milling and low‐temperature annealing to produce anisotropic flakes while enabling controlled in situ oxidation of the intrinsic Mn. The resulting MnO/HEA interfaces were accompanied by changes in the local strain state and magnetic anisotropy environment of the adjacent ferromagnetic matrix, providing a structural basis for the evolution of resonance linewidth and effective damping. At 300°C, limited MnO formation produced a moderate effective damping state while maintaining relatively high permeability and sufficient ferromagnetic‐phase contribution, enabling effective absorption over 3.2–4.9 GHz at a thickness of 3.5 mm. At 400°C, further MnO formation increased the fraction of the non‐ferromagnetic phase and weakened the microwave magnetic response. These results demonstrate that controlling the oxidation degree of intrinsic alloying elements can balance interfacial regulation, dynamic magnetic relaxation, and ferromagnetic‐phase retention, providing a feasible strategy for low‐frequency microwave absorption in corrosion‐resistant HEAs.
n130c3cea288d: Controlling the condensed‐state properties of π‐conjugated macrocycles via molecular structure remains a fundamental challenge in supramolecular chemistry. Here, we report benzophosphole‐embedded nanohoops as a heteroatom‐doped platform where spatial configuration (exo vs. endo) directly governs molecular conformation, self‐assembly, and electronic function. The endo‐nanohoop adopts a unique outward‐facing conformer that assembles into discrete tetrameric cage‐like assemblies stabilized by cooperative P═O···H2O interactions, which further evolve into hierarchical hollow nanobowl architectures exhibiting aggregation‐induced emission enhancement (AIEE). This differentiation generates distinct hydration microenvironments that correlate with divergent memristive behaviors. The exo‐analogues exhibit highly uniform volatile threshold switching arising from transient ion migration dynamics, enabling physical reservoir computing. In contrast, the endo‐framework possesses a distinct hydration microenvironment and exhibits robust analog non‐volatile memory behavior. Available evidence suggests a possible mechanism in which water acts as structural nodes that bridge Ag clusters and coordinate ion transport with filament stability, thereby enabling non‐volatile memristive behavior. Leveraging the humidity‐dependent switching characteristics of the exo system, we further demonstrate a humidity‑sensitive resistive switching capable of real‐time and noise‐resistant respiratory monitoring. These findings establish a direct correlation between molecular structure, water confinement, and adaptive electronic functionality, providing a supramolecular strategy for designing intelligent organic memristive materials and sensing‐memory integrated hardware.
n24b98e45de60: Hepatocellular csarcinoma (HCC) progression is driven by dynamic interactions between cancer cells and stromal fibroblasts that evolve with spatial proximity and physical association. However, conventional co‐culture models either combine these populations from the outset or maintain them in permanent separation, limiting compartment‐specific analysis of their progressive interaction. Here, we develop a distance‐programmed tumor–stromal assembloid platform in which tumor and stromal microtissues are bioprinted at defined surface‐to‐surface separations. We engineer a collagen–alginate hybrid bioink that restrains spreading, promotes cell–cell cohesion, and preserves discrete tumor and stromal compartments throughout assembly, while interface angle and neck length quantify structural integration, which TGF‐β1 accelerates. Compartment‐specific tracking resolves a graded E‐cadherin‐to‐N‐cadherin transition within the tumor compartment together with progressive activation and spatial expansion of the stromal compartment. Paracrine signaling, fibroblast activation, matrix remodeling, and drug‐resistance programs predominate at distinct phases, producing phase‐dependent responses to pathway‐specific inhibition combined with doxorubicin. Modular repetition of these units extends assembly across a large spatial field, yielding an interconnected centimeter‐scale array with high viability. This platform couples compartment‐resolved analysis of tumor–stromal remodeling with a scalable route to macroscale tumor tissues.
n0d1d70614f79: Organic low-dimensional heterostructures (OLDHs) possess remarkable optoelectronic properties, positioning them as candidates for next-generation optoelectronic integrated systems. While epitaxial self-assembly enables efficient preparation, ensuring precise orientation during heteroepitaxial growth remains a fundamental challenge. Herein, a staged orientation controlled epitaxial growth strategy is developed to obtain OLDHs composed of two 4H-Cyclopenta[2,1-b:3,4-b']dithiophene (CDT)-based cocrystals. Importantly, each epitaxy stage is governed by in-plane molecular spacing matching relationships between multiple crystal-plane combinations, which allows for the controllable relative position and continuously adjustable epitaxy-length of axial/lateral OLDHs by regulating the material ratio (R = n CB/n CQ) of the heterogenous components. The fabricated OLDHs exhibit promising functionalities as optical filters and multi-channel optical routing by exploiting energy transfer and photon propagation within the heterostructures. This strategy provides a crucial pathway for controllable epitaxial self-assembly, thereby shedding light on the synthesis methodology of OLDHs.
nca2233f3d73e: Stretchable millimeter‐wave (mmWave) electronics are essential for next‐generation wearable wireless systems. However, intrinsically stretchable mmWave devices remain challenging because it is difficult to fabricate metallic structures that simultaneously combine high conductivity, mechanical stretchability, high‐resolution patterning, and skin biocompatibility for epidermal wireless operation. To bridge this gap, we report a mmWave nanomesh with low sheet resistance of 0.24 Ω/sq and µm‐level patterning precision, and broad‐spectrum antibacterial activity for hygienic epidermal deployment. The proposed nanomesh is compatible with the fabrication of mmWave antennas operating above 20 GHz and supports efficient mmWave radiation. Meanwhile, the nanomesh exhibits mechanical robustness and electrical stability even after 1000 cycles of mechanical deformations. On this basis, we realized a stretchable dual‐unit nanomesh antenna array with a high realized gain of 6.8 dBi at 24 GHz, and demonstrated the first robust mmWave wireless data transmission based on nanomesh electronics. Beyond electromagnetic performance, the nanomesh antenna exhibits long‐lasting and broad‐spectrum antibacterial effects, ensuring hygiene and safety by avoiding epidermal bacterial accumulation. Combining high electromagnetic performance, mechanical‐electrical stability, and antimicrobial ability, the proposed nanomaterial and mmWave device provide a practical strategy for wearable mmWave wireless electronics.
n0fbd0a7a9f46: Self‐assembled monolayers (SAMs) have been extensively studied in perovskite solar cells (PSCs). Nevertheless, the aggregation tendency of SAM molecules results in non‐uniform deposition and inadequate substrate coverage, thereby severely impeding device performance. Herein, we introduce a multifunctional additive, nonafluorobutane‐1‐sulfonic acid (PFBS), to actively regulate the growth of SAM layers. Our investigations reveal that PFBS suppresses the self‐aggregation of SAM molecules through hydrogen bonding and steric disruption, thus promoting their dispersion in the solution and facilitating the exposure of anchoring groups. The PFBS‐modified SAM exhibits improved coverage, robustness, and interfacial energy‐level alignment. Furthermore, PFBS effectively passivates interfacial defects, reduces non‐radiative recombination, and promotes the growth of high‐quality perovskite film. Consequently, the PFBS‐optimized PSC with a 1.68 eV bandgap delivers a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 24% and significantly enhanced stability. This work presents an additive‐induced ordering strategy, providing a scalable route for high‐performance PSCs and tandem photovoltaics.
n1d38f53c847c: Having long lifetimes and intrinsic electric dipole moments, interlayer excitons in van der Waals heterostructures are promising quasiparticles for excitonic optoelectronics. However, their practical implementation has been largely hindered by the fact that most interlayer excitons suffer from strongly suppressed radiative recombination and are stable only under cryogenic conditions. Here, we identify a distinct class of interlayer excitons that are simultaneously optically active and robust at room temperature in an atypical van der Waals heterostructure formed by a two‐dimensional layered perovskite (PEA)2PbBr4 and monolayer MoS2. These interlayer excitons appear as a distinct photoluminescence feature and exhibit a polarization‐anisotropic response in a tilted sample geometry, consistent with an out‐of‐plane component of the optical transition dipole moment. Remarkably, the interlayer exciton emission persists up to 400 K, indicating exceptional thermal robustness. Time‐resolved measurements reveal a moderate lifetime enhancement compared to intralayer excitons, indicating a hybrid state that balances partial spatial charge separation with retained electron‐hole wavefunction overlap. First‐principles calculations support a type‐II electronic structure with spatially displaced band‐edge states, finite interfacial coupling, and charge redistribution across the interface. Our findings establish (PEA)2PbBr4/MoS2 as a promising platform for optically active interlayer excitons under ambient and elevated‐temperature conditions.
n9b63fddfff11: Halide perovskites are promising memristive materials for neuromorphic computing, yet their practical deployment in hardware is severely hindered by instability against moisture, oxygen, and reactive metallic ions. Here, we develop an ultra‐robust perovskite memristor with all‐weather adaptability protected by a ∼100 nm conformal polymeric nanoscale coating. Deposited by low‐temperature, solvent‐free chemical vapor deposition (CVD) technique, the polymeric Parylene serves as an encapsulation, interfacial passivation, and homogeneous dielectric layer. The memristor exhibits excellent bipolar resistive switching under ambient conditions with high uniformity, an endurance of 1.5 × 104 cycles (over 12.5‐fold improvement), and a low set voltage of ∼0.27 V. It maintains stable operation under 100% relative humidity, thermal treatment at 348 K, 6‐month ambient storage, and 300 bending cycles at 90°, and even passes the stringent IPX7 waterproof standard. A hardware‐mapped convolutional neural network leveraging the synaptic properties of these memristors achieves a highly reliable MNIST recognition accuracy of 90%±0.4% across 10 independent test cycles. This work demonstrates that conformal Parylene encapsulation offers a comprehensive solution to the perovskite instability, paving the way for flexible and low‐power neuromorphic systems.
n3026dd9b202c: The primary pathological hallmarks of Parkinson's disease (PD) comprise the loss of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra and abnormal accumulation of α‐synuclein, accompanied by severe oxidative damage due to excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS). Clinical electrical stimulation therapies pose invasive risks from long‐term electrode implantation with neuroinflammation side effects, while antioxidant drugs for scavenging brain ROS also fail to meet clinical demands due to poor blood–brain barrier permeability and short half‐lives. Herein, we report a brain‐targeted piezoelectric nanogenerator (PEL) for wireless electrotherapy for PD. Under ultrasonic stimulation, the piezoelectrically induced output current generated by the PEL promotes voltage‐gated calcium channel‐mediated calcium influx, upregulating tyrosine hydroxylase expression to promote dopamine synthesis. Concurrently, acting as a piezoelectric catalyst, the PEL rapidly decomposes water to continuously release hydrogen, which scavenges excess ROS and mitigates oxidative damage. In the mouse model of PD, the ultrasound‐responsive PEL nanogenerator alleviated the symptoms of the disease without causing obvious toxicity. This synergistic approach targeting ion channels and hydrogen therapy may inspire the development of other minimally invasive therapeutic strategies for PD.
n0fe64f0aa9e4: Birefringent crystals are vital functional materials for light‐polarization modulation, widely utilized in optical communications, laser technology, displays, imaging, and photodetection. High‐performance birefringent crystals require broad optical band gaps to realize wide visible‐to‐ultraviolet transparency. However, large birefringence and wide band gap are difficult to achieve simultaneously, since highly polarizable structural units easily induce low‐energy electronic transitions. Herein, an amino‐position regulation strategy is proposed via proton‐transfer‐driven self‐assembly of 2‐, 3‐, and 4‐aminopyridines with 4, 5‐dicyanoimidazole, integrating prominent polarizability anisotropy and large molecular HOMO–LUMO gaps. Three organic crystals, [(C5N2H7)+(C5N4H)−]·H2O (2AP‐DCI‐W), [(C5N2H7)+(C5N4H2)(C5N4H)−] [3AP‐(DCI)2], and [(C5N2H7)+(C5N4H)−] (4AP‐DCI), were successfully synthesized. Amino‐substitution position modulates the electrostatic distribution, intermolecular interactions, and packing modes of π‐conjugated units, progressively improving both birefringence and optical band gap. 4AP‐DCI exhibits the optimal overall performance with a calculated birefringence of 0.514 at 546 nm and a broad band gap of 4.06 eV. To our knowledge, this value represents the highest birefringence among all organic birefringent crystals with band gaps over 4.0 eV. This work provides an effective molecular strategy to balance large birefringence and broad transparency by tuning the position and spatial arrangement of organic π‐conjugated functional units.
n70d4b7f00aaa: Efficient two-photon-excited fluorescence (TPEF) in crystalline frameworks requires compact, ordered chromophore organization while suppressing nonradiative decay from uncontrolled aggregation. Herein, tetranuclear organotin clusters were used to regulate the spatial arrangement and intramolecular rotation of tetraphenylethylene (TPE) chromophores. Two organotin coordination networks, OCN-1 and OCN-2, were synthesized from TPE-based carboxylate ligands and tetranuclear organotin clusters. OCN-1 adopts a 3D entangled architecture of interwoven 2D (4, 4)-grid layers, whereas OCN-2 comprises densely staggered 1D coordination chains. In both structures, coordination anchoring and short-range contacts involving adjacent phenyl groups and tin-bound alkyl substituents restrict aromatic rotation. Consequently, OCN-1 and OCN-2 achieved high solid-state photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQYs) of 92% and 95%, respectively. The hydrophobic organotin internal surface further imparted superhydrophobicity, broad aqueous stability, and negligible PL quenching under high-humidity. Under 800 nm femtosecond excitation, OCN-1 exhibited a pronounced TPEF response with an apparent two-photon absorption cross section (σ2 , app) of approximately 4755 GM. In colloidal dispersions, its σ2 , app was nearly 7.3-fold higher than that of H4ETTC aggregates under identical conditions. These findings establish organotin-directed chromophore packing as an effective strategy for converting AIE chromophore aggregation into moisture-resistant crystalline materials with enhanced nonlinear fluorescence.
n3738feb97b51: Achieving high‐energy‐density lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs) requires deep delithiation of layered oxides, yet operating LiCoO2 (LCO) above 4.55 V triggers Co‐O electronic instability and accelerates electrolyte degradation. Electrolyte additives can passivate this interface, yet which molecular features control surface coordination and interphase chemistry remains unclear. Here we show that the regioisomeric substitution pattern of pyridone additives couples surface coordination to protective interphase formation, producing distinct stabilization mechanisms. Among the isomers, the para‐isomer 5‐fluoro‐2‐hydroxy‐3‐nitropyridine (p‐HNFP) yields the most effective stabilization. Spectroscopic and computational analyses indicate that p‐HNFP adsorbs preferentially on the delithiated LCO surface through σ‐type lone‐pair donation from the pyridone carbonyl oxygen to electron‐deficient Co4+ centers, lowering the O 2p band center and widening the Co 3d‐O 2p gap, consistent with a reduced thermodynamic driving force for lattice‐oxygen oxidation. This interaction operates in tandem with a compact, LiF‐ and nitrogen‐enriched cathode‐electrolyte interphase (CEI) formed by regioselective oxidative decomposition of p‐HNFP, suppressing dehydrogenation‐initiated carbonate decomposition and preserving LCO structural integrity. Consequently, 1 wt% p‐HNFP enables fast‐charging 2 Ah Gr||LCO pouch cells (2.46 mAh cm−2) to retain 92.4% capacity after 400 cycles at 4.6 V. These findings establish regioisomeric engineering as a molecular design strategy for stabilizing high‐voltage LiCoO2 interphases in LIBs.
n416ae2c02351: The insufficient stability of transition metal nitrogen-doped carbon (TM-N-C) catalysts has hindered the widespread adoption of non-precious-metal proton-exchange-membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs). Herein, using Fe-doped MET(Zn)-derived materials as a versatile platform, we unravel the role of oxygen groups in Fe-N-C catalyst degradation while achieving substantially enhanced fuel cell performance. DFT results indicate that carbonyl (C═O) and epoxy (C─O─C) groups lower the energy barrier of the rate-determining step in the carbon oxidation reaction (COR), strengthen intermediate *OOH adsorption, and thereby accelerate carbon support corrosion. Based on this, a hydrogen-thermal reduction strategy was developed to construct the FeSA/NC-H catalyst with low surface oxygen content. Experimental results demonstrate the outstanding activity and stability of the FeSA/NC-H catalyst. In H2-O2 PEMFCs, the catalyst achieves a peak power density (P max) of 1.32 W cm−2, which is 1.26 times that of the reference catalyst (1.05 W cm−2). After 30 000 accelerated stress tests, FeSA/NC-H retains 77.3% of its initial P max, 1.56 times that of FeSA/NC (49.5%). It also shows only 7.5% voltage decay during a 100 h open-circuit voltage durability test.
n7eff699c0df1: The ZIF-8/Ag2SeO3 heterostructure was designed to combine the adsorption capacity and porous architecture of zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (ZIF-8) with the multifunctional response of Ag2SeO3 (ASO), seeking synergistic interactions that could yield a material with enhanced, complementary functionalities. We report the synthesis and interfacial evolution of ZIF-8/ASO heterostructures and the in situ formation of metallic Ag nanoparticles (NPs) under electron irradiation. X-ray diffraction confirms the coexistence of cubic ZIF-8 (I43m) and monoclinic ASO (P21/c) phases, with a microstructure consisting of ZIF-8 NPs uniformly anchored on ASO microrods in intimate interfacial contact. Time-resolved electron microscopy directly captures the nucleation and growth of Ag NPs on the ZIF-8 surface during electron irradiation, as confirmed by HRTEM-SAED and elemental maps, indicating spatially confined cubic Ag NPs with exposed (111) and (200) planes. Photoluminescence measurements show pronounced emission quenching and spectral redistribution, indicating modified optoelectronic behavior following heterostructure formation. First-principles calculations identify the ZIF-8/ASO(010) interface as a favorable configuration, characterized by strong interfacial interaction and significant charge redistribution. These results are consistent with the experimentally observed localized formation of Ag NPs and suggest that interfacial electronic interactions contribute to Ag+ reduction. Overall, the ZIF-8/ASO heterostructure provides an electron-responsive platform for localized Ag NP formation and interfacial optoelectronic modulation, offering insights into electron-beam-induced processes in ZIF-8-based heterostructures.
nf0eefd93a180: No single scalar captures disorder in high-entropy and compositionally complex fluorites. This Perspective evaluates compositional and structural descriptors by physical meaning, reference frame, covariance, and transferability. Pairwise cation mismatch contains the same information as size variance, whereas host-referenced misfit adds a reference-dependent mean-radius offset. Analysis of twenty-four published compositions from three systematic datasets illustrates the limits of configurational entropy and size variance as independent descriptors of phase formation and transport. With equal Hf, Zr, and Ce fractions, changing the host reference reverses misfit rankings and alters the host-offset term up to 78-fold. In twelve dual-phase zirconates and mixed zirconate-hafnates, the nominal rA/rB ratio correlates with phase fraction but describes neither coexisting phase, whereas measured phase compositions give non-overlapping fluorite and pyrochlore values, distinguishing descriptor limitations from inappropriate evaluation frames. Structural observables are assessed by specificity, reproducibility, and relevance. Together, these criteria and the compositional analysis define a framework that distinguishes compositional inputs, multiplicity and crystal-chemical mismatch, from their structural realization. Its purpose is to test descriptor relevance and limits rather than predict untested compositions.
n1a277cd90f77: Template-guided crystal-chemical design offers a route to oxonitridosilicates, but transfer of an oxide topology requires compatible cation coordination and charge balance. Here, we report the synthesis and structural characterization of the 6-ring host La2Ca3[Si4N4O8], designed by considering [SiN]+ for [AlO]+ substitution in the Ca3[Al2O6] template together with aliovalent La3+/Ca2+ substitution. The idealized structural description contains isolated rings of corner-sharing [SiN2O2] tetrahedra and partially occupied or vacant cation sites. The nominal substitution scheme, 3Ca2+ → 2La3+ + VCa, provides a charge-balanced crystal-chemical rationale for the cation deficiency. Theoretical calculations reveal that the aliovalent substitution induces cation vacancies accompanied by local charge redistribution and coordination rearrangement, which may alleviate the lattice strain arising from the cation-size mismatch. Eu2+ activation produces broadband orange emission centered near 600 nm, with a reported photoluminescence quantum yield of 29.3%. The phosphor was further applied to a white LED by combining it with multiple phosphors. This work illustrates how cation composition and occupancy can be considered alongside the topology in template-guided exploratory synthesis.
n8480f57e0833: The development of efficient, low-cost, and earth-abundant electrocatalysts for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) is essential for sustainable green hydrogen production and the transition toward a carbon-neutral energy economy. Although...
n3e692bd3627d: Catalytic conversion of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) waste into biodegradable plastic monomers, terephthalic acid (TPA) and glycolic acid (GA), has emerged as a compelling strategy toward sustainable plastic valorization. Conventional two-step...
nb6e0a7738829: The first asymmetric total syntheses of sesterterpenoids (+)-asperterpenoids D and E, together with a concurrent synthesis of diterpenoid ent-(−)-homoverrucosanol were achieved from (S)-limonene through a chiral-pool strategy featuring a common late-stage intermediate. Key transformations include a Michael addition and a highly diastereoselective Type I [5 + 2] cycloaddition, which successively establish the C-14 and C-11 methyl-bearing stereocenters with complete stereocontrol. Subsequent oxa-bridge cleavage, cyclopropanation, and A-ring formation via hydroformylation and Carreira cyclopentenal synthesis proceed stereospecifically.
ne89ec8555ad1: Fast battery charging is limited by sluggish Li+ transport at the anode/electrolyte interface, which is governed by the interfacial solvation structure (ISS). However, negative polarization disfavors anion accumulation at the anode interface, hindering the formation of anion-rich ISS required for rapid Li+ transfer. Here, leveraging the cation effect in electrocatalysis, we propose a cation-mediated strategy to reshape the interfacial electric field and construct anion-rich ISS in commercial electrolytes. With benzyltriethylammonium serving as a model cationic regulator, we show that it accumulates near the polarized graphite surface and forms a cation layer that alters the local electric field. This cation-mediated interfacial regulation promotes PF6– accumulation at the interface, redirects early solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) formation toward anion-derived pathways, mitigates solvent decomposition, and accelerates Li+ desolvation and transport.
