As a result, graphite-based pouch cells deliver ∼88.2% state of charge within 6 min, maintain stable cycling for 2000 cycles with ∼71% capacity retention, and provide ∼218.2 Wh kg–1 with 10 min charging. Beyond LiPF6-based electrolytes, this cation effect also promotes reduction of the anions in other lithium-salt systems. This work bridges electrocatalytic cation effects and battery interfacial chemistry, offering a practical route to fast-charging lithium-ion batteries.
n600ebf29ce0b: De novo design of catalytic metalloproteins has the potential to generate enzymes that combine the efficiency of natural proteins with the reactivity of synthetic organometallic catalysts. Here, we develop a computational strategy to design enzymes with novel tertiary structures that bind metal salen complexes, classic small-molecule catalysts not found in biology. Six proteins were designed and screened for function; five of six express well, bind a Co-salen cofactor, and catalyze a transition metal hydrogen atom transfer (MHAT)-mediated deallylation reaction, representing the first de novo proteins to catalyze this class of transformation. The spectroscopic properties and crystal structure of the most active sequence were in excellent agreement with the design, and the holoprotein retained its structure and activity over a broad range of pH (2–12), temperatures up to 95 °C, and aqueous/organic solvent mixtures. We suggest that the combinatorial space provided by metal ion identity, ligand substitution, and active site structure can be used to generate artificial metalloenzymes that catalyze many chemical transformations.
ne678a1e6e440: Two-dimensional (2D) carbon allotropes have unique properties, synthetic tunability, and potential applications across several fields including catalysis, energy storage, and electronics. One such allotrope is the recently discovered graphullerite, which results from the oxidation and deintercalation of the layered rhombohedral fullerene polymer (Mg4C60)∞. The current synthetic approach to (Mg4C60)∞ is limited by low yield, phase impurity, and small crystal size, all of which preclude a comprehensive investigation of the physical and electronic properties of bulk graphullerite and its 2D derivative, graphullerene. Here, we demonstrate two chemical vapor transport methods that produce rhombohedral (Mg4C60)∞ and tetragonal (Mg2C60)∞ as millimeter-sized single crystals with near-complete conversion. Our methods spatially separate the starting materials to circumvent both the thermal decomposition of (Mg4C60)∞ and the significant disparity in vapor pressure between C60 and Mg. We find that using Mg foil results in a near-complete conversion of C60 into a mixture of (Mg4C60)∞ and (Mg2C60)∞. Replacing the foil with Mg2Si produces phase-pure (Mg4C60)∞ with an isolated crystalline yield of 55 to 62%. This high-yielding, phase-pure synthesis enables us to investigate the electrochemical intercalation and deintercalation of Mg2+ into the lattice.
na487b059128e: Metabolic theories for the origin of life postulate that chemical reaction networks emerged spontaneously from geochemistry and grew more complex due to positive feedback effects in catalysis. However, experimentally establishing protometabolic networks has proven challenging. In this Perspective, we make the case for electric field catalysis at charged aqueous interfaces as a crucial overlooked element for initiating protometabolic networks, an initial constraint that foreshadows the eventual takeover of electrostatic catalysis by enzymes. We first overview types of positive feedback relevant to the early evolution of metabolism, the theory of electric field catalysis, and its dominant role in enzyme catalysis. We then examine recent experiments and calculations highlighting the ability of external electric fields to enable nonenzymatic analogues of challenging metabolic reactions in micro- to millisecond reaction times. An underexplored mode of small molecule catalysis (reorientation catalysis) that can only operate in external electric fields is proposed to make positive feedback within prebiotic reaction networks more achievable. By embodying electrostatic catalysis, compartmentalization, and ion concentration gradients, charged aqueous interfaces prepattern three fundamental features of biology, making them a preferred environment for a metabolic origin of life. Making robust progress on the origin of life may surprisingly require exploring the nascent area of electric field-mediated chemistry at aqueous interfaces. Life does not use electric fields to catalyze its metabolic network by accident.
n62b1351e5d7c: Three-dimensional covalent organic frameworks (3D COFs) have emerged as a rapidly growing class of crystalline porous materials, yet reported structures adhere to the reticular chemistry paradigm of fully connected building blocks. Here, we report a geometry-induced construction strategy that enables the synthesis of sub-stoichiometric 3D COFs─JUC-748, JUC-749, and JUC-750─by deliberately combining building blocks with similar geometries but distinct connectivity. Their structures are determined by continuous rotation electron diffraction and powder X-ray diffraction, revealing that connectivity incompatibility enforces partial condensation and leaves unreacted aldehyde groups periodically arrayed along the pore walls. The frameworks exhibit Brunauer–Emmett–Teller surface areas up to 2836 m2 g–1, and the spatially ordered aldehyde modified pores create a highly favorable adsorption environment for SO2. Remarkably, JUC-748 achieves a SO2 uptake of 16.9 mmol g–1 at 298 K and 1 bar, representing one of the highest values reported for porous organic materials to date. This work establishes geometry-induced construction as a powerful and general strategy for creating intrinsically functionalized 3D COFs with ordered reactive sites, high porosity, and excellent adsorption performance
n4c2b0cc6f0f8: Divalent rare-earth solids with a 4fn+1 configuration provide access to electronic structures in which localized 4f states coexist with low-lying, structurally responsive 5d states, yet the combined magnetic, electrical, and optical manifestations of these states remain underexplored in extended Tm2+ compounds. Here, we investigate layered TmI2 as an extended Tm2+ solid and employ Cs4TmI6 with isolated TmI6 units and dilute SrI2:Tm2+ as targeted reference systems. Structural, spectroscopic, and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopic measurements support Tm2+ as the dominant oxidation state, while electronic-structure calculations reveal narrow, localized, occupied Tm 4f-derived bands and low-lying Tm 5d-derived unoccupied states, with substantially greater 5d dispersion in TmI2 than in Cs4TmI6. Magnetic measurements establish localized 4f13 Kramers-ion behavior on the triangular Tm2+ lattice of TmI2, together with a small negative low-temperature Weiss temperature and no evidence of long-range magnetic ordering down to 2 K. Comparative luminescence, photothermal, and photocurrent measurements reveal distinct photoresponses across the three systems within a shared electronic-level framework encompassing 4f–5d and 4f–4f transitions. Relative to Cs4TmI6 and SrI2:Tm2+, TmI2 exhibits a lower-energy optical absorption onset, weaker photoluminescence, and a more pronounced light-induced current response despite its high electrical resistivity. Its wavelength-dependent photothermal response broadly follows the 4f–5d absorption profile. Together, these results establish layered TmI2 as a distinctive rare-earth platform that combines the 4f13 magnetic characteristics familiar from Yb3+ systems with low-energy 4f–5d excitations, expanding the scope for investigating rare-earth magnetic solids with optical excitation channels beyond 4f–4f transitions.
n8ca38aefcd83: Membrane proteins engage in dynamic transient interactions with surrounding lipids along with their substrates. Capturing these concomitant contacts often remains a challenging problem. Here, we demonstrate that generative deep learning-designed WRAP domains can preserve weak interactions of membrane proteins in native mass spectrometry. Using WRAP-fused GlpG, AqpM, and OmpA as model systems, we show that lipids can bind in multiple positions inside the WRAP, allowing for their characterization by native mass spectrometry. We show that lipid interactions can be altered by changing the WRAP structure. We use the approach to show that WRAP–OmpA binds phosphatidylethanolamine lipids within cavities formed at the protein–WRAP interface, while simultaneously accommodating weak chitobiose ligand binding. These findings establish WRAPs as versatile vehicles to probe ligand and lipid interactions of membrane proteins.
n7c0a74c93f5a: NMR spectroscopy enables reliable quantification of the metabolites present in a biological sample. The number of metabolites that can be assessed from NMR spectra is often limited by the intrinsically high complexity of the spectra, arising from the large number of molecules paired with their complex spectral patterns. 31P NMR based metabolomics embraces a reduced yet broad view of the metabolism and significantly facilitates the interpretation of the spectra due to a lower number of signals and a larger chemical shift dispersion. However, full quantification of metabolites can still be hindered by the presence of crowded regions. Here we exploit the fact that NMR lineshapes can be simulated precisely from quantum mechanical calculations for disentangling these crowded regions. Iterative subtraction of accurately simulated and fitted spectra of metabolites presenting isolated signals from the experimental spectrum yields meaningful residuals, enabling assignment and quantification of completely hidden metabolites. This approach ended at a noise-level residual spectrum, granting the full quantification of the 31P NMR spectrum. We implemented this approach in MR-SHIFT, a program developed in this work for spin Hamiltonian simulations and spectral fitting, which was then applied to the fully automated analysis of 31P NMR spectra of mouse tissues.
n0984d5a51c57: Semiconductor nanocrystals (NCs) are of interest due to their tunable electronic and optical properties. However, the atomic-level characterization of surface structures of NCs remains an unresolved challenge. Here, we demonstrate that rotational-echo double-resonance (REDOR) experiments can be used to determine structural models of surfaces of CdSe NCs. An atom-efficient ligand-exchange scheme is demonstrated to introduce partially 13C-enriched oleate ligands onto CdSe NCs and enable 13C-dephased REDOR experiments. DNP-enhanced 13C{77Se}, 77Se{13C}, 13C{111Cd}, and 111Cd{13C} REDOR NMR experiments were performed on the 13C-enriched oleate-capped zinc blende CdSe NCs. Despite the modest isotope abundance of 77Se and 111Cd, DNP-enhanced 13C{77Se} and 13C{111Cd} REDOR NMR experiments show significant dephasing due to dipolar coupling between 13C atoms and multiple 77Se or 111Cd atoms that are present in the underlying NC lattice. Multispin simulations of 13C{77Se}, 77Se{13C}, 13C{111Cd}, and 111Cd{13C} REDOR curves are performed for different surface structure models, accounting for the structure of the underlying CdSe NC lattice. Based upon these simulations, we propose a structural model of oleate-capped CdSe NCs where chelating carboxylate ligands bind to Cd atoms on {100} zinc blende CdSe surfaces. The combination of REDOR NMR experiments and multispin simulations is a powerful and general method for determining the atomic-level structures of semiconductor NCs and other inorganic materials.
na21dc6408162: Molecular ferroelectrics hold great potential for bioelectronics because of their excellent piezoelectric responses and biocompatibility. However, conventional integration into gel matrices suffers from two major drawbacks: solvent evaporation methods often yield brittle films with poor modulus matching with soft tissues, whereas physical blending typically leads to filler agglomeration and random crystal dispersion, making it difficult to achieve preferential crystal orientation and thereby limiting the piezoelectric performance. Here, we report an in situ crystallization strategy assisted by solvent exchange. This approach enables preferentially oriented triglycine sulfate (TGS) crystals to form within a polyacrylamide (PAM) network reinforced by glycidyl methacrylate-grafted bovine serum albumin (B-G). The B-G macromer strengthens the network through covalent integration and reversible hydrogen-bonding interactions. Subsequent treatment with a choline chloride/sorbitol deep eutectic solvent (DES) induced the preferential orientation of TGS within the gel matrix. The resulting gel achieved a fracture strain exceeding 2800%, maintained mechanical integrity over 10000 loading–unloading cycles, and exhibited mechanical compliance within the range of human soft tissues (10–5–10–4 Pa–1). In vitro and in vivo evaluations further demonstrated favorable biocompatibility and its potential for flexible piezoelectric sensing applications. This work provides molecular-level insight into the design of highly conformable piezoelectric gels containing preferentially oriented molecular ferroelectrics for tissue-matched biointerfaces.
n8efab071cfee: Oxidation governs the stability and functional conversion of two-dimensional semiconductors, yet its propagation through layered crystals remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate the thickness-dependent oxidation of GaSe using optical spectroscopy, cross-sectional microscopy, and first-principles calculations. Experiments reveal concurrent top-down and edge-initiated oxidation, accompanied by Se redistribution and transient Ga2Se3 formation. Calculations identify Se vacancies as favorable sites for O2 adsorption and activation, which weaken neighboring Ga–Se bonds and promote oxygen incorporation. Molecular O2 faces a 4.03 eV barrier when penetrating a monolayer Ga2O3 model, compared with 0.54 eV along a GaSe van der Waals gap. This contrast supports interlayer diffusion as a plausible pathway for lateral oxidation, consistent with the pronounced thickness dependence and spatial anisotropy observed experimentally. Oxidation also yields a progression from p-type GaSe through ambipolar Ga2O3/GaSe heterostructures to n-type Ga2O3, whose devices retain stable characteristics after 300 °C air annealing.
nfecb34b17aec: Two-dimensional (2D) van der Waals (vdW) magnet-based heterostructures provide a vital platform for manipulating magnetic ground states and hosting complex spin textures. The topological Hall effect (THE) is a powerful tool for probing these textures in such systems. However, achieving a sizable THE in 2D vdW ferromagnets remains challenging due to the absence of broken inversion symmetry and sufficiently strong spin–orbit coupling (SOC). Here, we report an emergent giant topological Hall resistivity of 6.9 μΩ·cm at 10 K by interfacing the 2D ferromagnet Fe3GeTe2 (FGT) with the topological insulator BiSbTeSe2 (BSTS). Systematic temperature- and thickness-dependent studies suggest the origin of this pronounced signal to be the interfacial Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction (DMI). Furthermore, temperature-field mapping reveals the coexistence of two distinct phases that we identify as having opposite topological charge. Our results establish these vdW ferromagnet/topological insulator heterostructures as a robust platform for enhanced interfacial THE, opening new avenues for high-efficiency topological spintronics.
n70f75f0de887: Controlling doping density in correlated quantum materials offers a route to tuning their electronic states, but chemical doping can introduce disorder and limits dynamic control. Here, we demonstrate optically tunable electron doping of the layered Mott insulator α-RuCl3 through photoinduced interlayer charge transfer in MoS2/α-RuCl3 heterostructures. Photoluminescence and transient absorption measurements support electron transfer to α-RuCl3, leaving holes in MoS2. The layer-separated carrier population persists for more than 100 ps with an estimated doping density tunable through the excitation fluence. Selective excitation of α-RuCl3 further reveals hole transfer to MoS2. Transient absorption microscopy yields an early time effective hole diffusion coefficient of approximately 100 cm2 s–1 in the heterostructure, supporting a predominantly unbound carrier population. These results establish photoinduced charge transfer as a means of dynamically controlling carrier doping in α-RuCl3, providing a route toward optical manipulation of correlated electronic states.
n72d73a2d9bd9: Quasi-bound states in the continuum (quasi-BICs) offer a powerful platform for refractometric sensing by combining narrow resonances with strong electromagnetic confinement, promising high spectral resolution and large figures of merit (FOM). In practice, however, these advantages are often compromised by stringent angular alignment in passive transmission/reflection interrogation. Here, we demonstrate an active sensing platform that couples the defect-related photoluminescence (PL) of a freestanding silicon nitride nanomembrane to quasi-BIC modes. The substrate-free architecture suppresses radiation leakage and sustains tightly confined high-Q resonances, while emission-based readout bypasses stringent angular alignment. The resulting PL resonances exhibit line widths of 0.17 nm (Q ≈ 4000) in air and 0.26 nm in water. In aqueous sensing, the platform achieves a FOM of 250, substantially exceeding representative values reported for passive quasi-BIC sensors in the visible regime. This synergy translates the high-Q advantage of quasi-BICs into a practical active platform for high-performance refractometric and surface-binding sensing.
n13fe6e555fad: Lithium niobate (LiNbO3) crystals have been widely used in photonic and electronic devices owing to their outstanding intrinsic optoelectronic properties. However, fabricating hundreds-of-micrometer-thick LiNbO3 wafers remains dominated by diamond wire sawing, which causes substantial material loss. Although ultrafast laser processing offers a promising alternative, the intrinsic noncentrosymmetric lattice, spontaneous polarization, and anisotropic photothermal response of LiNbO3 severely hinder high-quality laser cutting. Here, a thermal dissipation-guided vector scanning technology is proposed to realize ultrafast laser slicing of LiNbO3 crystals for the first time. By tailoring the scanning direction according to the anisotropic thermal dissipation, we achieve crystal exfoliation with an ultrathin subsurface damage layer of 10 μm and an exceptionally high-quality separation surface. The results establish vector scanning technology as an innovative route for high-quality femtosecond laser processing and low-damage separation of anisotropic crystals.
naad0a4dfa2c3: Redox processes in oxides are central to materials synthesis and functionality, but their control is often hindered by surface instabilities. Using ambient-pressure X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, we show that a nominally 1 nm-thick SrTiO3 (STO) cap markedly enhances the surface stability of La0.05Sr0.95FeO2.5-δ (LSFO) thin films during H2 reduction by suppressing the formation of a secondary metallic Fe0 phase. Kinetic analysis indicates that the STO cap reduces the effective Fe0 formation rates by more than 6-fold at both 250 and 350 °C. These findings highlight ultrathin capping layers as an effective strategy for stabilizing oxide surfaces during redox.
nab3528a186d8: Ru single-atom catalysts are promising for NH3 oxidation but still suffer from poor activity and N2 selectivity, mainly owing to the poisoning of the isolated Ru active sites by the over-strong NH3 adsorption. Herein, we fabricated an asymmetric Ru-W atomic pair anchored on CeO2 (Ru1–W1/Ce) exhibiting considerable low-temperature activity (∼90% at 200 °C), high N2 selectivity (∼85% at 350 °C), and notable stability (∼500 h at 200 °C), surpassing most of the previously reported catalysts for NH3 oxidation. Systematic experimental and theoretical investigations demonstrated that a strong d-f orbital interaction between Ru and W atoms was revealed, inducing the smooth electron transfer from W to Ru atoms. The electron-rich Ru single atom not only weakened NH3 adsorption strength to alleviate NH3 poisoning but also reduced the energy barrier of the rate-determining step of NH3 activation. Besides, isolated W atoms coordinated with active Ru species, leading to a decrease in Ru–O–Ce coordination number. This could suppress the activation of O2 and thereby the deep oxidation of NH3. Accordingly, the reaction mechanism over this asymmetric Ru–W catalyst changed from the initial i-SCR to an imide-like pathway, accounting for its considerable catalytic performance. This work provided a paradigm for advanced Ru-based catalysts enabling both high activity and high N2 selectivity in NH3 oxidation.
n8d31f1b33dd3: A fundamental challenge in harnessing substrate promiscuity for industrial biocatalysis lies in reconciling broad substrate acceptance with high catalytic specificity. Although promiscuous enzymes provide attractive starting points for accessing non-natural transformations, their native active-site architectures and conformational dynamics often lack the precision required for efficient and selective conversion of desired unnatural substrates. Thus, systematically decoding and reprogramming the interplay between promiscuity and specificity remains a key obstacle toward versatile biocatalysts. Here, we address this challenge by integrating virtual screening, machine learning, and molecular dynamics simulations into a unified engineering framework. A tropinone reductase from Cochlearia officinalis (CoTR) was identified as a broadly promiscuous scaffold. By converting complex enzyme–substrate interaction dynamics into quantifiable and actionable design principles, we predict and validate key residues that govern substrate promiscuity. Guided by these insights, distinct CoTR variants were engineered for three representative substrates. The optimized variants—CoTR‑8M, CoTR‑5M‑1, and CoTR‑5M‑2—exhibited 7.0‑ to 16.3‑fold higher catalytic efficiencies than wild-type CoTR toward their respective target substrates and supported substrate loadings of up to 50 or 100 g L–1 while maintaining >99% ee. This work not only delivers scalable routes to three industrially valuable chiral alcohols but also provides mechanistic insights into the synergistic modulation of promiscuity and specificity. This study demonstrates a general strategy for translating intricate molecular-recognition features into rational design principles, thereby facilitating the development of tailored biocatalysts for non-native substrates.
nf27e7805d3f1: Tin–lead (Sn–Pb) perovskites are essential narrow-bandgap absorbers for two-terminal perovskite–perovskite tandem solar cells, yet their extreme air sensitivity has confined stability studies indoors, leaving real-world durability unexplored. Here, we substantially lower this barrier using industrially relevant, lamination-based encapsulation that enables, to our knowledge, the first outdoor demonstration of Sn–Pb devices. Combining polyisobutylene edge sealing with polyolefin elastomer encapsulation, we demonstrate that the lamination process is highly compatible with Sn–Pb devices, causing negligible performance loss while preserving optoelectronic quality during short-term air exposure. Under package-oriented accelerated aging, epoxy-based encapsulation fails rapidly, whereas the lamination-based package remains intact. Outdoors under tandem-relevant filtered illumination, lamination-encapsulated devices retain ∼80% of initial efficiency after 12 days, while epoxy-encapsulated devices lose all output within 6 days. By adapting manufacturable module packaging to Sn–Pb devices, this work enables their realistic field evaluation, marks a critical step toward deployable all-perovskite tandems, and strengthens confidence in their commercial viability.
nc0ed9774edbf: The lack of clear identification or understanding of the key perpetrators activating the tumor microenvironment (TME) impedes development of TME-modulating therapeutic strategies that could overcome the challenges associated with tumor growth, metastasis, and therapy resistance. Here, we report the development of a hybrid nanomaterial designed to genetically silence one key regulator, IGFBP2 (insulin-like growth factor binding protein 2), responsible for multicellular crosstalk within the TME. We demonstrated that silencing of IGFBP2 by this hybrid nanomaterial suppressed angiogenesis, stromal activation, and tumor cell phenotypes both in vitro and in vivo in preclinical models of ovarian cancer. Mechanistically, the hybrid nanomaterial utilizes the caveolae-mediated intracellular uptake pathway rather than a mixture of clathrin and caveolin as seen with a nonhybrid counterpart. Given the role of IGFBP2 as a prognostic factor for several cancers, and the absence of any small molecule inhibitor of IGFBP2, the current strategy may be exploited as a promising and generalized approach to target the TME and improve therapeutic outcomes in numerous cancers, including ovarian cancer
nee4603330991: Small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) represent promising cell-free therapeutics for spinal cord injury (SCI). However, their therapeutic efficacy remains limited by variable cargo potency and insufficient cell-selective delivery. Here, we developed a modular biomimetic vesicle platform integrating hypoxic remodeling of mesenchymal stem cell-derived sEV (MSC-sEV) cargo with astrocyte membrane engineering. In a rat model of SCI, hypoxia-preconditioned MSC-sEVs (Hyp-sEVs) attenuated C3-positive astrocyte reactivity and improved functional outcomes. Proteomic profiling and functional analyses identified ERBIN as a key therapeutic cargo enriched in Hyp-sEVs that contributed to suppression of the NOD2/IRF3/GBP1 signaling axis. To enhance astrocyte-directed delivery, Hyp-sEVs were fused with astrocyte-derived membranes to generate astrocyte membrane-engineered vesicles (A-EVs). A-EVs were preferentially taken up by astrocytes, and blocking and knockdown experiments implicated MERTK and the ligands PROS1/GAS6 in this uptake. A-EVs outperformed Hyp-sEVs in preserving spinal cord tissue and promoting functional recovery. Together, these findings indicate that coupling hypoxia-remodeled sEV cargo with astrocyte membrane engineering promotes preferential vesicle uptake by astrocytes, attenuates C3-positive astrocyte reactivity, and improves functional recovery after SCI in rats.
ncb5a7cf80538: As conventional complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor technology approaches its fundamental scaling limits in binary logic, alternative device concepts have attracted increasing attention. Negative differential resistance (NDR) devices offer a promising route toward multivalued logic. However, their practical implementation requires both a high peak-to-valley current ratio (PVCR) and high drive current density at room temperature, necessitating complex device architectures and fabrication processes. Here, we report a heterojunction-free WSe2 NDR device on a hexagonal boron nitride dielectric, exhibiting a PVCR of up to 42.9 and a width-normalized peak current density of approximately 280.8 μA/μm at room temperature. The NDR emerges evidently after gate-polarity reversal, thus suggesting the formation of a bias-history-dependent nonequilibrium carrier configuration. Systematic variations of the gate-bias magnitude, duration, hold time, and sweep rate indicate that the relaxation of this nonequilibrium carrier configuration governs the peak current, peak voltage, and PVCR of the NDR characteristics. Surface passivation using poly(methyl methacrylate) further enhances both the PVCR and peak current, highlighting the sensitivity of the NDR to the surface electrostatic environment. These findings establish a bias-history-driven electrostatic mechanism for NDR in homogeneous two-dimensional layered semiconductors and provide a simple and scalable strategy for realizing high-performance heterojunction-free NDR devices.
n50c95ed372a2: Bloodstream infections (BSIs) are life-threatening systemic syndromes with a high mortality rate, characterized by a highly sequential pathophysiological progression. Although early antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory treatments have improved short-term survival rates, single-stage interventions are insufficient to reverse the high risk of long-term mortality among survivors. To address the urgent clinical need for stage-specific interventions to improve patient outcomes, nanomaterials have emerged as a highly promising platform due to their design flexibility and intelligent microenvironmental responsiveness. This Review first outlines the pathophysiological characteristics of BSIs at each stage, from the initial pathogen invasion to the final multiple-organ dysfunction, which serves as the basis for the design of nanomaterials. Then, following the progression of BSIs, the representative nanotherapeutic strategies developed in recent years for different pathological stages are systematically categorized and discussed. Finally, the review discusses the challenges confronting nanomaterials in BSI management, such as the selection of optimal treatment timing and clinical translation, and provides future perspectives on design strategies and developmental directions for nanomaterials in BSI treatment.
nd4f78996163a: The continued scaling of silicon-based dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) slows down due to increased process complexity and reduced storage capacitance. Oxide semiconductors (OS), represented by InGaZnOx (IGZO), offer an attractive alternative owing to their ultralow leakage and low thermal budget, making them promising candidates for next-generation DRAM as well as monolithic three-dimensional (M3D) architectures. However, realizing IGZO devices with well-balanced overall performance, including high performance and high reliability under ultrascaled dimensions, remains challenging. Here, we report ultrascaled IGZO field-effect transistors (FETs) fabricated using an optimized O2 plasma-enhanced atomic-layer deposition (PE-ALD) process. The IGZO FETs deliver state-of-the-art performance, including an on-state current (Ion) of 785 μA/μm at a drain voltage of 0.5 V and a transconductance (gm) of 620 μS/μm at a drain voltage of 1.0 V alongside a contact resistance (Rc) of 164.5 Ω·μm with positive threshold voltage (Vth). Reliability degradation is effectively suppressed, with bias-temperature instability (BTI) down to 8 mV even at extremely scaled contact length (Lc) of 50 nm. Leveraging these optimized devices, we further demonstrated a scaled two-transistor-zero-capacitor (2T0C) DRAM capable of up to 6-bit per cell, long data retention over 4000 s, and write time down to 10 ns. We proposed an M3D-DRAM architecture with vertically stacked multilayer embedded memory for artificial intelligence (AI) accelerators, achieving 77× faster weight loading and 9.6× lower energy consumption compared with mature high-bandwidth memory (HBM) counterpart, while maintaining graphics processing units (GPU)-equivalent inference accuracy of 92.25%. This work demonstrates an effective approach for the co-optimization of performance and reliability in ultrascaled IGZO FETs, providing critical foundation for next-generation DRAM and M3D applications.
n2d216eedd750: This study demonstrates proximity-induced ferroelectric switching in a stacked ferroelectric film composed of fluorite-structured HfZrO2 (HZO) and wurtzite-structured AlN, which are grown by thermal atomic layer deposition (ALD) and plasma-enhanced ALD (PEALD), respectively. The stacked film shows remanent polarization close to that of HZO but with a much higher coercive field, desirable for enhancing the memory window of ferroelectric thin-film transistors (FeTFTs) for storage applications. The FeTFT with a 5 nm-thick amorphous In–Ga–Zn–O (a-IGZO) channel layer, also grown by ALD, shows a memory window of ∼6.1 V, and data retention over 10 years. It also shows stable endurance cycles of ∼104. These enhancements over the single-layer HZO or stacked HZO/Al2O3 films, which show a minimal memory window of ∼0.3 V and ∼−0.3 V, respectively, are ascribed to the proximity ferroelectric effects between the soft ferroelectric HZO and hard ferroelectric AlN. These results, together with the conformal deposition of the HZO/AlN stack in high-aspect-ratio structures, demonstrate the feasibility of extending the ALD/PEALD-based Prox-FE materials platform toward three-dimensional (3D) process integration.
n4c887f9d2d63: The photochemical behavior of two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors in aqueous environments is conventionally framed primarily by reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation and consumption balance, yet the molecular weight (MW) heterogeneity of ubiquitous dissolved organic matter and its interfacial modulation remain poorly understood. Using few-layer black phosphorus (FLBP) and MW-fractionated fulvic acid (FA) as a model system, we employ an integrated analytical platform, hollow fiber flow field-flow fractionation–inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (HF5-ICP-MS) for thickness-based fractionation and element-specific quantification of FLBP, coupled with fluorescence spectroscopy and ultrahigh-resolution mass spectrometry for molecular-level characterization of FA. We find that FA accelerates FLBP photodegradation while suppressing its photocatalytic activity across all MW fractions. Three distinct MW-dependent interfacial interaction modes account for this behavior: low-MW FA (<3 kDa) acts as a freely diffusing, sustained 1O2 photosensitizer with negligible compositional degradation, promoting FLBP degradation without substantially occupying surface sites; intermediate-MW FA (3–10 kDa) exhibits irradiation-enhanced surface adsorption, simultaneously delivering ROS to the FLBP interface and progressively blocking active sites; high-MW FA (>100 kDa) undergoes FLBP-mediated photoinduced disaggregation, selectively releasing aliphatic fragments while retaining condensed aromatic moieties on the nanosheet surface, maintaining interfacial ROS generation and surface occupancy. Photocatalytic tests show that surface site blockage by adsorbed FA outweighs supplementary ROS generation. These findings demonstrate that interfacial macromolecular organization, not radical yield alone, plays a critical role in the aqueous photochemistry of FLBP in macromolecule-rich media, and provide a mechanistic basis for understanding the behavior of 2D nanomaterials in complex aquatic systems.
n256e01efe0a3: Radiotherapy (RT) remains a cornerstone in cancer treatment, yet its immunogenic potential is not fully harnessed for personalized immunotherapy. Here, we report that extracellular vesicles released after radiotherapy (REVs) encapsulate tumor-specific antigens reflective of individual tumor profiles, thereby enabling them to serve as potential personalized antigen repositories. We found that REVs were enriched with immune-related proteins, particularly those involved in antigen processing and presentation. Leveraging this immunostimulatory capacity, we constructed a personalized antigen nanocarrier by surface-engineering these REVs with a thin iron hydroxide coating (REVs@FeOOH). This nanocarrier, which functions as a personalized cancer vaccine, efficiently disrupted the acidic endosomal environment in dendritic cells (DCs), promoting antigen escape into the cytosol and facilitating cross-presentation. Concurrently, the FeOOH layer catalyzed the generation of reactive oxygen species via a Fenton-like catalytic reaction, further driving DC maturation. REVs@FeOOH activated robust antitumor T cell responses and remodeled the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. This nanoengineering strategy provides a cost-effective and personalized platform for cancer immunotherapy, with translational potential in breast cancer and other solid tumors.
nf08342a52b19: Multilayered films composed of uniaxially aligned polythiophene layers stacked with controlled rotational offsets around the film normal were fabricated via a film transfer process. Although the polymer itself is achiral, the resulting multilayer structures exhibit structural helical chirality. The films show pronounced circular dichroism (CD) in the visible region, with both the intensity and sign systematically tunable by the number of layers, twist angles, and handedness of stacking. Ion-exchange doping further extends the CD response into the near-infrared region through polaron absorption. Optical simulations based on Mueller matrix analysis quantitatively reproduce the experimental CD spectra, thereby providing general design principles for tuning chiroptical responses. The simulations predict that insertion of transparent spacer layers enables enhancement of CD intensity by optimizing the optical pitch, which is experimentally validated. These results establish a versatile platform for engineering chiroptical responses from achiral polymer systems through structurally defined helical architectures.
nd91795f01b7f: Advancing modern energy storage requires a fundamental understanding of electrochemical interfaces, where the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) critically governs efficiency, safety, and cycle life. However, the atomic-level mechanism of its initial formation remains elusive, owing to the complexity of interfacial chemistry that challenges conventional ab initio simulations. Here, we developed a reactive machine learning potential to simulate electrolyte reduction at the anode/electrolyte interface, enabling nanosecond-scale machine learning molecular dynamics to obtain the atomic structure of SEI. By systematically varying the local Li loading at edge sites corresponding to different electrochemical potentials in the anode, we decipher the reaction pathways and identify reactive species, thereby revealing the underlying mechanism of SEI formation. Low Li loading leads to insufficient reduction and facilitates the diffusion of intermediates into the electrolyte, whereas high Li loading promotes the formation of inorganic-rich interfacial clusters that suppress further solvent decomposition. This work develops a computational framework for understanding interfacial chemistry and provides atomic-level insights into potential-dependent SEI evolution on graphite, thereby informing rational interfacial engineering in high-performance batteries.
nece520ae51d4: Measuring low‐frequency or infrasound acoustic signals plays a crucial role in the monitoring of natural disasters, structural health, and predictive maintenance of critical energy structures. Smart sound sensing systems often consist of linear sound sensors coupled to a separate processing unit, nonlinearly transforming the signal to solve the given task. However, nonlinear sensors have seen increased scientific interest in fields like reservoir computing, with the goal of minimizing power consumption by implementing the signal processing in the sensor itself. Here, the use of an organic electrochemical transistor based on conductive polymeric fibers embedded inside a free‐standing solidified gel membrane as a robust, highly sensitive, and nonlinear low‐frequency sound sensor is demonstrated. The slow dynamics of the device allow sensing in the low‐frequency and infrasound regime with a −3dB$-3 \,\mathrm{dB}$ cutoff‐frequency at around 1Hz$1 \,\mathrm{Hz}$ with power consumptions below 100μW$100 \,\umu\mathrm{W}$. Our work further demonstrates that the introduction of a gating mechanism increases sensitivity, nonlinearity, and stability compared to a previously introduced linear two‐terminal sensors. As a demonstration, we show that a three‐terminal device contains sufficient information to classify spoken digits from ten classes, using in‐software reservoir computing.
nbbaad6ef1ed3: Organic mixed ionic‐electronic conductors (OMIECs) sustain a wide range of bioelectronic, sensing, energy storage, and neuromorphic technologies. While water is known to enhance ionic transport and redox activity in these materials, the role of polarization dynamics in their electrical response remains largely unexplored. Here, eumelanin (EuM) is used as a model platform in which polarization‐assisted charge transport can be systematically resolved by varying hydration. To assess whether this characteristic polarization signature extends beyond EuM, complementary measurements were performed on the widely studied OMIEC PEDOT:PSS. By combining large‐ and small‐signal sinusoidal electrical measurements of EuM films with an analytical transport model, we demonstrate that hydration‐induced polarization dynamics generate displacement currents that can become comparable to conventional conductive currents. The results reveal a progressive transition from low‐hydration regimes characterized by limited charge redistribution and long relaxation times to highly hydrated states exhibiting a large density of polarization‐active sites and shorter relaxation times. These findings show that the electrical response of OMIECs cannot be fully described solely in terms of ionic and electronic conduction mechanisms, establishing a framework for identifying and interpreting polarization‐related contributions to their hysteretic electrical responses and providing a basis for future design strategies in sensing and memory technologies.
n62ab36ae12e6: Transient bioelectronics, as an emerging class of electronic systems, can degrade at controlled rates or within predefined time frames, thereby avoiding the risks associated with secondary surgical removal while reducing electronic waste. In biomedical applications, these systems offer new opportunities for short‐term monitoring, diagnosis, and therapy in both implantable and wearable formats. Within these systems, biodegradable conductors serve as core functional materials that enable sensing, electrical stimulation, and transmission of signals and energy, thereby determining overall device performance. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in biodegradable conductors, focusing on their degradation mechanisms and the key performance requirements for integration into transient bioelectronics. The characteristics of different classes of biodegradable conductors, including metals, conducting polymers, ionic conductors, and conductive composites, are discussed. Strategies for evaluating and regulating their functional lifetimes, as well as suitable fabrication approaches, are presented. Finally, representative biomedical applications in sensing, stimulation, energy devices, and drug delivery systems are summarized, and future perspectives for the development of transient bioelectronics are outlined.
n1eebd2f47c16: Spin‐charge interconversion mediated by spin‐orbit interaction represents a central concept in modern spintronics. The efficiency of spin‐charge interconversion is conventionally estimated from the Berry curvature of Bloch states within the linear‐response regime. Besides the linear regime, recent studies have uncovered nonlinear spin‐charge conversion arising from higher‐order electric‐field terms in noncentrosymmetric materials with nontrivial spin textures. Hence, harnessing and controlling such nonlinear responses promise opportunities for designable and reconfigurable nonlinear spintronic devices. Here, we report the nonlinear planar Hall effect in topological semimetal SrIrO3(001) thin film, enabled by inversion‐symmetry breaking at the interface. Furthermore, systematic transport measurements reveal robust second‐order electrical transport that can be dynamically and reversibly tuned by ionic‐liquid gating. This tunability originates from gating‐induced structural reconstruction, valence‐state modulation, and oxygen‐vacancy formation, which modify the interfacial inversion‐symmetry breaking and consequently reshape the band structure. These findings establish an effective electrical route for controlling nonlinear planar Hall responses through ionic engineering of spin texture in momentum space and provide a promising platform for reconfigurable nonlinear spintronic applications.
n493f38de36be: Photocatalytic methanol reforming affords a sustainable route for the synergistic production of hydrogen and high‐value formaldehyde; however, the atomic‐scale orbital interactions that fundamentally govern interfacial charge transfer and substrate activation remain a critical challenge. Herein, we overcome this challenge by developing a gradient 5s–3p–6p (Cd 5s–S 3p–Bi 6p) orbital coupling strategy via in situ epitaxial growth of Bi2S3 on CdS (BS/CdS‐H). This orbital coupling is defined as the gradient hybridization of Cd 5s, S 3p, and Bi 6p orbitals across the epitaxial interface, forming a continuous orbital network that creates a directional electron migration channel and tailors the Cd 5s orbital occupancy. Consequently, it simultaneously promotes interfacial charge separation and modulates Cd 5s–O 2p hybridization, which primarily facilitates O–H dissociation and thereby modulates the kinetic barrier for the subsequent C–H bond cleavage toward HCHO formation. The BS/CdS‐H heterojunction delivers exceptional H2 and HCHO co‐production rates of 5111.7 and 4630.0 µmol g−1, representing 47.2‐ and 72.8‐fold enhancements over pristine CdS. This work establishes atomic‐scale orbital coupling as a predictive design principle that transcends conventional band‐alignment paradigms, offering a versatile orbital‐engineering framework for rational development of high‐efficiency solar fuel co‐conversion systems.
n44239e9b834c: Next‐generation soft robotics and shape‐morphing electronics demand materials that possess intrinsic softness yet processable into freeform 3D architectures. However, direct‐write 3D printing of soft elastomers suffers from a rheological trade‐off, where high yield stress required for printability increases stiffness. This work presents a ternary silicone elastomer ink that breaks this limitation by incorporating liquid metal (LM) as a Newtonian liquid filler. The fluidic LM droplets act as stress buffers, accelerating stress relaxation during flow without compromising post‐curing compliance. Additionally, they induce an excluded‐volume effect that increases the effective local concentration of the dispersed multi‐walled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs), thereby enhancing the percolating conductive network. This strategy enables support‐free 3D printing, achieving maximum bridging spans of 32 mm and a peak resolution of 124 µm independently. The composite exhibits high stretchability (446% elongation), a bulk conductivity of 7.08 S/m, and electrical stability under large deformation (∆R/R0 = 0.51 at 100% strain). The versatility of this platform was further validated through reconfigurable 3D circuits, demonstrating that in addition to functioning as compliant conductors, the printed structures can also serve as robust load‐bearing structural elements. By reconciling printability, softness, and deformation‐tolerant electrical conductivity, this work establishes a general approach for freeform 3D soft electronics.
ndf20f9a0df25: Deterministic assembly of microscale devices enables heterogeneous integration in advanced electronic, optoelectronic, and display systems. These applications require precise placement of components such as micro‐light‐emitting diodes (micro‐LEDs), thin‐film transistors, and sensors onto rigid or flexible receiving substrates. Transfer printing provides a scalable route for this alignment‐sensitive assembly, but lateral and rotational misalignment during manufacturing remain important limitations. Conventional elastomeric stamps based on poly(dimethylsiloxane) (PDMS) deform under contact loading, particularly in micropillar configurations, where pillar bending produces positional error and reduces transfer fidelity. Here, we introduce a skeleton‐reinforced hybrid PDMS micropillar stamp that suppresses deformation while retaining the compliant interface required for reliable pick‐up and release. Each pillar contains an embedded high‐modulus PDMS skeleton surrounded by soft PDMS at the periphery and contact surface. The internal skeleton constrains pillar deformation, while the compliant outer layer preserves conformal contact and interfacial adhesion. This architecture improves dimensional stability during compression and reduces sliding of supported microscale devices on receiving substrates. The hybrid stamp therefore provides a scalable strategy for precision transfer printing in high‐resolution displays, flexible electronic systems, and heterogeneous microsystems.
na2a2473a5988: Topotactic phase‐transition (TPT) oxide memristors contain ordered 1D oxygen‐vacancy channels (OVCs) that enable anisotropic oxygen‐ion migration and reversible brownmillerite/perovskite transition, offering a materials platform for neuromorphic computing. However, the lack of spatially predefined oxygen‐ion migration sites in conventional TPT films promotes stochastic perovskite SrFeO3 conductive filament (CF) growth, compromising the response stability and state distinguishability required for reliable temporal signal processing. Here, a single‐component self‐assembled SrFeOx memristor with alternating vertical and horizontal superlattice‐like OVC regions is reported. Structural characterization, density functional theory calculations, and kinetic Monte Carlo simulations indicate that this intrinsic self‐assembled architecture directs oxygen‐ion migration through vertical channels while horizontal regions restrict stray out‐of‐plane transport, promoting localized CF growth. The device combines forming‐free bipolar switching, an ON/OFF ratio of ∼4.4 × 103, low cycle‐to‐cycle (C2C) variation with CV(VSET)/CV(VRESET) of 3.2%/0.6%, 16‐state retention over 104 s, and endurance up to 107 pulse cycles. Reproducible device‐to‐device (D2D) switching is obtained across 32 cells, with D2D CV(VSET)/CV(VRESET) values of 10.1%/5.9%. Finally, the device's short‐term memory transforms temporal inputs into distinguishable states that a fixed linear readout decodes with 84.59% accuracy on a temporal classification task. This work highlights intrinsic OVC‐orientation engineering as a materials‐level strategy toward reliable single‐component TPT memristors.
n99e7b94e9689: Attracted by short‐process and uniform regenerated properties, oxidation‐homogenization then reduction‐reconstruction of spent LiFePO4 (SLFP) has been successfully industrialized. Two types of SLFP exist: production scrap and cycled retired battery materials. Nevertheless, these treatments enable efficient regeneration of the former, yet fail to restore the latter effectively, always with unsatisfactory energy‐storage properties. From our experience, the introduced mechanochemical behaviors (MCB) would induce the tailoring of their properties. Herein, through the controlling of MCB, the evolution of physical‐chemical properties is revealed during the full‐loop process. MCB would induce the exposure of the metastable Li1−xFePO4 transition region. Clearly, along with the competition of carbon and O2, they were transformed into Fe3(PO4)2 intermediate coated with a dense Fe2O3 layer, bringing about the uneven carbon layers and lattice stress distribution. By replacing ball milling with jet milling, excessive mechanical stress is avoided. The as‐optimized sample deliver a capacity of 148.2 mAh g−1 after 200 cycles at 1.0 C and 108.4 mAh g−1 after 1000 cycles at 5.0 C. Furthermore, kg‐scale experiments are conducted to prove the practical reliability of recycling manners. Thus, this work is expected to elucidate the full‐loop regeneration mechanism of cycled retired battery materials, meanwhile providing the significant treatment strategy for practical industry production.
n16987ad5ee55: Lithium dendrite formation in solid‐state lithium metal batteries originates not only from mechanical failure but also from spatially heterogeneous interfacial electrostatic fields that induce localized Li+ accumulation. However, existing electrolyte designs mainly regulate mechanical strength or chemical interfacial reactions, while dynamic regulation of interfacial electrostatic disorder remains unexplored. Here, we introduce an interfacial potential homogenization enabled by polarization‐mediated regulation. A molecularly entangled PEO/polyurethane/MOF‐177 electrolyte is constructed, where polar polymer networks and MOF polarization domains cooperatively redistribute local electric‐field fluctuations. This electrostatic regulation homogenizes Li+ flux, lowers migration barriers, and suppresses preferential lithium nucleation. Consequently, CPEZ exhibits an ionic conductivity of 1.9 × 10−3 S cm−1 and a Li+ transference number of 0.71, both measured at 60°C. The Li/CPEZ/Li cell cycles stably for 9000 h at 0.1 mAh cm−2. The Li/CPEZ/LFP retains 90 % capacity after 5000 at 1 C, while Li/CPEZ/LFP retains 85% capacity after 500 cycles at 100°C and cycles stably for 150 cycles at −15°C. This work establishes electrostatic regulation via polar interactions as a transferable design principle for durable, wide‐temperature solid‐state lithium metal batteries.
n413a7c8a491b: Multilayer stretchable electronics with vertically integrated architectures and intrinsic conformability enable system‐level functionality and alleviate the mechanical mismatch between rigid silicon‐based electronics and curvilinear surfaces, holding promise for multimodal sensing, on‐board computing, closed‐loop feedback, and wireless communication under large‐scale deformation. However, the intricate mechanical‐electrical design required for heterogeneous vertical integration introduces coupled challenges in molecular engineering, interfacial reliability, structural topology, and scalable manufacturing. This review presents a synergistic technological framework for multilayer stretchable electronics from molecular engineering to system integration, based on a comprehensive summary of advances in material development, topological design, manufacturing technologies, and application expansion. In particular, key interface‐engineering strategies are examined, including the regulation of thermodynamic compatibility, the design of dynamic self‐healing interfaces, the optimization of interlayer mechano‐electrical coupling, and manufacturing approaches for heterogeneous integration. Finally, unresolved challenges and future directions are discussed, including sustainable materials, advanced manufacturing techniques, and artificial intelligence integration. This review aims to provide a systematic theoretical and methodological reference for next‐generation high‐performance multilayer stretchable electronic systems.
n0a8794982c60: Rechargeable Na-Cl2 batteries have emerged as a promising alternative and supplement for lithium-ion batteries due to their ultra-high energy density. Nevertheless, developing satisfactory cathode materials to facilitate the complex solid, liquid, and gas three-phase conversion process during charge-discharge cycling remains a significant challenge. Herein, we propose a three-dimensional ordered macroporous Prussian blue analog (3DOM PBA) fabricated via a stepwise vacuum impregnation template strategy, which can serve as an ideal cathode material for rechargeable Na-Cl2 batteries. The hierarchically ordered porous structure arranging from micropores to macropores can provide appropriated channels for ions transfer, Cl2 storage, and NaCl crystal deposition. Moreover, customizable metal site doping not only optimize the electronic and ionic conductivity but also provide efficient adsorption and in-situ catalytic conversion sites for Cl2/Cl − , thereby effectively increasing the reversible reaction kinetics and long-term cycling stability. As a result, the assembled Na-Cl2 battery delivers a reversible capacity of 2000 mAh g − 1 and stable cycling life of 2500 cycles at 15 000 mA g − 1, which can still maintain reversible charge-discharge behavior even at 30 000 mA g − 1, much superior to the reported results. This study provides new insights for developing high-performance electrode materials for rechargeable Na-Cl2 batteries.
nb0b8df01f6e8: Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) have emerged as promising power sources for self-powered human-machine interfaces (HMIs). However, self-powered sensing interfacing with the human body requires matching with the low-elasticity human skin, as well as high-efficiency energy production in response to skin interface compliance and minute skin movements. Here, we present a skin-matched self-powered HMI based on a ferroelectric three-dimensional porous triboelectric interface (f-3PT). The interconnected porous microarchitecture redistributes mechanical stress to achieve an ultralow Young's modulus (<20 kPa), enabling compliance with diverse minute skin deformations. The ultracompliant porous framework undergoes localized deformation under subtle mechanical stimuli, while uniformly dispersed ferroelectric fillers enhance dielectric permittivity and polarization. This structural-material synergy maximizes triboelectric charge generation, achieving a power density of ∼140 mW m− 2 under an ultralow preload (<0.2 N). Furthermore, integration with a bioinspired adhesive interface and an orthogonal stretchable wrinkle electrode preserves a skin-level effective modulus (≈80 kPa) for the fully integrated device while simultaneously providing robust skin adhesion, high breathability, and stable operation under elevated-temperature and underwater conditions. The resulting platform enables reliable biomechanical sensing and energy harvesting from subtle human motions, offering a general design strategy for next-generation skin-matched self-powered skin electronics.
n41f0bb639e16: High‐capacity optical multiplexing is crucial for next‐generation intelligent information systems, spanning high‐speed communications, optical computing, and immersive displays. A fundamental challenge is to maximize the number of independent channels while maintaining high fidelity, compact footprint, and low structural complexity, constraints that severely limit existing diffractive optical elements. Here, we overcome these long‐standing trade‐offs by introducing a multi‐dimensional reconfigurable diffractive neural network (MRDNN) that enables high‐capacity, high‐fidelity optical multiplexing within an exceptionally compact and simple architecture through the co‐design of predictive neural optimization and multi‐physical‐dimension multiplexing. Experimentally, a dual‐layer MRDNN realizes 24 independent channels for distinct functionalities, including focusing, beam steering, and holographic image reconstruction. Owing to its excellent scalability, only four metasurface layers comprising a minimal library of 2002 meta‐atoms achieve 120 distinct optical channels with low crosstalk and high fidelity (measured mean structural similarity index measure of over 0.8), representing a record experimental multiplexing capacity with one of the smallest normalized footprints and simplest structural configurations in a metasurface‐enabled system. This work establishes a scalable and efficient paradigm for extreme optical multiplexing in multifunctional and reconfigurable photonics systems.
n6f4008eead9e: Electrocatalytic ammonia oxidation reaction (AOR) offers a green route to nitrite (NO2 −) synthesis while coupling hydrogen evolution reaction. However, maintaining NO2 − selectivity at high current density remains challenging due to the narrow thermodynamic windows for NO2 − and nitrate (NO3 −) formation and competition of oxygen evolution reaction at high anodic potentials. Herein, we report a Cu2S/NiOOH heterojunction that sustains high NO2 − selectivity over a wide oxidative window at industrially relevant current densities. Operando Raman spectroscopy, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations reveal that the heterointerface induces interfacial electronic redistribution within the Ni–O framework, strengthens NH3 adsorption, and rebalances AOR energetics, favoring NO2 − release over oxidation. Consequently, in a membrane electrode assembly-based flow cell, Cu2S/NiOOH delivers a Faradaic efficiency for NO2 − (FE(NO2 −)) exceeding 90% at 800 mA cm− 2 with a high production rate of 383.2 mg cm−2 h−1. These results highlight the potential of Cu2S/NiOOH for NO2 − electrosynthesis at industrial production rate.
nc257691975f8: Physical reservoir computing (PRC) has emerged as a highly energy‐efficient paradigm for processing high‐dimensional spatiotemporal data in edge‐intelligent systems. However, the deployment of PRC is often limited by the quantization mismatch between continuous input signals and the finite dynamic range of hardware substrates. Conventional binary time‐multiplexing ensures high noise immunity but necessitates protracted pulse sequences that induce high latency and premature physical saturation. Conversely, multi‐valued analog encoding enhances information density but frequently induces state overlap, operating devoid of physical quantization boundaries. To resolve this physical‐information trade‐off, we propose a saturation‐constrained information capacity (SCIC) framework. This framework considers task‐specific encoding variables and substrate‐intrinsic constraints, enabling device‐informed optimization of input mapping. We experimentally demonstrate this framework on a highly uniform, selector‐free 32 × 32 crossbar array, utilizing the volatile dynamics of memristors. Under the experimentally selected encoding conditions, the SCIC‐guided RC achieves exceptional performance in temporal prediction (NRMSE of 0.019), speech recognition (free‐spoken digit dataset (FSDD) subset accuracy of ∼94.5%), and real‐time obstacle avoidance. Our approach links encoding constraints to solid‐state device physics, providing a device‐informed method for PRC parameterization at the edge.
n9ed377baf34e: Achieving effective and economical hemostats requires a robust clot‐wound interface constructed by spatiotemporally coordinated coagulation. However, accumulated interfacial blood causes delayed clotting in adhesion‐reliant dense hemostats, and rapid but off‐site coagulation in absorptive porous materials. Here, we present MAGIC (Micromesh‐At‐Grid Integrated Cotton) gauze, which leverages a reversible transition between dense and porous states to precisely coordinate the spatial and temporal dynamics of coagulation. This transition is achieved by a pressure‐responsive micromesh composed of supramolecular procoagulant microparticles. Spatially, blood‐derived ions trigger the gelation of these procoagulant particles on the gauze surface, laterally repelling interfacial blood to ensure on‐site coagulation. Temporally, applied pressure induces micromesh dissociation to re‐expose the gauze macropores for wicking residual fluid, followed by the rapid co‐assembly of sol‐state procoagulant particles with blood components. This tightly synchronized process seals the cleared wound with a robust clot. Consequently, a single MAGIC pad arrested lethal porcine femoral artery hemorrhage within 30 s. Compared to standard gauze, it reduced blood loss by 98%, cotton consumption by 96%, treatment costs by 83%, and lifecycle CO2 emissions by 84%. Collectively, MAGIC gauze delivers exceptional preclinical first aid efficacy while pioneering a viable pathway for the decarbonization of surgical consumables.
n26215435948b: Ultrasound (US)‐triggered sonodynamic therapy (SDT) combined with immunotherapy shows considerable promise, yet its therapeutic efficacy remains constrained by insufficient intratumoral drug activation and limited immunogenicity. Herein, we report a self‐amplifying US‐responsive nanoplatform (PMB@R848) for synergistic sonodynamic immunotherapy. The nanotherapeutic was constructed by conjugating the sonosensitizer methylene blue (MB) to polylysine through US‐labile urea‐based linkages, providing a stable framework for efficient complexation of immunostimulant R848. Under physiological conditions, PMB@R848 exhibited excellent colloidal stability and biocompatibility. Upon US irradiation, the generated reactive oxygen species (ROS) initiated selective cleavage of urea bonds, exposing protonatable amino groups that enhanced intraparticle electrostatic repulsion under mildly acidic tumor microenvironment. This cascade process further accelerated nanoparticle destabilization and established a self‐amplified release behavior, enabling synchronized liberation of both MB and R848. The released MB markedly enhanced ROS generation, inducing robust immunogenic cell death and tumor antigen release, while R848 further amplified dendritic cell maturation and systemic antitumor immunity. Benefiting from the synergistic integration of self‐amplified SDT and immune activation, PMB@R848 achieved potent inhibition of primary tumors, effectively suppressed recurrence, and established durable immune memory in multiple murine tumor models. This work presents a self‐amplifying, US‐activatable nanoplatform for precision sonodynamic immunotherapy.
n15ffdb3f683f: The explosive advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) has driven vast amounts of unstructured data that directly emerges at sensory interaction interfaces. Memristors with superior computing ability are among the most promising computing blocks. However, conventional vertical Metal/Resistive layer/Metal (V‐MRM) memristors tend to generate intense electric fields, suffer from limited sensory response, inflexible, and rigid functional modes, as well as long‐standing variability and overshoot issues. Here, we present an unconventional two‐terminal quasi‐vertical (QV) van der Waals heterostructure (vdWH) memristor as opto‐reconfigurable hardware. Unlike the V‐MRM memristor with a strong, rigid vertical electric field, this QV‐vdWH memristor realizes a significantly softened, tunable electric field, enabling parametric configurable and wavelength‐dependent reconfigurable modes across nonvolatile/volatile memory, neurons, synapses, and optical perception. Moreover, the light‐memristive switching‐vdWH coupling triggers a super‐additive synergistic enhancement of memristive performance (> 100‐fold) and photoresponse (> 3000‐fold). Meanwhile, the long‐standing variability and overshoot issues are overcome, yielding ultra‐uniform memristive behavior with even a single‐valued distribution. Leveraging the opto‐reconfigurability, high‐accuracy object tracking, and human motion recognition (∼96.8%) are successfully performed. Breaking through the inherent functional limitation of the conventional V‐MRM memristive structure, the QV‐vdWH memristor provides a flexible, opto‐reconfigurable hardware platform for emerging computing paradigms, and AI applications.
ne5f1e113778e: Diamondoid Cu3SbSe4 is an earth‐abundant thermoelectric material with strong potential for near‐room to mid‐temperature applications. However, its performance has been limited by intrinsically low carrier mobility. Here, we report the first successful growth of large‐sized Cu3SbSe4 crystals, achieving a fivefold enhancement in carrier mobility, and demonstrate the first Cu3SbSe4‐based thermoelectric cooling device. We show that Ag substitution reduces both the effective mass and deformation potential through strengthened bond covalency, yielding a high carrier mobility of ∼150 cm2 V−1 s−1. This leads to a remarkable power factor of ∼23 µW cm−1 K−2 at 300 K, a maximum ZT of ∼1.6 at 700 K and an average ZT of ∼0.85 over 300–700 K, representing state‐of‐the‐art performance among Cu‐based thermoelectric materials in this temperature range. A 7‐pair device based on Cu3SbSe4 crystal achieves a cooling temperature difference of ∼25 K at room temperature, and reaching a maximum of ∼34 K at 343 K. Additionally, the optimized sample demonstrates a single‐leg power‐generation efficiency of ∼7% at ΔT = 350 K. These results highlight crystal‐growth as a powerful strategy to unlock high‐performance refrigeration in previously limited materials, establishing diamondoid Cu3SbSe4 crystals as a viable, low‐cost and environmentally benign platform for practical thermoelectric applications.
nfdbdab68904a: Periodontitis, the sixth most prevalent global disease, causes tooth loss and systemic disorders, imposing a significant global burden. Functional regeneration of the periodontium remains a major challenge due to the hierarchical soft‐hard tissue interface and complex spatiotemporal functional demands. In this study, a synchronously in situ co‐injectable, interlayer‐bonding, and wet‐adhesive bilayer hydrogel (Bio‐Fun bilayer) consisting of PCAC and PCMC layers is developed. An anti‐delamination interface is engineered via polymer chain topological entanglement and dynamic boronate ester and ionic networks, while precise complex viscosity matching enables synchronized microscale laminar co‐extrusion. Concurrently, the hydrogel maintains wet adhesion, especially to moist root and bone surfaces. Spatiotemporal biofunctionalization is achieved by loading microRNA‐26a liposomes in the PCAC layer to activate Wnt/β‐catenin signaling for osteogenesis, and covalently tethering a PDGF‐BB mimetic peptide within the PCMC layer to trigger PI3K/Akt‐LOX signaling for fibroblast recruitment and functional collagen formation. In vivo, the Bio‐Fun bilayer hydrogel achieves integrated regeneration of alveolar bone and aligned periodontal ligament fibers, forming Sharpey's fiber‐like structures with firm bone‐ligament attachment. Meanwhile, the modular and injectable design might provide broad reference for the reconstruction of periodontal, osteochondral, and other soft‐hard tissue interfaces.
n4cd242b40c4c: Wound infections represent a major clinical concern due to their high incidence and subtle early manifestations, often resulting in prolonged healing and increased risk of complications. While wearable bioelectronics facilitate real‐time diagnostics and therapeutic interventions, their widespread clinical translation remains constrained by the complexity, power demands, and high cost of current systems. Here, a wearable platform that integrates colorimetric sensors with a wireless optoelectronic microneedle patch was presented for in situ wound infection status detection and on‐demand photodynamic therapy (PDT). This wireless colorimetric optoelectronic microneedle (COMN) patch enables rapid (15 min) and reliable detection of typical wound infection biomarkers with minor interference. By integrating microneedles and wireless light‐emitting diodes (LEDs), this system supports concurrent delivery of photosensitizers and light into deeper wound tissues, achieving > 99.9% eradication of drug‐resistant bacteria through penetration‐enhanced PDT. In a murine full‐thickness wound infection model, this system promptly assessed the infection status of the wound and then triggered PDT, resulting in > 3 log reduction in bacterial burden and accelerated healing, with > 80% wound closure observed by day 14. This work demonstrates a flexible and adaptive bioelectronic platform based on colorimetric analysis and optoelectronic microneedle therapy, offering an accessible strategy for precision wound care.
nf1e7304c8b96: Solid‐state metal hydrides offer high volumetric hydrogen density and intrinsic safety for hydrogen storage, yet their practical application is severely hindered by poor room‐temperature thermodynamics, sluggish kinetics, impurity gas poisoning, difficult activation, and cycling degradation. Multi‐principal element alloys (MPEAs) have recently emerged as promising candidates to overcome these bottlenecks through their vast compositional space, severe lattice distortion, and synergistic cocktail effect. This review systematically summarizes recent advances in MPEAs for solid‐state hydrogen storage, bridging atomic‐scale design to system‐level performance. A unified composition‐process‐structure‐property framework is established that integrates engineering‐driven design rules, post‐processing techniques, multi‐scale computations, machine learning (ML), and high‐throughput experiments. Using advanced in situ and ex situ characterization, the atomic‐scale origins and cross‐scale evolution of surface poisoning, hydrogen‐induced amorphization (HIA), disproportionation, pulverization, and defect accumulation. A theoretical framework linking electronic structure to heat and mass transport is further developed, and hydrogen storage bed design, device integration, fuel‐cell coupling, manufacturing scalability, and cost analysis are discussed. Finally, key scientific and engineering challenges and future research directions are outlined. This review provides scientific guidance for designing MPEA‐based solid‐state hydrogen storage systems with high capacity, long cycle life, high poisoning tolerance, fast de‐/hydrogenation kinetics, and low cost.
n32750dd51e1c: Electrocatalytic reactions occur at a dynamic, ion‐regulated electrochemical interface, rather than at a static electrode boundary. In electrocatalytic processes such as hydrogen evolution/oxidation and CO2 reduction, which operate at potentials below the electrode's potential of zero charge, electrolyte cations are not mere spectators but active participants that shape reaction behavior. Their size, charge density, solvation structure, and spatial organization within the electric double layer (EDL) govern interfacial energetics, transition states, and reaction activity and selectivity, giving rise to pronounced, system‐dependent cation effects. Furthermore, cation accumulation dynamically modifies the interfacial electric field, reorganizes water structure, and alters local pH, thereby coupling electrostatics, solvation, and mass transport in a highly nonlinear manner. These intertwined effects complicate mechanistic interpretation and have contributed to ongoing debates and seemingly contradictory conclusions across experimental and theoretical studies. Here, we synthesize the current understanding of cation effects at electrochemical interfaces, highlight emerging interfacial molecular structures revealed by in situ and operando studies that challenge classical EDL models, identify key unresolved debates, and outline pathways toward a quantitative, molecular‐level description of cation–interface–reactivity relationships.
n04110bd9915f: Electrocatalytic seawater hydrogen evolution is fundamentally limited by the rigidity of interfacial water structures and static electron distributions at catalyst surfaces. Here, we report a bias‐responsive S‐scheme heterojunction that dynamically couples nonequilibrium electron redistribution with interfacial water activation during operation. Using a MoN/NiCoN model system, in situ x‐ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) reveals a cathodic‐bias‐induced reversal of interfacial electron transfer relative to the equilibrium state, leading to progressive electron enrichment at the catalytic interface. In situ infrared spectroscopy reveals potential‐dependent restructuring of the interfacial water environment associated with this electronic redistribution, transforming strongly and intermediately hydrogen‐bonded water into catalytically active free or weakly hydrogen‐bonded species. Ab initio molecular dynamics simulations further reveal accelerated hydrogen‐bond exchange kinetics, shortened hydrogen‐bond lifetimes, and a more adaptive dipole orientation at the MoN/NiCoN interface, providing molecular‐level evidence for dynamic water‐network reorganization. Ionic‐liquid‐based experiments further demonstrate that this restructuring originates from electronically driven interfacial activation rather than bulk water availability. Consequently, water dissociation and hydrogen evolution kinetics are synergistically accelerated, enabling ultralow overpotentials in real seawater and high solar‐to‐hydrogen (STH) conversion efficiency. This work establishes dynamic S‐scheme heterojunctions as a general strategy for electronically programmable interfacial reaction environments in electrocatalysis.
nc4c24af78598: High‐temperature proton exchange membrane fuel cells (HT‐PEMFCs) offer compelling advantages for energy conversion, including simplified water and thermal management and high tolerance to fuel impurities. In these systems, phosphoric acid (PA) serves as the primary proton conductor, enabling anhydrous proton transport. However, cathode performance and durability remain constrained by sluggish oxygen reduction kinetics and the challenge of controlling PA distribution and retention. Uneven acid distribution, manifesting as local flooding that blocks gas pathways and covers active sites or local depletion that disrupts proton‐conducting networks, causes severe mass‐transport losses and performance decay. Concurrently, gradual PA migration and loss during operation progressively degrade proton conduction pathways, accelerating voltage decay. Recent studies have established cathode binder engineering as an effective strategy to regulate both PA distribution and retention. This review systematically examines the design of cathode binder systems—encompassing polymer binder optimization and functional additive integration—and the characterization and diagnostic frameworks for evaluating their efficacy in PA management. We further integrate advanced PA characterization techniques with a comprehensive electrochemical performance evaluation framework. By establishing explicit connections among binder design, PA distribution and retention behavior, and device‐level performance assessment, this review provides an instructive guide for the rational development of high‐performance, durable HT‐PEMFC cathodes.
n190ad3cf54e0: Aqueous zinc–iodine (Zn─I2) batteries are attractive for large‐scale energy storage yet remain limited by two coupled failure mechanisms: unstable zinc interface at the anode and polyiodide shuttling at the cathode. To address both challenges with a single additive, we systematically screened 44 amino acids and dipeptides using molecular dipole moment and LUMO energy as key descriptors. L‐Carnosine (LC) emerged as a unique candidate exhibiting both the highest dipole moment and a moderate LUMO energy across the screened library. Experimentally, LC's zwitterionic, multicenter charge distribution drives persistent multidentate adsorption at the zinc interface, suppressing HER, directing (101)‐oriented crystallographic deposition through facet‐selective passivation, and enabling formation of a vertically graded organic‐inorganic hybrid solid electrolyte interphase. Concurrently, the electron‐rich imidazole group rapidly quenches polyiodide intermediates through a rapid redox reaction. This synergistic regulation enables Zn||Zn symmetric cells to operate stably for 4980 h, Zn||Cu cells to achieve 99.76% average Coulombic efficiency (CE) over 1400 cycles, and Zn||I2 full cells to sustain over 18 000 cycles with nearly 100% capacity retention. Furthermore, the practical viability is demonstrated in Ah‐level pouch cells with 85% capacity retention after 500 cycles. This work establishes a unique molecular transformation strategy for stabilizing high‐energy aqueous energy systems.
n6cd95c8b5031: Protective materials for harsh environments should dissipate transient impact energy while maintaining mechanical reliability under thermal fluctuations.
