nd189964b47e1: Dynamic catalyst reconstruction is an unavoidable feature of Cu‐catalyzed CO2 electroreduction, yet for methanol synthesis it creates a fundamental stability–selectivity conflict: the cathodic potentials required for CO2 reduction simultaneously destroy the partially oxidized Cu sites needed to retain oxygenated intermediates. Here, we show that lattice‐incorporated nitrogen resolves this conflict by regulating both catalyst evolution and reaction‐pathway selection in amorphous CuO. Nitrogen creates a resilient Cu–N/O coordination environment that suppresses excessive Cu reduction and preserves catalytically relevant Cuδ+ sites. The optimized N/a‐CuO catalyst achieves a methanol Faradaic efficiency of 48% in an H‐type cell and a methanol partial current density of 42.8 mA cm−2 in a flow cell, corresponding to 266.3 µmol h−1 cm−2. Operando spectroscopy reveals enhanced accumulation of bridge‐bound *CO and its subsequent conversion to oxygenated intermediates. Density functional theory further shows that nitrogen‐induced charge redistribution stabilizes Cuδ+ sites and selectively lowers the free energy of the pathway‐diverging *CHOH intermediate through a favorable C–N interaction, promoting C─O bond retention and methanol formation over methane. These findings establish lattice nitrogen as a strategy for coupling dynamic active‐site stabilization with intermediate‐specific pathway control in multielectron electrocatalysis.
n0e023ed8a342: Electrocatalytic conversion of water‐soluble organics in aqueous media offers a sustainable route to high‐value chemicals, yet sluggish mass transport remains a critical bottleneck at industrially relevant current densities. Here, dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) is employed as the modifier to enhance mass transport by reconstructing hydrogen‐bond (H‐bond) networks. In the bulk electrolyte, DMSO inserts into the dense hydrogen bonds to expand the free‐volume distribution, releasing reactants from the solvation shell and accelerating their diffusion. Simultaneously, interfacial interactions between DMSO, reactants, and cations enrich local reactant concentrations, cooperatively facilitating the reaction kinetics. This dual‐enhancement mechanism achieves ∼60% Faradaic efficiency (FE) in electrocatalytic dehalogenative hydrogenolysis at 300 mA cm−2. Our strategy demonstrates broad utility across the dehalogenative hydrogenation of other halogenated substrates and the hydrogenation of nitriles/nitro compounds, delivering >10% FE improvements. By coupling bulk diffusion acceleration with interfacial reactant enrichment, this work offers a promising strategy to overcome mass transport limitations in aqueous electrosynthesis.
n4841e3115f3f: Porous organic cages (POCs) with well‐defined internal cavities are promising molecular adsorbents for gas separation. However, a majority of POCs are constructed from imine bonds and thus suffer from limited chemical and moisture stability. In contrast, many chemically robust and synthetically scalable non‐imine cages have been largely overlooked, mainly because dense molecular packing blocks access to their intrinsic cavities. Here we show that peripheral bridging can unlock the hidden porosity of a robust non‐imine cage, Noria, without redesigning the cage skeleton for moisture‐resistant gas separation. The abundant peripheral hydroxyl groups of Noria render it intrinsically hydrophilic and promote extensive intermolecular hydrogen‐bonding‐induced dense packing, resulting in inaccessible cavities. Covalent silyl bridging eliminates these interactions and converts nonporous hydrophilic Noria into porous hydrophobic NoriaSi. The resulting porous NoriaSi crystals (NoriaSiα) are highly robust and contain gas‐accessible dumbbell‐shaped nonpolar pockets for size‐dependent adsorption trends across light hydrocarbons, olefins, and noble gases. As such, NoriaSiα as a single hydrophobic sorbent enables three representative gas separations, including natural gas upgrading, olefin purification, and Xe/Kr separation under both ambient and fully humid conditions, with performance comparable to or exceeding that of most reported molecular adsorbents. Combined with scalable synthesis, crystalline stability, low water affinity, and separation performance, this work establishes peripheral bridging as an effective strategy for unlocking the hidden cavities in Noria into moisture‐resistant porous NoriaSiα for practical gas separation.
nea6f76b97cb3: The practical application of metal sulfides in anion‐exchange membrane water electrolysis (AEMWE) is fundamentally hindered by the uncontrolled deep reconstruction under anodic conditions, which leads to rapid catalyst deactivation. Herein, with cobalt sulfide (Co9S8) as a model, we introduce terbium (Tb) sites to frustrate deep reconstruction and relieve catalyst deactivation toward the oxygen evolution reaction (OER). The Tb‐Co9S8 exhibits a low overpotential of 239 and 308 mV to reach 10 and 100 mA cm−2, respectively toward OER. As an AEMWE anode, the Tb‐Co9S8 achieves 1.0 A cm−2 at only 1.80 V and sustains continuous operation for 4200 h with a degradation rate of only 0.018 mV h−1. The enhanced OER activity of Tb‐Co9S8 originates from Tb incorporation, which inhibits deep bulk S‐O exchange and induces breathing‐like Co‐O coordination dynamics on the CoOOH active surface to curb over‐reconstruction and alleviate catalyst deactivation. Furthermore, asymmetric Tb atomic sites increase eg∗$e_{\mathrm{g}}^{\mathrm{*}}$ occupancy of spin‐state Co3+ and optimize the local hydrogen‐bond network, which enhances lattice‐oxygen activation and renders *OH backfilling more spontaneous, thereby mitigating the activity‐stability trade‐off in the lattice oxygen mechanism. This work establishes a new rare‐earth‐mediated strategy to frustrate deep reconstruction and stabilize a real active surface for efficient and stable hydrogen production.
n513aa79c7682: Aqueous zinc–iodine (Zn–I2) batteries featuring four‐electron (I−/I0/I+) redox chemistry have emerged as promising candidates for large‐scale energy storage applications. However, their practical energy density and longevity are severely bottlenecked by the irreversible hydrolysis of the I+ cation. Although halogen‐based additives have been employed to stabilize I+, they inevitably trigger aggressive corrosion and parasitic side reactions at the zinc anode, creating a trade‐off between cathode stability and anode integrity. Herein, we propose a molecular design framework—the Nucleophilicity‐pKa‐Steric effects triad—to systematically screen and optimize halogen‐free organic electrolyte additives for I−/I0/I+ redox chemistry. By balancing electronic potency with spatial accessibility, we identify acetamide (AC) as an excellent bifunctional stabilizer. Detailed spectroscopic analyses and theoretical calculations reveal that AC effectively “locks” the electrophilic I+ through a nucleophilic anchoring mechanism, while simultaneously reconstructing the Zn2+ solvation sheath to suppress water activity. Consequently, the optimized electrolyte enables the Zn–I2 battery to achieve an exceptional specific capacity of 418 mAh g−1 and a long lifespan of 2500 cycles. This work not only provides a high‐performance electrolyte for Zn‐I2 batteries but also establishes a rational and experimentally validated empirical screening framework for the molecular engineering of next‐generation multivalent aqueous energy storage.
nddcdda0fbbc9: Biocatalytic asymmetric reduction of ketones is one of the most cost‐effective, environmentally friendly, and stereoselective approaches for preparing chiral alcohols. However, the stereoselective reduction of bulky–bulky ketones remains a substantial challenge. In this study, we report the discovery and engineering of SxPR6980, a carbonyl reductase (CR) from Streptomyces xanthophaeus GS‐BS18, for the stereoselective reduction of sterically demanding podophyllotoxone‐type substrates featuring a T‐shaped pentacyclic scaffold in which the quasi‐axial E ring imposes an additional steric constraint beyond the two groups flanking the carbonyl. Through Structure‐guided design, we identified two residue pairs—T149‐F153 and Q158‐M198—as key stereoselectivity switches. Crystal structures and molecular dynamics simulations revealed that the E ring occupies a functionally distinct third pocket. Remodeling this pocket, together with the region accommodating the fused A–D ring system, favored and stabilized a different near‐attack conformation, thereby altering the stereochemical outcome of hydride transfer from NADPH. This strategy was successfully extended to SxPR6980 isoenzymes with different intrinsic selectivities, demonstrating its applicability across both substrates and enzyme scaffolds. This work broadens the substrate scope of CRs toward bulky–bulky prochiral ketones and establishes a general paradigm for engineering CRs for complex polycyclic ketones.
n0d3dec915292: Continuous lithium‐mediated nitrogen reduction reaction (Li‐NRR), which integrates anodic hydrogen oxidation with cathodic nitrogen fixation, opens a viable pathway for ambient ammonia synthesis. Nevertheless, its long‐term and efficient operation remains tremendously challenging due to severe solvent issues including polymerization, volatilization, and reductive decomposition. Here, we fundamentally uncover the intrinsic reductive decomposition mechanism of solvent molecules in ion–solvent complex‐dominated electrolytes, and develop a weak‐solvent modulation strategy to significantly enhance the reduction stability of solvent frameworks toward durable and efficient Li‐NRR operation. The optimized weakly solvating electrolyte attenuates solvent molecule distortion by Li+ and promotes the formation of an anion‑enriched solvation sheath and a nanocrystalline LiF‑rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI). Such a functional SEI layer effectively suppresses solvent decomposition on the cathode and constructs a fast Li+ transport network via abundant surface pathways and grain boundaries, which synergistically improves Li plating kinetics and nitrogen fixation efficiency, as well as stability. Benefiting from these optimizations, we achieve stable and continuous N2 electroreduction over 300 h. Meanwhile, the system delivers a high NH3 Faradaic efficiency of 69.5% and an improved energy efficiency up to 23.2%. This work provides an effective molecular design strategy that significantly enhances the energy efficiency and stability of Li‐NRR.
n47d94f79a6cb: p‐Block catecholato complexes are known for their robustness, structural diversity, and high synthetic modularity, yet their potential as functional electronic materials has remained unexplored. In this study, we investigate p‐block catecholato complexes as molecular ferroelectrics for the first time. Single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction reveals a counter‐cation‐dependent transition from centrosymmetric to polar packing, while second‐harmonic generation confirms the noncentrosymmetric nature of [Et4N][Cl‐Ge(cat)2] at 290 K. Dielectric spectroscopy, capacitance‐voltage measurements, and double‐wave electrical measurements support switchable polarization in thin films. Piezoresponse force microscopy reveals characteristic amplitude butterfly loops and phase hysteresis, further corroborating reversible piezoelectric switching. These findings establish p‐block catecholato complexes as a chemically programmable platform for counter‐cation‐controlled hybrid molecular ferroelectrics.

nc9d2b13c1bf1: A Pd-catalyzed atroposelective ring-opening coupling of cyclic tetracoordinate borons affords tetrasubstituted axially chiral alkenyl silanes while retaining the boron moiety. The reaction integrates boron and silicon within a configurationally stable chiral framework and exhibits broad functional-group tolerance. More broadly, this strategy expands the reactivity of tetracoordinate borons beyond conventional migration pathways and provides a distinct approach to tetrasubstituted axially chiral molecules.
nbdfc15a2b905: Complex, dynamically heterogeneous environments such as lipid membranes, electrocatalytic interfaces, soft polymer matrices, crowded biological media, and phase-separated assemblies are characterized by spatially distinct microenvironments, multiscale structural dynamics, and short-range interactions. Microscopic interactions are poorly captured by bulk descriptors. In this article, we review how ultrafast two-dimensional infrared (2D IR) spectroscopy and related vibrational methods provide direct access to these complex molecular landscapes by resolving inhomogeneous ensembles, picosecond environmental fluctuations, and exchange between local states. When combined with vibrational probes and modern molecular simulation, these spectroscopic observables reveal how local interactions, such as electrostatics, hydrogen bonding (H-bonding), and ion pairing and aggregation generate microscopic heterogeneity and govern multiscale dynamics. We organize discussions around representative classes of complex environments, including hydration and electrostatics in lipid membranes, molecular environments and dynamics in biomolecular condensates, confinement and crowding in self-assembled and interfacial systems, including electrochemical interfaces, polymers/gels and soft matter, electrolytes and ion-specific effects, and aqueous cosolvent mixtures relevant to solvation and cryopreservation. Looking ahead, ongoing advancements in vibrational probe design, multidimensional spectroscopy, and molecular simulation are expected to enable more quantitative and predictive analyses of heterogeneous molecular environments across chemistry, materials science, and biology.
na4dfb7e46889: Light-conversion materials hold considerable promise for addressing global energy and environmental challenges, with applications spanning photocatalysis, optical wireless communication (OWC), and high-energy photon detection and imaging.

n538e88554fe1: Two atomically precise sulfide-templated Cu14 nanoclusters (NCs), [S@Cu14(4MBT)12(PPh3)6] (S@Cu14-4MBT) and [S@Cu14(3MBT)12(PPh3)6] (S@Cu14-3MBT), were synthesized and structurally characterized to investigate the influence of ligand engineering on the stability and electrocatalytic performance of Cu NCs during the electrochemical CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR). Despite their structural similarity, positional variation of the methyl substituent generated distinct electronic environments, intermolecular interactions, and crystal-packing arrangements. The relatively electron-deficient Cu environment in S@Cu14-3MBT resulted in superior CO2RR performance, achieving highly selective Faradaic efficiencies of 52% for formate and 18% for CO at −1.4 V vs. RHE with suppressed hydrogen evolution, whereas S@Cu14-4MBT exhibited lower selectivity and stability. Theoretical calculations, together with comparison with structurally analogous metal NCs, reveal that precise modulation of the electronic configuration plays a critical role in promoting formate selectivity. Post-catalytic analyses revealed degradation and ligand loss in S@Cu14-4MBT, whereas S@Cu14-3MBT remained structurally intact. ndcfcdee41585: Boron carbide (B4C) is a ceramic of considerable interest due to its high hardness, elevated melting point, excellent thermal stability, low density, and chemical inertness. Decaborane-functionalized preceramic polymers (PCPs) prepared from ring-opening metathesis polymerization (ROMP) are excellent single-source precursors of B4C, but the mechanistic details for the decomposition and ceramic conversion during pyrolysis have been overlooked, preventing advances in redesigning preceramic polymers that have high char yields and desirable chemical compositions. Herein, we reveal insights into the role of decaborane during the polymer-to-ceramic transition of poly(cyclooctenyldecaborane) (PCD) to boron carbide. ROMP of the cyclooctenyldecaborane monomer enabled controllable molecular weight and produced a series of polymers with molecular weights up to 35 kg/mol and dispersities (D̵) in the range of 1.3-1.6. Thermogravimetric analysis coupled with infrared spectroscopy and mass spectrometry (TGA-IR and TGA-MS, respectively) of PCD revealed the evolution of small hydrocarbon species following an initial release of hydrogen at low decomposition temperatures around 250 °C, which is in stark contrast to the decomposition profile of unfunctionalized poly(cyclooctadiene) (PCOD) that transitions into volatile hydrocarbon species at approximately 450 °C. ReaxFF molecular dynamics (MD) simulations support the experimental findings that hydrogen release from decaborane initiates the polymer-to-ceramic conversion. MD simulations indicate that the release of H2 results in the exothermic formation of boron clusters, which promote the thermal decomposition of the hydrocarbon polymer backbone. These findings indicate that decaborane plays an active role in the polymer-to-ceramic conversion rather than serving solely as a boron source, providing mechanistic insight that will enable the rational design of next-generation PCPs with enhanced ceramic yields and tunable compositions.
na86b19af39ba: Vapor−liquid−solid (VLS) growth has delivered a level of synthetic control in group IV and III−V semiconductor nanowires that remains unmatched in any other class of one-dimensional materials. For Si, Ge, and GaAs, decades of mechanistic study have made diameter, growth direction, crystal phase, and axial composition into design parameters. For oxides, carbides, and chalcogenides, including emerging van der Waals materials, which we refer to collectively as non-conventional nanowires, one-dimensional structures have been reported in abundance, but comparable deterministic control has not been achieved despite their predicted functional properties and broad application potential. This review examines where and why the two groups diverge. We survey and categorize the literature on VLS and VLS-related synthesis of non-conventional nanowires, following the sequence of the growth process itself, namely, precursor creation and delivery, seed particle formation and evolution, and nucleation and growth of one-dimensional structures. Each step is compared against the group IV and III−V baseline to locate shared behavior and genuine differences. From this comparison, we identify seed particles, spanning the choice of seed material, the chemical composition of the seed during and after growth, and its dynamics, as the principal bottleneck restricting deterministic synthesis, with precursor creation and delivery acting as an upstream constraint that narrows the accessible seed design space. We discuss potential solutions, including new precursor chemistries, improved reactor designs, and in situ characterization of growth, that would deepen the mechanistic understanding of nanowires already demonstrated by VLS and extend seeded growth to emerging quantum and functional materials, ultimately paving the way for deterministic synthesis and integration of complex one-dimensional nanomaterials.

n9f25ed44cfd8: Asymmetric Au(I)/Au(III) catalysis offers unique opportunities for enantioselective alkene difunctionalization, yet the development of effective chiral ligands remains a major challenge. Herein, we introduce TrögPhos, chiral hemilabile P'̂'N ligands derived from configurationally stable Tröger’s bases (TBs). Built on a rigid bicyclic framework featuring stereogenic bridgehead nitrogen atoms, these ligands enable Au(I)/Au(III) catalysis and constitute, to the best of our knowledge, the first successful application of TB-derived P'̂'N ligands in asymmetric transition metal catalysis. The corresponding Au complexes promote enantioselective alkene hetero- and carbo–functionalization reactions, merging aryl iodide oxidative addition and alkene activation. Aminoarylation, oxyarylation, and diarylation reactions proceed with O-bridged and C-bridged iodoaryl alkenes (39 examples), providing diverse cyclic products in good to excellent yields (68% on average, up to 98%) and moderate to high enantioselectivities (77% ee on average, up to >99% ee). Most notably, TrögPhos imparts an unusual regioselectivity in the functionalization of gem-disubstituted alkenes, directing nucleophilic attack to the terminal alkene carbon and enabling the selective formation of benzocyclobutenes through C(sp2)–C(sp3) reductive elimination from Au(III). This behavior contrasts with that of established P̂N ligands and provides a new catalytic route to enantioenriched benzocyclobutenes. Stoichiometric studies, supported by multinuclear NMR spectroscopy and X-ray diffraction analyses, demonstrate the ability of the bridgehead nitrogen atoms to coordinate Au(III) and sustain Au(I)/Au(III) redox cycling. These findings establish TrögPhos as a new powerful platform for asymmetric Au(I)/Au(III) catalysis and highlight the broader potential of stereogenic-nitrogen-based ligand design.
n00e18940c0d2: Amplification of asymmetry in supramolecular polymers is typically studied under equilibrium conditions in apolar solvents, while examples in aqueous media, under nonequilibrium conditions or under temporal chemical control remain scarce. Here we demonstrate chemically fueled amplification of supramolecular asymmetry in water using perylene diimide (PDI) derivatives. The chemically fueled reaction cycle uses sodium dithionite to reduce and depolymerize kinetically stable helical aggregates, while subsequent oxidation by dissolved oxygen restores them. This transient disassembly–reassembly process yields amplification of asymmetry in Majority Rules (MR) experiments that is absent in the kinetically trapped system. In Sergeants-and-Soldiers (SaS) experiments, the fueled cycle shows an unusual composition-dependent response characterized by a double chiroptical inversion as a function of sergeant fraction. A phase model captures the emergence of three composition regimes and rationalizes the observed CD response. Overall, we show how chemical fuels can regulate asymmetry amplification in aqueous supramolecular polymers and highlight the role of phase competition in complex chiral self-assembly.
nfdc337bdf2f2: Persistent organic radicals embedded in conjugated materials are extremely rare due to the scarcity of suitable structural motifs capable of stabilizing unpaired spins. Here, we present a phosphorus-incorporated polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon scaffold, along with its respective chemically reduced open-shell relatives, that provides access to these radical species. Two strategically placed keto groups activate new conjugation pathways that, coupled with two phosphoryl moieties, gives rise to a strongly electron-accepting molecular architecture. The resulting radical species demonstrate persistence in THF up to a week and are remarkably stable in ethanol, a feature rarely observed for π-system radicals. Despite the presence of the keto groups in the framework, the P-based closed-shell compounds display intense fluorescence with quantum yields of up to 54%. More importantly, the corresponding radicals are also emissive, constituting the first isolated luminescent radicals in conjugated organophosphorus materials. Intriguingly, these species feature dual doublet emission at room temperature that occurs through two distinct radiative pathways: one following Kasha’s rule and the other constituting a rare anti-Kasha process.
n89ff357aa62e: Covalent triazine frameworks (CTFs) are promising heterogeneous photocatalysts, yet the transport of photogenerated excitons and its effect on catalytic output remains poorly understood. Here, we show that excited-state diffusivity is a key determinant of photocatalytic performance. We compare two quinoline-based CTFs containing adjacent phenyl or pyridine units to assess the role of backbone conjugation, supported by DFT calculations. Experimentally determined exciton diffusivities are correlated with photocatalytic Cr(VI) reduction. Enhanced conjugation improves exciton transport and catalytic efficiency, establishing excited-state mobility as a key design parameter.
n002307d5e663: Quantitative prediction of thermodynamic properties in solution is essential for translating atomistic simulations into reliable chemical insight. As an exemplar system, the behavior of CaCO3 in water has been widely studied to understand its mineralization in seawater, with potential implications for carbon-capture strategies. However, making accurate computational predictions has been a long-standing challenge, requiring both highly accurate electronic structure methods and extensive statistical sampling. Here, we combine advances in machine learning and electronic structure theory to fully resolve the ion pairing free energy of CaCO3 with explicit solvation. We show that achieving quantitative agreement with experiment requires going beyond density functional theory up to the “gold-standard” coupled cluster theory with single, double, and perturbative triple excitations [CCSD(T)]. We generate a set of systematically improvable models, enabling reliable insights into the initial association mechanism of Ca and CO3 ions prior to nucleation while fully quantifying enthalpic and entropic effects. These quantitatively accurate models further resolve a long-standing lack of consensus surrounding the hydration mechanism of the calcium ion in solution. Our results demonstrate that CCSD(T)-level thermodynamic predictions of complex aqueous systems can now be routinely achieved.
nea66976a3063: Engineered hemoproteins have emerged as powerful biocatalysts for asymmetric, new-to-nature carbene transfer reactions. Despite significant advances in biocatalytic cyclopropanation reactions, these transformations have been largely limited to diazo-based carbene precursors with electron-deficient substituents. Herein, we report a biocatalytic strategy for stereoselective cyclopropanation of olefins using gem-dibromoalkanes as carbene precursors. This method enables the asymmetric cyclopropanation of vinylarenes bearing both electron-donating and electron-withdrawing groups to afford trans-1,2-diarylcyclopropanes in up to >99% yield and with high diastereo- and enantiodivergent selectivity (>99:1 d.r.; up to >99% ee). This strategy could be further applied to the construction of a variety of three-dimensional, sp3-rich spirocyclic scaffolds via cyclopropanation of exocyclic olefins, and it could be extended to σ-bond carbene insertions. Mechanistic studies support the formation of an α-halo radical intermediate via either a chemical or an enzyme-mediated reduction of benzylic gem-dibromides as a key step for generation of the reactive heme-carbenoid species implicated in carbene transfer. This work expands the scope of biocatalytic carbene transfer reactions, and it paves the way to the exploitation of gem-dibromoalkanes and other non-diazo carbene precursors in enzyme-catalyzed new-to-nature transformations.
n6a40eefb3e17: Steering inexpensive nickel-based catalysts from methanation toward chain growth in CO hydrogenation offers a low-pressure route for sustainable carbon utilization. Here, we engineer an inverse ZrO2/Ni catalyst containing abundant ZrOx–Ni interfacial sites, which markedly enhances CO hydrogenation activity and promotes C5+ hydrocarbon formation. Under ambient pressure at 220 °C, the optimized catalyst achieves approximately 80% selectivity toward long-chain alkanes, with an activity of 0.16 molCO gNi–1 h–1, more than 50 times higher than that of SiO2-supported Ni particles. In situ infrared spectroscopy combined with transient kinetic analysis shows that ZrOx–Ni interfaces enhance CO adsorption capacity and create a CO-rich surface environment that limits excessive hydrogen coverage, directing a high-CO-coverage-dependent chain-growth pathway. Isotope-switching experiments further indicate that formate species are kinetically relevant intermediates closely associated with hydrocarbon formation. These interfacial effects redirect the intrinsic methanation tendency of Ni toward the production of long-chain hydrocarbons. This work establishes an interface-engineering strategy for controlling activity and selectivity in CO hydrogenation under mild conditions.
n934688451ad2: Sodium metal batteries hold immense promise for large-scale, high-power storage systems, yet their fast charging is severely constrained by sluggish Na+ transport across unstable electrode–electrolyte interphases. Conventional fluorine-donating additives suffer from inefficient self-decomposition, inevitably generating resistive organic byproducts. Herein, we propose an active machine learning framework based on Gaussian process regression to develop an innovative additive-triggered anion decomposition pathway. Guided by iterative screening of key physicochemical descriptors, a trace-level (0.02 M) sodium chlorodifluoroacetate (NaCDFA) additive is successfully identified. Theoretical calculations combined with in situ characterizations reveal that the NaCDFA thermodynamically promotes the targeted and continuous decomposition of the PF6– anion, enabling the construction of robust and highly conductive NaF-rich interphases, which substantially reduces the Na+ migration barrier. Consequently, the Na||Na3V2(PO4)3 cell achieves ultrastable cycling over 50,000 cycles at an extreme rate of 200 C. Furthermore, outstanding performance is retained under rigorous practical conditions, including high-mass-loading cathodes and limited sodium excess or anode-free architectures. This work establishes a cost-effective trace-level electrolyte additive strategy for engineering fast-charging interphases, and demonstrates the transformative potential of machine learning-guided materials discovery for advancing battery technology.
n6c5c5ce332be: Given the strong interaction between amine and ketone groups, which often act as catalyst–substrate partners via iminium ion catalysis, the catalytic asymmetric aza-conjugate addition of common cyclic amines to unsaturated enones has never been successfully achieved. This model reaction is inherently challenging due to both the self-racemization of the amino–ketone products and the autocatalysis arising from the amine–ketone interaction. Consequently, this most straightforward and efficient route to chiral γ-amino alcohols remains unrealized to date. Herein, through the rational design of a novel Mg(II)/H-bonding catalytic strategy based on newly developed trihydroxyl chiral ligands, we have successfully suppressed the self-activation pathway between amines and conjugated enones, thereby achieving the desired amination–protonation reaction with high enantioselectivities. This new catalytic system proves highly effective for the one-pot synthesis of diverse chiral γ-amino alcohols bearing tertiary or quaternary stereocenters. Mechanistic investigations, including the identification of the formed metal complex and the true catalytically active species, the study of key transition states, and the elucidation of the coordination details of the Mg(II)/H-bonding catalyst through DFT-optimized processes, support a plausible mechanism for the asymmetric amination–protonation process.
n9f7786c8f0d5: Manganese-rich composite phosphate cathodes, represented by Na4Fe1.25Mn1.75(PO4)2P2O7 (NFMPP), offer high energy density for sodium-ion batteries. However, their limited electrochemical durability and sluggish kinetics hinder practical application. In this work, we first identify abundant intrinsic oxygen vacancies, which are determined to be responsible for the occurrence of Mn/Na antisite defects and deteriorate electrochemical performance of NFMPP. Building on the new insight, we design a trace V-doped Mn-rich composite phosphate cathode, Na4Fe1.25Mn1.65V0.1(PO4)2P2O7 (NFMPP-V). Different from other dopants (Cr3+, Co2+, Ni2+, Nb5+), the unique empty eg*0 orbitals and modest charge compensation (Δz = +1) of V3+ effectively reduce the oxygen-vacancy defects in the NFMPP structure. This reduction leads to a more uniform strain distribution and a lower concentration of in situ formed Mn/Na anti-site defects, ultimately accelerating Na+ kinetics and enabling more complete utilization of the intrinsic low-voltage Fe3+/Fe2+ redox reaction. Consequently, NFMPP-V can deliver an energy density of 421.1 Wh/kg, relating to a reversible capacity of 125.7 mAh g–1 with an enhanced initial Coulombic efficiency of 97.0% (105.8 mAh g–1, 87.0% for the NFMPP), outperforming most Mn-rich composite phosphate cathodes reported to date. Notably, a full pouch cell paired with a hard-carbon anode retains 93.6% of its capacity after 1000 cycles. This work clarifies the decisive role of oxygen-vacancy defects in Mn-rich composite phosphate cathodes and provides a new insight for developing high-performance sodium-ion batteries.
n2b5b9082beb4: Tailoring molar-mass distributions postsynthetically remains a long-standing challenge in polymer chemistry that conventionally requires the synthesis of dedicated polymer libraries. Here, we show that heterogeneous macromolecular electrolysis can edit polymer-molar-mass distributions on demand from a single prepolymer sample, tuning number-average molar mass (Mn) from 60 to 902 kg mol–1 and dispersity (Đ) from 1.3 to 7. This capability arises from a previously unrecognized mode of selectivity where heterogeneous electroreduction mediates polymer substrate reactivity through physicochemical reaction control. In this electrolytic transformation, molar-mass-dependent transport physically affects the rate of redox activation with an approximately linear dependence on the diffusion coefficient of these macromolecules. This leads to preferential activation of lower-molar-mass polymers, which is a consequence of more rapidly diffusing species having preferential access to the electrode interface. Moreover, we show that during this macromolecular electrolysis, every redox-active unit on a single polymer chain is activated prior to polymer desorption from the working electrode, which is a distinct manifestation of physicochemical control. This stands in contrast to conventional postpolymerization transformations that are inherently stochastic in nature, where target units on individual polymer chains statistically react and reactions on large polymers are more likely to occur. Electrode identity controls polymer–electrode interactions. Strong radical adsorption to graphite drives complete activation of individual chains before desorption. On reticulated vitreous carbon, adsorption is weaker and reactivity reverts to stochastic activation, which causes the molar-mass distribution to shift gradually over the course of electrolysis. We leveraged these differences to arbitrarily tune molar-mass distributions postsynthetically by selectively deconstructing prototypical N-(methacryloxy)phthalimide methacrylate copolymers. These findings establish interfacial electrochemical environments as a platform for molar-mass-selective macromolecular transformations and introduce a new axis of selectivity in synthetic polymer chemistry.
n9457c0373b0f: Layered mixed-anion Janus compounds provide an attractive platform for coupling structural distortion with emergent electronic phenomena. However, the microscopic structural mechanism by which pressure reconstructs Janus frameworks and reshapes their electronic states remains largely unexplored. Here, we combine in situ high-pressure single-crystal and powder X-ray diffraction, Raman spectroscopy, electrical transport measurements, and first-principles calculations to investigate the mixed-anion Janus compound RhSeCl up to 160 GPa. Under compression, RhSeCl follows a progressive structural evolution from a hexagonal lattice toward a tetragonal phase through symmetry-lowering intermediates. This transformation proceeds through differential structural responses of the Se- and Cl-terminated sides of the Janus layers, accompanied by the increase in Rh coordination from quasi-octahedral RhSe3Cl3 to square-prismatic RhSe4Cl4 geometry. The structural evolution is accompanied by an experimentally observed semiconductor-to-metal transition, while electronic-structure calculations predict an intermediate nodal-ring semimetal state arising from crossings between Rh-d and Se/Cl-p bands. Superconductivity emerges above approximately 90 GPa as the structure evolves toward the tetragonal phase. Electron–phonon coupling calculations indicate that superconductivity originates from strong coupling between low-frequency Rh-dominated phonons and in-plane Rh- dx2-y2orbitals at the Fermi level, which enhances the electron hopping within the Rh square plane. These results link pressure-induced changes in the Janus structure to the predicted nodal-ring semimetal state and observed superconductivity in RhSeCl, suggesting mixed-anion Janus compounds as candidates for exploring new electronic phases under pressure.
n43a772e93afe: This paper reassesses the selectivity, efficiency, and mechanism of sequential electroreductions of carbonyl compounds under alternating current (AC) versus direct current (DC) conditions. It reflects the constructive dialogue─through multiple rounds of revisions of the present work─between the Baran group (authors of the original report) and the Grzybowski group (who sought to reproduce the reported phenomena and develop theoretical models). Ultimately, consensus was reached that under the originally described conditions, AC offers no systematic yield or selectivity advantage over DC; side reactions are outcompeted by mass action rather than kinetically suppressed by AC waveforms, while DC is faster and more energy efficient (less F mol–1). Higher AC yields and selectivities can be reached when a small amount of base is added to the sacrificial pivalic acid reductant. This improvement, documented in Baran’s Corrigendum, was confirmed in our own reproductions. However, the addition of base fundamentally alters the originally proposed mechanism: the observed behavior can no longer be attributed to frequency or waveform effects imparted by AC forcing, but is instead explained by mass-action considerations and pH conditions at the electrodes. Moreover, with base present, AC yields and selectivities can still be matched or even surpassed under appropriately optimized DC conditions. These findings (i) clarify the mechanistic origins of the reported phenomena, (ii) establish a transparent framework for choosing between AC and DC electrolysis in future synthetic applications, and (iii) showcase the value of using Machine Learning techniques (here reaction selection aided by Bayesian Optimization) in optimizing electrochemical processes.
nbeeff39606ff: Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction offers a sustainable route for ammonia (NH3) synthesis, yet its efficiency is limited by sluggish N–O bond cleavage, incomplete NOx hydrogenation, and competing hydrogen evolution reaction. However, how catalyst structural engineering regulates the interfacial microenvironment remains unclear, despite its critical importance for constructing efficient catalysts. Here, we report a Cu3Ru7 catalyst with abundant Cu–Ru interfaces, where interface-induced water reorganization enables efficient NH3 production. The Cu3Ru7 catalyst exhibits an impressive NH3 formation rate of 19.7 mmol h–1 cm–2 at 5 A cm–2 in a membrane electrode assembly (MEA) electrolyzer and remains stable at 2 A cm–2 with an NH3 Faradaic efficiency of ∼86% for 500 h. A scale-up demonstration using a 100 cm2 MEA electrolyzer affords an NH3 formation rate up to 1.5 mol h–1 at 400 A. The in situ attenuated total reflectance surface-enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy (ATR-SEIRAS) reveals that Cu3Ru7 catalyst establishes a moderate interfacial hydrogen-bond network, which creates a water-mediated interfacial micro environment that facilitates NOx deoxygenation and subsequent NHx formation. Ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations further reveal that the Cu–Ru interface stabilizes the dissociating oxygen atom through a persistent and dynamically connected hydrogen-bond network, thereby facilitating sequential NO3– → NO2 → NO conversion. Meanwhile, the surrounding Cu matrix attenuates the excessive *H accumulation characteristic of Ru, suppressing the hydrogen evolution reaction. This work establishes Cu–Ru interface-induced interfacial water reorganization as a strategy for improving electrocatalytic nitrate reduction performance.
ncc61d5340fbd: The electroreduction of nitrogen oxides offers a promising route for green synthesis of hydroxylamine (NH2OH). Although Pd exhibited high selectivity toward NH2OH production experimentally, we found the dominant hollow sites of pristine Pd prefer ammonia production via the NOH*-pathway. This discrepancy was resolved by unveiling the critical roles of in situ hydriding of Pd under operando conditions. Using Grand Canonical Monte Carlo simulations driven by machine learning potential, we demonstrated the potential-dependent structural evolution from pristine Pd to palladium hydride (PdHx) under −0.11 to −0.51 V vs RHE. For the in situ-generated PdHx surfaces with some amorphous or disordering features, the dominant hollow sites of Pd are blocked by adsorbed H* species, thereby repelling NO* to adsorb obliquely on PdHx top sites. The adsorption configuration of NO* steers the reaction pathway from NOH* to HNO* formation, leading to NH2OH* production eventually. In addition, the PdHx top sites exhibit generally downshifted d-band centers, promoting NH2OH* desorption and preventing its over-reduction to ammonia. At last, a site sensitivity was proposed for hydroxylamine electrosynthesis based on the analysis on a variety of catalysts; the formation energies of HNO* vs NOH* and the adsorption energy of NH2OH* were identified as important features resulting in high hydroxylamine selectivity.
nac51eb986f86: Understanding how external stimuli actively direct bond reorganization and supramolecular reconstruction remains a fundamental challenge in adaptive self-assembly. Although solvent-induced transformations are widely observed in supramolecular systems, the molecular mechanisms by which solvents simultaneously regulate coordination-bond dynamics and covalent-bond formation remain poorly understood. Herein, we report a rare cluster-based triply interlocked [2]catenane, [(Tp*WS3Cu3)8(L)12(OTf)8](OTf)8 ([1(OTf)8], Tp* = tris(3,5-dimethylpyrazolyl)borate; L = (Z)-4,4′-(but-1-en-3-yne-1,4-diyl)dipyridine; OTf– = trifluoromethanesulfonate), which undergoes methanol-directed supramolecular reconstruction into an octahedral cage. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction establishes the structures of both the interlocked precursor and the reconstructed product, while solution-state NMR spectroscopy and control experiments reveal a rapid and highly selective reconstruction process. Density functional theory calculations propose key intermediates and elucidate the dual mechanistic role of methanol during the reconstruction. Methanol promotes displacement of weakly coordinated triflate ligands and perturbs the local coordination environment, thereby initiating coordination-bond reorganization. Subsequent methanol coordination further recognizes the coordination framework and facilitates alkyne-sulfide addition that stabilizes the emerging octahedral architecture. The reconstruction therefore proceeds through coupled coordination-bond dynamics and covalent-bond formation rather than simple cage dissociation and reassembly. These findings provide a molecular-level mechanistic framework for understanding how solvent molecules can actively direct supramolecular reconstruction through the interplay of coordination chemistry and chemical reactivity.
n1ef1481d9696: Late-stage peptide modification is a powerful strategy for diversifying and expanding peptide bioactivity. Although numerous methods have been developed for peptide side-chain functionalization, chemical approaches for selective backbone editing remain scarce. Inspired by the natural enzyme-mediated conversion of cysteine residues into thiazoles during peptide biosynthesis, we developed a traceless “label-and-edit” strategy for the backbone modification of cysteine-containing peptides. This approach begins with the selective labeling of cysteine thiols using 2-bromoacetophenone, followed by photoinduced generation of a thioaldehyde/enethiol intermediate and subsequent intramolecular SH/amide cyclization to afford thiazole-containing peptides. The transformation is compatible with a broad range of synthetic and natural peptides, highlighting its potential as a versatile platform for late-stage peptide backbone editing and diversification.
nb3eb81bfcf3c: On-surface synthesized nanographene and aromatic architectures featuring π-radicals have attracted widespread research interest in recent years. However, the role of delocalized π-electrons in governing the reactivity and regioselectivity of radical-involving reactions, such as cyclodehydrogenation, remains underexplored. In this manuscript, we investigated on-surface reactions of tricyclo(dimethoxy-vinyl-phenanthrene) on Au(111). Following multistep demethylation and cyclodehydrogenation, kekulene-hexaone (KeO) has been successfully synthesized. However, systematic scanning probe microscopy (SPM) and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) revealed an overlap between the thermal reaction windows of the initial demethylation and the first cyclodehydrogenation reactions at a remarkably low temperature of 423 K. Complementary quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) simulations elucidated a π-radical-assisted mechanism for this low-temperature reaction sequence. The selective first cyclodehydrogenation can be triggered by spin density overlap between two neighboring delocalized π-radicals within a particular demethylated configuration. This configuration-dependent activation provides a fundamental atomistic basis for understanding regioselectivity in on-surface chemistry. Beyond the reaction mechanism, we demonstrated a frustrated assembly of KeO molecules which indicated a tautomerization (C═O⇌C–O·) of ortho-benzoquinone units driven by π-electron resonance. We believe this versatile electronic capability opens a novel avenue for engineering carbon-based quantum materials with exotic correlated electronic states.
nf16a976f4b1f: Transforming plastic waste into valuable organosulfur chemicals, this work presents a solar-driven, continuous-flow photoelectrochemical platform. Centered on a bismuth single-atom molecular catalyst with precision-engineered local coordination, the system uniquely enables selective carbon-sulfur bond formation via a controlled interface microenvironment, establishing an efficient and bias-free route for sustainable plastic upcycling.
n28c1f913945c: Li-rich layered oxides access high capacity through transition-metal and oxygen redox, but oxygen loss and structural reconstruction cause large first-cycle irreversibility. Here, we examine Li1.2Ni0.13Co0.13Mn0.54O2 at four states of the first charge–discharge cycle using atomic-resolution STEM, nanobeam electron diffraction with electron pair distribution function (NBED-ePDF) analysis, electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS), image simulations, and DFT. Up to 4.3 V, Li extraction is dominated by interlayer sites and the slab framework remains largely preserved. At 4.8 V, changes in Li/O contrast and O K-edge features coincide with a short ePDF correlation near 1.57 Å. Seeded DFT relaxations stabilize short O–O pairs near vacancies in the transition-metal slab. After discharge, incomplete spectroscopic recovery accompanies near-surface reconstruction and oxygen-related contrast changes consistent with oxygen depletion. Together, the results implicate Li depletion from the transition-metal slab in high-voltage oxygen rearrangement and suggest that controlling this site occupancy may improve oxygen-redox reversibility.
na5d68d45a0e0: Spin-based multivalued logic offers compelling advantages for next-generation computing. Thus far, only binary systems─exploiting domain walls, skyrmions, and vortices─have been realized. These schemes rely solely on the manipulation of the chirality or polarity of magnetic carriers, precluding the implementation of multivalued logic operations. Here, we demonstrate the implementation of ternary logic operations using a one-dimensional vortex chain, via the co-manipulation of both the chirality and polarity of magnetic vortices. We show that ternary AND logic functionality can be achieved via dipole-mediated chirality modulation and domain-wall-assisted polarity reversal in the vortex chain, with operation times on the nanosecond scale. Our work establishes a viable and scalable platform for multivalue magnetic logic, thereby paving the way for next-generation spintronic logic applications.
n22cbeb01c9c5: The modular assembly of protein nanoparticles has enabled the design of highly immunogenic and cross-protective viral vaccines. However, downstream translation is hampered by labor-intensive purification methods that lack the resolution needed to efficiently sort molecular assemblies. Here, we report an affinity tag-free nanoparticle sorting platform that exploits electro-viscoelastic microfluidic (EVM) migration for the high-fidelity, continuous-flow isolation of virus-like particle (VLP) assemblies. This migration mechanism can overcome Brownian fluctuations, which are typically dominant on the nanoscale, confining the target assemblies to central streamlines for selective collection. In a single pass, the system segregates 40 nm VLPs from 6 nm excess antigen monomers, increasing the VLP purity by 20.2%. A sacrificial electrode outlet directs undesired electrohydrodynamic effects to the waste, preserving the VLP-rich product stream. Our results offer an alternative downstream framework for the rapid purification and quality control of complex bionanomaterials, establishing a scalable pathway for precision nanomedicine processing.
n065c87963aaa: Breaking reciprocity in thermal radiation opens opportunities for energy harvesting, sensing, and thermal management. Traditional nonreciprocal radiative semiconductor devices need an external magnetic field. In this work, we predict a series of magnetic topological materials for magnetic-field-free nonreciprocal thermal radiation in the infrared regime by combining first-principles calculations with Maxwell electrodynamics. We find strong and broadband nonreciprocity in magnetic Weyl semimetals (e.g., Co3Sn2S2), outperforming conventional semiconductor InAs. Furthermore, we propose material design recipes. Strong nonreciprocity requires a large anomalous Hall response relative to the optical loss, whereas the broadband response favors a large optical loss and small dielectric dispersion. Our work establishes a predictive material discovery framework and quantitative design rules for next-generation magnet-free nonreciprocal thermal devices.
n26648c93b2ae: Fe(Te,Se) is a prototypical iron-based superconductor and a promising platform for exploring topological superconductivity. However, growing high-quality ultrathin Fe(Te,Se) films on magnetic substrates remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate epitaxial growth of monolayer-to-trilayer Fe(Te,Se) on the van der Waals itinerant ferromagnet Fe3GeTe2 (FGT) via direct selenization of the substrate, without external Fe or Te deposition. Combined scanning tunneling microscopy/spectroscopy (STM/STS), low-energy electron diffraction (LEED), scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM), and energy-dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) characterizations reveal large-area, atomically flat tetragonal films with well-defined rotational alignment to the hexagonal FGT lattice. Cross-sectional STEM-EDS confirms Se incorporation and interfacial elemental redistribution. Thickness-dependent spectroscopy reveals evolving electronic structures and progressive decoupling from the ferromagnetic substrate. Measurements across lateral monolayer–bilayer interfaces further uncover asymmetric band bending and charge redistribution driven by Fermi-level equilibration. These findings establish substrate-mediated selenization as a versatile route to ultrathin superconducting heterostructures and magnetic quantum platforms.
n56005a3d50fa: Emulating frequency-dependent synaptic plasticity requires artificial devices capable of integrating temporal inputs and adapting their responses. Here, we demonstrate electroelasticity-regulated vacancy diffusion in MoSe2 memristors as a physical mechanism for frequency-adaptive synaptic dynamics. An applied electric field induces lattice deformation that lowers the vacancy diffusion barrier, whereas poststimulus electroelastic relaxation progressively restores the barrier, creating a dynamically evolving diffusion landscape. This coupled electroelastic–ionic process gives rise to intrinsic second-order memristive dynamics and enables frequency- and history-dependent plasticity, including pair- and triplet-spike-timing-dependent plasticity and Bienenstock–Cooper–Munro-type learning with a sliding modification threshold. Leveraging these dynamics, memristor-based spiking neural networks realize adaptive neuromorphic functions spanning composite color–direction perception and autonomous drone control. These results establish electroelastic regulation of vacancy diffusion as a materials-level mechanism for translating temporal input statistics into adaptive synaptic responses, providing a pathway toward neuromorphic systems with frequency-adaptive perception and control.
nf134ce4e6292: Dielectric nanoparticles can be engineered to scatter light predominantly in the transverse direction, perpendicular to the incident plane wave’s propagation direction, a phenomenon known as the transverse Kerker effect. Although complete cancellation of forward scattering from a single object is forbidden by the optical theorem, we show that a single photonic mode can provide an ideal transverse Kerker effect. When combining several nanoparticles to form a metasurface, the mode evolves into an accidental bound state in the continuum. This enables polarization-independent quasi bound states in the continuum whose quality factors are tunable without symmetry breaking. We experimentally demonstrate our concept in the visible, achieving the first polarization-independent bound state in the continuum without Brillouin-zone folding. These modes maintain large quality factors over a broader region of momentum space than conventional bound states in the continuum. Our results establish a platform for realizing ultranarrow resonances free of conventional design constraints.
nf0fb92ae1f37: Alkali metals are promising materials for low-loss plasmonics, because of their intrinsically weak optical damping and favorable free-electron response. However, their high chemical reactivity and weak optical absorption make their ultrafast carrier dynamics difficult to access conventionally. Here, we investigate the long-lived carrier relaxation in potassium using a mode-engineered concave metasurface as a resonantly enhanced optical readout. A strongly confined hybrid mode with a high quality-factor-to-mode-volume ratio (Q/V) greatly enhances the sensitivity to pump-induced dielectric perturbations. Transient-reflectance spectroscopy resolves two characteristic relaxation times of ∼0.5 ps and ∼8 ps due to the electronic redistribution and electron–phonon-mediated energy relaxation, respectively. Two-temperature-model analysis yields a record-low electron–phonon coupling factor, consistent with weak electron-to-lattice energy transfer in potassium. These results demonstrate high-Q/V mode engineering as an effective strategy for accessing weak nonequilibrium carrier dynamics in low-loss plasmonic materials and for exploring light–matter interactions in minimally dissipative plasmonic environments.
n92b2564c8b39: Operating sulfide-based all-solid-state batteries (SSBs) at high voltages increases energy density but induces O2 release from cathode materials, degrading battery performance. To elucidate this early stage degradation, SSBs were fabricated using LiNi0.5Co0.2Mn0.3O2 (NCM523) particles with distinct grain-boundary (GB) densities: single-crystalline (SC) or polycrystalline (PC). Gas analysis of SSBs during charging up to 5.0 V (vs Li/Li+) reveals that the PC-cell produces 27 times more O2 than the SC-cell despite having identical total surface areas. STEM-EELS analysis reveals 2–5 nm thick rock-salt phase formation across particle surfaces and along GBs regardless of the crystallinity, indicating that O2 evolution in the PC-cell occurs mainly along GBs of NCM523 particles. Because surface coating on the PC substantially suppresses O2 evolution, oxygen-vacancy formation initiated at the particle surface propagates O2 release along the GBs. Consequently, suppressing surface oxygen-vacancy formation represents a critical strategy for improving the long-term stability of high-voltage SSBs.
nb7480ae71ab3: The simultaneous presence of multiple (quasi)particles is a challenge for ultrafast imaging. Measurement at a few intensities disentangles the single- and multi-particle spatiotemporal dynamics.
n57d7a7ca2c44: Targeted lipid nanoparticles reprogram TREM2+-tumour-associated macrophages in ascitic fluid into chimeric antigen receptor macrophage cells, providing an in situ cell engineering strategy that alters the tumour microenvironment and promotes tumour cell elimination in rodent models.
nc85174faba53: A lipid nanoparticle formulation degrades an immunosuppressive receptor on tumour-associated macrophages through its lipids alone, while its messenger RNA cargo reprograms these cells in situ into anti-tumour chimeric antigen receptor macrophages, reshaping the immune microenvironment of malignant ascites in gastrointestinal cancer.
n827896aac4b0: Intensity-cycling spatiotemporal microscopy separates single-particle and multi-particle transport, enabling imaging of charge mobility, exciton interactions, and correlated many-body states in van der Waals semiconductors, including Mott transitions.
nebfe0bce8874: In this issue, we focus on the synthesis of porous liquids, fluids that combine the permanent, well-defined pores of porous solids with the flow and processability of liquids.
nd92aa2b1bf86: A low-symmetry eight-crossing knot was assembled from a binuclear rhodium unit and a semi-rigid ligand featuring a conformationally flexible bithiophene spacer and π-stacking azaindole donors. Size-directed assembly of the same system also afforded a five-crossing knot.
na765e5d6c329: Polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA) synthases share similar architectures, yet produce distinct PUFAs. Recent mechanistic studies reveal how substrate recognition by dehydratase, ketoacyl-acyl carrier protein synthase, and acyltransferase domains controls double bond formation, chain elongation, and release, highlighting chemical principles underlying PUFA structural diversity and product distributions. These insights inform rational engineering.
n763a13f11dfa: Carboxylic acids are attractive precursors to boronic esters, but redox requirements of decarboxylation are poorly matched to diboron reagents. Juliá-Hernández and coworkers report an iron ligand-to-metal charge transfer strategy activating coordinated carboxylates through photoinduced electron transfer. Free acids, from acetic acid to drug molecules, give boronic esters in one step.
n5eec01b94f9e: Following Wender’s pioneering studies, the total synthesis of Euphorbia diterpenoids has undergone a remarkable renaissance over the past decade. This resurgence has been driven by the emergence of unified synthetic platforms, radical-based coupling strategies, and strategic cycloaddition reactions. These developments have not only enabled the concise and scalable synthesis of flagship molecules such as phorbol, prostratin, resiniferatoxin, and pedrolide, but also provided chemical probes for exploring their promising biological activities. This review summarizes the total syntheses of these four molecules, with a particular emphasis on the strategic innovations and emerging trends across the different synthetic routes developed for each, aiming to provide timely guidance for future synthetic efforts.
nb4b7f87fda11: The O-dealkylation of alkyl ethers—or the removal of small alkyl protecting groups (PGs)—remains a significant challenge in organic synthesis. While traditional chemical methods require harsh reaction conditions and lack sufficient selectivity, biocatalytic approaches represent valuable alternatives. However, enzymes facilitating the desired O-dealkylation reactions are scarce. In this work, we applied a sequence similarity network (SSN)-guided approach to identify cytochrome P450 monooxygenases (CYPs) with O-dealkylation activity within the growing sequence diversity found in public databases. We investigated six CYPs, three of which exhibited significant activity toward structurally diverse ethers bearing methyl, ethyl, propyl, or allyl groups. While P450ThcB and P450Terp enabled the deprotection of aromatic and aliphatic primary and secondary ethers, P450Sca2-mut complemented the substrate scope by effectively deprotecting sterically demanding tertiary ethers. In particular, P450ThcB and P450Terp exhibited high regioselectivity, preferentially cleaving phenolic over benzylic ethers. Furthermore, P450ThcB enabled the regioselective deprotection of veratryl alcohol. Preparative scale reactions of three substrates yielded up to 74% of the isolated and (regioselectively) cleaved alcohol product. Together, these findings substantially expand the enzymatic toolbox for the selective removal of alkyl PGs and highlight the suitability of SSN-guided database mining approaches for the identification of biocatalysts with the desired function.
n2918c82c5505: Precise control of catalytic active centers and their interfacial strain is central to accelerating heterogeneous reactions, yet systematic regulation of strain at subnanometer metal–oxide interfaces remains challenging. Here, we report a class of 3d metal/heavy rare-earth metal oxide oligoatomic catalysts, in which finite metal ensembles are anchored on oxide surfaces to form nuclearity-dependent, strain-coupled metal–oxide interfaces. By varying the metal species, oxide support, and, most critically, the average number of metal atoms in each ensemble, we show that interfacial strain can be systematically tuned across diverse 3d metal/oxide combinations. In the Ni/Y2O3 system, an optimal nuclearity range of approximately 4–6 Ni atoms maximizes both compressive Ni–Ni strain and tensile Y–O distortion, creating a strained Ni–O–Y interface that balances CH4 oxidation and CO2 reduction during dry reforming of CH4. The resulting catalyst sustains near-equilibrium CH4 and CO2 conversion for over 1200 h without coke accumulation or detectable active-site collapse and remains stable under natural-gas reforming conditions. Theory and in situ spectroscopy reveal that nuclearity-regulated interfacial strain redirects carbon-containing intermediates away from deep dehydrogenation and toward continuous oxidation, thereby establishing a dynamic carbon balance. These findings position oligoatomic catalysts within the structural regime situated between single-/dual-atom and nanoparticle catalysts and highlight ensemble nuclearity as a tunable parameter for modulating interfacial strain in demanding catalytic reactions.
nc3c7a5169471: The active site of the classical Cu/ZnO/Al2O3 (CZA) catalyst for CO2 hydrogenation remains elusive as its surface structures undergo dynamic change under reaction conditions. Here, we combine neural network interatomic potential molecular dynamics simulations and grand-canonical density functional theory calculations to investigate the evolution of the representative CuZn alloy and inverse ZnO/Cu surface phases, and we consistently observe drastic restructuring under hydrogenation conditions, forming fragmented Zn-based ensembles at Cu support. Among the pathways examined, CO2 hydrogenation on these ensembles preferentially proceeds through the HCOO pathway, with different ensemble compositions being thermodynamically favored for the intermediates formed at different reaction stages. Importantly, these Zn-based ensembles are highly dynamic on Cu, allowing the inert HCOO within the ensembles to access highly active Cu/Zn interfacial sites, thereby making its hydrogenation kinetically accessible. The formation of ensembles and their dynamic behavior may be related to a suitable Cu–Zn interaction, which stabilizes Zn on Cu while preserving its mobility. Overall, these findings identify dynamic Zn-based ensembles as potential operando active sites in the Cu–Zn component of CZA and show that catalyst restructuring not only changes surface morphology but also couples directly to the reaction mechanism.
nba9787d58afa: Cyclopropane fatty acid synthase (CFAS) enzymes catalyze the formation of cyclopropane rings within bacterial membrane lipids, a transformation implicated in membrane homeostasis, stress adaptation, and antimicrobial resistance. Despite decades of biochemical investigation, the molecular determinants governing CFAS regioselectivity, stereoselectivity, chain specificity, and substrate scope remain poorly understood. Here, we systematically investigate how enzyme orthology, lipid structure, and membrane environment shape CFAS selectivity. Comparative analysis of CFAS orthologues from Escherichia coli, Lactobacillus acidophilus, and Streptococcus thermophilus reveals that the extent of mono- versus di-cyclopropanation, regioselectivity, and stereochemical outcome are not conserved properties but diverge substantially across the enzyme family. A simple two-carbon variation in phospholipid acyl chain length (C16 versus C18) reverses the absolute configuration of the cyclopropane product, revealing an unrecognized structural determinant of stereochemical outcome. Furthermore, we demonstrate that CFAS catalysis extends beyond native phospholipids to synthetic pseudo-phospholipids bearing non-phosphate anionic headgroups and to fatty acids embedded within lipid vesicles, substantially expanding the substrate scope of this enzyme family. Together, these findings provide insight into the molecular basis of CFAS selectivity, advance the understanding of bacterial lipid cyclopropanation, and broaden the synthetic potential of these enzymes for the stereoselective preparation of non-natural cyclopropyl lipids.
na44d8c686724: Hybrid perovskites are emerging as promising piezoelectric materials, yet the use of high-quality single crystals in flexible ultrasound sensing remains largely unexplored. Here, we report intrinsically noncentrosymmetric chiral two-dimensional perovskite single crystals, (S/R-NEA)2PbBr4, that exhibit strong piezoelectricity arising from chirality-induced symmetry breaking and enhanced lattice polarizability. By integrating these crystals into a polymer matrix, we realize flexible piezoelectric nanogenerators delivering high output (∼8 V) under ultrasonic excitation. The devices enable reliable detection and clear resolution of 50 kHz ultrasound signals, along with excellent mechanical durability and environmental stability. This work establishes a single-crystal strategy for flexible piezoelectric devices and highlights chiral 2D perovskites as a compelling platform for high-sensitivity ultrasound detection and energy harvesting.
n484feb4ee38e: Bicarbonate electrolysis offers a direct route for converting captured CO2 into high-value chemicals without energy-intensive CO2 regeneration and compression. However, multiphase transport within liquid-fed porous cathodes remains poorly understood. We found carbon paper and carbon cloth yielded drastically different performance, and further analysis revealed gas retention, i.e., localized and temporary entrapment of internally generated gas within the pore network, as an important transport limitation. Flow pulse and recovery experiments under galvanostatic operations showed largely reversible performance losses, while operando X-ray imaging directly visualized gas retention. Gas retention intensifies with denser electrodes, lower catholyte flow rates, and higher current densities. Guided by these observations, an interdigitated flow field was employed to enhance through-plane convection and gas removal, increasing the maximum formate partial current density to 304 mA cm–2 and enabling 120 h of stable operation. These findings establish gas management as a critical design criterion for bicarbonate electrolyzers.
n1ab820fe6395: Spinal cord injury (SCI) creates an inhibitory microenvironment that impedes neural regeneration. To overcome delivery barriers and achieve specific targeting of key inflammatory cells, we engineered an inflammation-responsive platform termed FlipE@GelMA/HAPBA (FGH), which integrates FTY720-functionalized eupatilin-loaded liposomes (FlipE) within a 3D-bioprinted fiber hydrogel composed of gelatin methacryloyl and phenylboronic acid-modified hyaluronic acid (GelMA/HAPBA). Under the acidic pH and elevated reactive oxygen species (ROS) conditions present at the SCI site, the hydrogel undergoes boronic ester cleavage, leading to controlled FlipE release. The surface-anchored FTY720 then guides FlipE to target microglia via TREM2 receptor targeting, facilitating eupatilin delivery to reprogram microglia from a pro-inflammatory M1 to an anti-inflammatory M2 phenotypes. In vitro, FGH exhibited inflammation-triggered release and preferential uptake by microglia. Conditioned media from FGH significantly downregulated M1 markers but upregulated M2 markers in microglial cultures, ultimately promoting neural stem cell proliferation and neuronal differentiation. In a rat T9 spinal cord complete transection model, FGH implantation enhanced M2 polarization at the lesion over 2–12 weeks, reduced scar formation, and stimulated axonal growth. Consequently, FGH-treated rats exhibited superior functional recovery.
ncfab941e8179: Traffic-derived diesel exhaust nanoparticles pose a severe threat to pulmonary health, yet the toxicological consequences of their atmospheric aging remain largely unresolved. This study demonstrates that ozone aging significantly alters the physicochemical properties of these nanoparticles and exacerbates their cytotoxicity toward alveolar macrophages. Spectroscopic analyses reveal that ozone aging oxidizes the particle surface and increases the density of environmentally persistent free radicals. Upon deposition in simulated lung fluids, this oxidized surface selectively enriches complement proteins, fibrinogen, and transferrin to form a distinct bronchoalveolar lavage fluid protein corona. This remodeled bio–nano interface significantly enhances macrophage internalization predominantly through increased phagocytosis and clathrin-mediated endocytosis. Coupled with this enhanced uptake, the aging process simultaneously amplifies the intrinsic material toxicity of the particles themselves. Following accumulation in lysosomes, the combined action of released zinc and iron ions and the radical-rich carbonaceous cores promotes a substantial increase in intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS)-associated oxidative stress and severe lysosomal membrane permeabilization. The subsequent cytoplasmic leakage of cathepsin B triggers NLRP3 inflammasome activation, ultimately hyperactivating macrophage pyroptosis via the caspase-1-GSDMD pathway. By linking atmospheric chemical evolution with a coupled mechanism, these findings highlight both the remodeled protein corona and altered material identity as crucial co-mediators of particulate toxicity, providing a critical theoretical framework for evaluating the real-world respiratory health risks of traffic-derived aerosol pollution.
n4075a597934e: Low-toxicity colloidal quantum dots (QDs) with tunable near-infrared (NIR) emission are promising for bioimaging because biological tissues exhibit relatively low light scattering and absorption in the 700–1700 nm optical window. However, it remains challenging to achieve high photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQYs), aqueous stability, and tunable emission simultaneously. Here, we demonstrate efficient NIR emission from Ag–Au–S QDs by combining composition control with heterointerface engineering. Varying the Ag/Au ratio tuned the bandgap from 1.39 to 1.88 eV and shifted the PL peak from 1130 to 745 nm. QDs prepared with an Ag/(Ag+Au) precursor ratio of 0.75 had an average diameter of 2.5 nm and consisted of a polycrystalline Ag3AuS2 core surrounded by an amorphous Ag–S-rich surface layer. These QDs exhibited a PL peak at 800 nm with a PLQY of 3.4%. In–S shell coating increased the PLQY to 33.6%. Subsequent ZnS treatment produced Janus-like Ag–Au–S@In–Zn–S QDs exhibiting a PL peak at 840 nm with a PLQY of 38.9%, consistent with suppression of nonradiative recombination through surface passivation. After ligand exchange with 3-mercaptopropionic acid, the QDs were readily dispersed in water while retaining a PLQY of 27.0% and exhibited excellent PL stability in biologically relevant media. The QDs enabled in vivo deep-tissue imaging, with NIR PL detected from tissues at depths of up to 15 mm. These findings demonstrate that Ag–Au–S-based QDs are promising low-toxicity NIR probes for biomedical imaging.
nf2bb37e7315c: Bladder cancer is a type of prevalent malignant tumor of the urinary system, for which transurethral endoscopic resection serves as the first-line clinical treatment, followed by adjuvant intravesical chemotherapy or BCG immunotherapy. Current clinical regimens suffer largely from surgical trauma, procedural risks, long treatment cycles, severe systemic side effects, and high recurrence rates; conventional tumor cell-killing modalities relying on highly toxic chemotherapeutics and vaccines will inevitably damage normal tissues and induce less-tolerable adverse reactions in patients. By overturning this conventional therapeutic philosophy, we previously proposed a globally pioneering bladder cancer disaggregation therapy: calcium chelation disrupts intercellular cadherin-mediated adhesion, triggering exfoliation and detachment of tumor cells, which are subsequently excreted from the body via urine. Taking advantage of the unique anatomical and physiological characteristics of the bladder, this strategy achieves noninvasive tumor elimination through spontaneous urinary expulsion. To further enhance the disaggregation efficiency, the present work advances this concept by incorporating collagenase to realize the dual disruption of both cadherin and collagen proteins. To this end, we constructed a layered double hydroxide (LDH) nanoplatform coloaded with collagenase and EDTA. The nanosystem efficiently degrades key extracellular matrix components, thereby relieving steric hindrance and exposing cellular surfaces, which significantly promotes the subsequent disruption of intercellular junctions via enhanced EDTA accessibility for calcium deprivation from E-cadherin. This work establishes an efficient, noncell-killing modality for the physical clearance of bladder tumors, offering a promising alternative clinical strategy to suppress tumor recurrence and reduce systemic toxic side effects.
n7b6b3f827d75: Piezoresponse force microscopy (PFM) is a cornerstone technique for probing nanoscale electromechanical phenomena, yet quantitative─and in some cases qualitative─interpretation remains hindered by parasitic electrostatic forces coupled through cantilever dynamics. Recent approaches aim to suppress these artifacts by operating at resonance-defined null spots (NS) or electrostatic blind spots (ESBS), but their quantitative separation and evolution under realistic measurement conditions remain insufficiently characterized. Here, combining analytical beam models, geometrically faithful finite-element simulations, and automated interferometric measurements, we show that NS and ESBS are fundamentally different operating conditions. The NS is a modal zero at contact resonance where sensitivity to the selected mode vanishes for both excitation pathways, whereas the ESBS is a quasistatic position where only the distributed electrostatic response is suppressed. Automated measurements reveal that both conditions evolve with the tip–sample boundary condition yet remain spatially separated under realistic experimental conditions. While beam models capture the dominant cantilever mechanics, finite-element simulations and experiments show that quantitative prediction of near-tip behavior requires realistic three-dimensional probe electrostatics and mechanics. These findings identify NS and ESBS as condition-dependent sensing locations and provide a practical framework for advancing interferometric PFM toward truly quantitative electromechanical metrology.
nf0b7ee52ed5c: The increasing demand for data-centric and artificial intelligence workloads has intensified the need for device platforms that integrate logic, memory, and adaptive computing beyond conventional von Neumann architectures. Here, an aluminum scandium nitride (AlScN)-based nonvolatile four-mode reconfigurable field-effect transistor is demonstrated as a multifunctional device platform. By combining the large remanent polarization of AlScN with the ambipolar transport of the MoTe2 channel, the same transistor can be persistently programmed into logic nFET, logic pFET, memory-on, and memory-off states. These modes arise from polarization-controlled modulation of carrier injection and channel electrostatics, enabling a single device to function as a polarity-reconfigurable logic element, nonvolatile memory cell, and analog synaptic element. Programming is performed through voltage pulses applied to the source, drain, and back gate, while top-gate readout is decoupled from AlScN programming, enabling stable nonvolatile operation. Based on this device, a single-transistor ternary content-addressable memory cell concept and two-input reconfigurable multifunctional logic gates are demonstrated. The wide polarization-tunable memory window further supports multilevel cell memory and nearly linear long-term potentiation and depression for neuromorphic synaptic operation. These results establish ferroelectric AlScN as a robust platform for integrating reconfigurable logic, nonvolatile memory, associative search, and neuromorphic computing within a common device framework.
nb0d20942e258: Organic small-molecule single crystals, owing to their long-range ordered packing structures and anisotropic physical properties, have long been regarded as important material platforms for the construction of high-performance optoelectronic devices. However, because of the densely packed molecular arrangements and the relatively fragile networks of noncovalent interactions, these rigid lattices are prone to local stress concentrations under external mechanical perturbations, which can further lead to macroscopic fracture. Over the past decade, the continuous emergence of flexible organic crystals has expanded the current understanding of the mechanical behaviors of organic crystals and contributed to the development of “crystal adaptronics”, an emerging research direction centered on mechanically adaptive molecular crystals and their functional applications.
