Under appropriate molecular conformations and lattice symmetry conditions, some organic crystals can accommodate pronounced deformation, including bending, through reversible and cooperative lattice expansion-contraction or through interlayer slippage, thereby dissipating stress while preserving structural integrity and intrinsic optoelectronic functionality. In this review, we move beyond a simple categorization of recent works to critically summarize the mechanical mechanisms of flexible organic crystals, the corresponding molecular design strategies, and recent advances in their applications in functional devices, and further discuss the major challenges and future directions in this field.
n60dc581f46e0: Biological membranes actively regulate their composition to fine-tune their packing, fluidity, phase, and surface charge, key properties that influence biomolecular interactions driving essential cellular pathways. While membrane surface charge is often attributed to specific lipid headgroups, the role of acyl-chain chemistry in modulating the interplay between these biophysical membrane properties remains unexplored. Here, we systematically investigate how the acyl-chain length and saturation modulate lipid packing, fluidity, and membrane surface charge in zwitterionic lipid membranes. Using amphiphilic DNA nanoprobes as model charged biomolecules, we describe the interplay between packing, fluidity, phase, and charge, identifying a packing-dependent guiding principle for membrane interactions that persists in the presence of anionic lipids. We also demonstrate that the identity and hydrophobicity of membrane anchors in nanoprobes significantly influence their binding to the membranes. By integrating acyl-chain chemistry and membrane biophysical properties into design criteria for biomolecular attachment, our findings provide a mechanistic framework for engineering membrane interactions with both DNA nanoprobes and DNA-based coacervates. Beyond direct application to biomimetic platforms and synthetic cell engineering, these insights are relevant to lipid-based vaccine nanotechnologies and a fundamental understanding of membrane–biomolecule interactions in living cells.
ncea641d04261: Ligand binding identified during screening does not necessarily translate into improved nanocarrier delivery. Here, we report a membrane-context screening strategy that uses BT-549 cell membrane-functionalized silica microspheres to identify peptide ligands with preserved nanodelivery activity. From a 7-mer combinatorial library, P1 (KFYVSGT) was selected as a membrane-enriched peptide candidate based on its preferential retention by the membrane-functionalized stationary phase relative to bare silica. After conjugation to PEG–PCL micelles, P1 preserved the nanocarrier’s size, charge, morphology, stability, and drug-loading capacity, yet markedly enhanced biological performance. P1-functionalized micelles increased BT-549 cellular uptake by approximately 5-fold and tumor accumulation by about 3-fold in a BT-549 xenograft model. When loaded with doxorubicin, P1 micelles restrained tumor expansion to 1.96-fold of the initial volume, compared with 4.83-fold for nontargeted micelles, with favorable preliminary systemic tolerance. Competitive uptake, energy depletion, peptide-affinity capture, inhibition, colocalization, and docking analyses suggest that P1 activity is associated with a Galectin-1-related membrane environment. This work establishes membrane-context screening as a practical route to function-preserving peptide ligands for targeted nanodelivery.
n1d049da7b2ad: Pore formation is a fundamental process for all forms of life. In the wake of antimicrobial resistance, drug-induced poration in microbial membranes attracts increasing interest. It is postulated that antimicrobial molecules bind to the membranes and insert into them, forming nanometer pores causing membrane disruption. Existing evidence indicates that pore formation completes within minutes but is energetically unfavorable, suggesting that there should be a transition state preceding it. Herein, we reveal such a state. Exemplified in a cecropin family of antimicrobial peptides we demonstrate that membrane blebbing occurs within milliseconds of introducing antimicrobials into membranes and manifests in the formation and rupture of elongated membrane blebs – causing membrane disruption under the first second of treatment.
n7cdf5999354b: Inflammation is a host defense mechanism. If the host cannot prevent severe inflammation, patients would experience persistent damage and chronic inflammation that can cause many diseases. The regulation of the inflammatory process includes complex mechanisms such as oxidative stress control, intracellular and genetic signaling, antibacterial defense, tissue repair, and related processes. Nanozymes, defined as nanomaterials with intrinsic enzyme-mimetic catalytic activities, have been considered as versatile tools for inflammation control on account of their programmable catalytic process, structural and surface tunability. By integrating exogenous stimulus response, endogenous microenvironment sensing, biological carrier coupling and intelligent design strategies, nanozymes have been increasingly employed for precise, multiscale, and multistage intervention. Herein, nanozyme-mediated inflammatory regulation is organized according to the predominant mode of intervention into reactive oxygen species (ROS)-based and primarily non-ROS-based strategies, including redox homeostasis restoration, antimicrobial defense, healing, gasotransmitter signaling, and probiotic-assisted processes. From a multimechanistic perspective, interaction logic and integration principles under different regulation modalities are revealed, and some suggestions for the rational development of next generation nanozyme systems are also discussed to contribute to smart and personalized inflammation therapy.
ne09ed43b9422: Peripheral myeloid cells are key regulators of systemic inflammation and promising targets for immune intervention in Alzheimer’s disease (AD). However, selective in vivo small interfering RNA (siRNA) delivery to these cells remains challenging because conventional lipid nanoparticles often exhibit predominant hepatic accumulation and usually require ligand or antibody modification for immune-cell targeting. Here, we report a structure-engineered lipid–mineral nanoparticle platform, termed MCP, for ligand-free myeloid RNA interference (RNAi) delivery. MCP integrates a calcium phosphate mineral phase with a phosphatidic acid-enriched lipid interface, enabling efficient siRNA incorporation. The Ca2+–lipid cooperative architecture promoted macropinocytosis-dependent uptake and preferential siRNA delivery to peripheral myeloid cells in vivo, particularly Ly6Chigh monocytes and macrophages, with enhanced delivery under AD-associated inflammatory conditions. Systemic delivery of MCP carrying siRNA against triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells 1 (TREM1) attenuated neuroinflammatory and neurodegenerative pathology in an AD mouse model, supporting peripheral myeloid reprogramming as a route to modulate central nervous system (CNS) disease progression. Notably, MCP also achieved efficient TREM1 silencing in AD patient-derived peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) and restored TREM1 expression toward healthy-control levels. This work establishes a structure-driven, ligand-free lipid–mineral RNAi platform for peripheral immune intervention in AD.
n23b1f9f682d7: The development of high-performance photocatalysts is essential for advancing light-driven micro/nanomotors. However, the limited morphological tunability and inefficient charge transport of most polymeric semiconductors significantly restrict their photocatalytic activity and propulsion performance. Herein, dendritic mesoporous m-aminophenol-formaldehyde (MAPF) resin semiconductors with tunable pore structures and particle sizes are synthesized via a micelle-mediated self-assembly strategy. By integrating metal–phenolic supramolecular coordination networks with MAPF nanospheres, followed by asymmetric Au deposition, a hybrid nanomotor system is constructed. The metal–phenolic network facilitates interfacial charge transfer and optimizes charge-carrier dynamics between the photoactive MAPF core and the Au layer, thereby enhancing propulsion performance. The resulting nanomotors exhibit multiwavelength-controllable motion and phototactic collective behaviors. Meanwhile, the metal–phenolic components endow the system with intrinsic antibacterial activity and pH-responsive degradability, enabling controllable antimicrobial effects. As a proof of concept, the nanomotors demonstrate synergistic photodynamic and chemical antimicrobial activities against Escherichia coli and Karenia mikimotoi. This work presents the demonstration of supramolecular interfacial engineering for enhancing the performance of polymeric semiconductor-based micro/nanomotors, highlighting its potential for constructing multifunctional, high-performance light-driven micro/nanomotor systems.
naa8c055efc37: The performance and lifetime of energy‐storage devices are determined at the interfaces between electrodes, electrolytes, and separators, where ion and charge transfer, parasitic reactions, and mechanical degradation originate within nanometers of the surface. Atomic layer deposition (ALD) and molecular layer deposition (MLD) enable precise engineering of these interfaces through self‐limiting surface reactions that produce conformal coatings with controlled thickness and composition, even on porous electrodes. Although ALD surface chemistry is well established on ideal oxide surfaces, energy‐storage materials present chemically and structurally complex surfaces, on which reaction mechanisms, growth per cycle, and coating function can differ. This Review develops a chemistry–process–structure–function framework that connects surface chemistry, precursor reaction pathways, and nucleation behavior with film structure, ionic transport, charge‐transfer kinetics, redox stability, and mechanical response. We examine growth on oxide, sulfide, metal, polymer, and carbon substrates and relate the films to their functions at cathodes, anodes, solid electrolytes, and separators in Li‐based and beyond‐Li batteries. We further assess process scalability in terms of precursor utilization, throughput, and energy consumption, and discuss in situ monitoring, post‐deposition characterization, and full‐cell test conditions needed to validate coating performance. These relationships are summarized as six design rules presented as a decision flow.
n90eece73f86a: The sluggish dynamic equilibration of ions in ionic liquid electrolytes, particularly under high viscosity conditions, originates from strong interionic interactions and inefficient utilization of charge carrier species. Here, we present a strategic electrolyte design that reconfigures the interionic interaction network and accelerates the dynamic equilibration of charge carriers in AlCl3/EMIC ionic liquid electrolyte. By incorporating an optimized moderator with low polarity and small molecular size, the dynamic redistribution and re-equilibration of charge carriers during cycling are significantly accelerated, while the continuous depletion of effective charge carriers is suppressed. Guided by this principle, the dichloroethane-enabled electrolyte exhibits rapid chloroaluminate equilibration and improved electrode-electrolyte stability. In situ Raman spectroscopy confirms that the moderator promotes reversible AlCl4 − /Al2Cl7 − conversion. As a result, the reorganized AlCl3/EMIC electrolyte suppresses dendrite growth and achieves unprecedented Al anode stability in symmetric cells. Matched with flake graphite cathodes, the full battery capacity increased by 120.7% from 92 to 203 mAh g−1 at 200 mA g−1 after 7000 cycles. This work establishes a dynamic speciation regulation principle for designing ionic liquid electrolytes with fast ion equilibration and provides a pathway toward long-life aluminum-ion batteries.
n3ac0471aeefc: Proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) is among the most promising techniques to provide hydrogen as both energy carrier and feedstock for the chemical industry, due to its compatibility with intermittent renewable electricity sources. However, a major bottleneck in scaling up PEMWE is the limited supply of the anode catalyst Ir. This work shows a novel approach to tailoring ionomer‐free catalyst layers based on custom‐made microporous substrates and two different atomic layer deposition (ALD) processes, both using Ir(EtCp)(CHD) precursor. Thermal ALD using O3${\rm O}_3$ as counter‐reactant yields mostly metallic Ir/IrOx${\rm IrO}_x$ and an electrode Ir loading of 0.21 mg·cm−2${\rm mg}\cdot{\rm cm}^{-2}$. The PEMWE cell‐level performance is comparable to a commercial catalyst‐coated membrane anode despite 7×$7\times$ lower loading, and is maintained over an accelerated durability test equivalent to 600 h of intermittent operation. Moreover, using a low‐loading ALD‐made cathode, the total platinum group metal loading is only 0.24 mg·cm−2${\rm mg}\cdot{\rm cm}^{-2}$. Plasma‐enhanced ALD reduces the Ir loading to 0.04 mg·cm−2${\rm mg}\cdot{\rm cm}^{-2}$ by tailoring the catalyst distribution, however, yields lower‐activity IrO2${\rm IrO}_2$. Finally, direct ALD catalyst deposition needs no ionomer‐bearing ink. The anodes are therefore compatible with various membrane materials, as demonstrated in a CO2${\rm CO}_2$ electrolysis experiment with an anion exchange membrane.
na1555fbe0b71: Aqueous proton batteries are promising alternatives to lithium‐ion batteries owing to their intrinsic safety, low cost, and fast proton transport. However, the small size, high charge density, and strong protonating ability of H+ often perturb host frameworks during repeated insertion/extraction, causing phase transformations, lattice strain, and rapid capacity decay. Herein, we synthesis we report a non‐stoichiometric tunnel‐structured molybdenum oxide, Mo5O14, as a highly reversible proton‐storage electrode. The interconnected tunnel framework enables direct and reversible H3O+ intercalation without phase transition, pronounced structural distortion, or significant volume variation, thereby ensuring excellent structural stability and rapid ion transport. As a result, Mo5O14 delivers a high capacity of 271 mAh g−1 at 1.5 A g−1 (∼5C) and retains 142.2 mAh g−1 even at 300 A g−1 (∼1000C) and sustains stable operation for over 310 000 cycles. When paired with a VHCF cathode, the full cell achieves 73.3 Wh kg−1 and maximum power density of 43.4 kW kg−1, and over 60 000 stable cycles. Furthermore, a flexible interdigital proton micro‐cell array demonstrates rapid‐charge capability, powering a red light‐emitting diode for over 5 min after only 10 s of high‐rate charging.
nd441043fe459: Battery safety remains a critical challenge in the large‐scale deployment of lithium‐ion batteries. While thermal runaway is typically attributed to exothermic reactions involving electrode materials and electrolytes, the contribution of current collectors has been largely overlooked. Here, we demonstrate that the conventionally presumed inert aluminum (Al) current collector engages in intense exothermic reactions with various cathode materials at temperatures exceeding 600°C. This reactivity is catalyzed by fluorides, which disrupt the Al passivation layer, resembling combustion mechanisms observed in Al‐based rocket propellants. The specific heat release from Al oxidation (−22 to −33 kJ g−1) is nearly twice that of the electrolyte (−12 to −16 kJ g−1). Considering that the Al mass is approximately half that of the electrolyte, its theoretical thermal contribution during thermal runaway is comparable to that of the electrolyte. Employing fluorine‐free electrolytes can suppress the propellant‐like reaction. Together with flame‐retardant strategies, the total heat release during thermal runaway can be further reduced, with the measured peak temperatures around pouch cells being effectively suppressed below 400°C. This work uncovers a pervasive yet previously underappreciated high‐energy reaction in batteries and offers new design strategies for improving thermal safety.
n502380544241: Solid‐state MgH2 holds immense promise for high‐capacity hydrogen storage, yet its practical deployment is severely hindered by extreme atmospheric susceptibility and an elusive activated dehydrogenation mechanism. Herein, we report a armor like architectural design featuring asymmetric Ni‐N3 sites and nanoparticles (NPs) co‐decorated within a flexible nitrogen‐doped graphene (NG). Driven by the electronic synergy between the Ni‐N3 sites and the highly active Ni NPs, the NG achieves robust encapsulation of MgH2, providing a rigid size‐exclusion barrier against ambient O2/H2O infiltration. Concurrently, strong electronic interactions between MgH2 and Ni species optimize the MgH2 electronic structure, which further reduces its reactivity toward O2/H2O, enabling the MgH2 to preserve its full capacity even after a 28‐day cumulative air exposure. Furthermore, the encapsulated Ni NPs undergo an in situ reaction to form Mg2Ni nanorivets, which serve as high‐flux interfacial hydrogen pumps, while creating a vital spatial buffer during dynamic cycling, thereby achieving 95% capacity retention over 360 cycles at 300°C. Density functional theory calculations confirm that the electronic hybridization induced by the asymmetric Ni‐N3 sites, Ni NPs, and Mg2Ni nanorivets destabilizes Mg‐H bonds. This multi‐scale engineering of environmental isolation, electronic modulation, and structural riveting presents a robust blueprint for air‐tolerant, fast‐kinetics solid‐state hydrogen storage.
ncafcaf34fab4: All‐solid‐state batteries (ASSBs) with Li‐metal or Li‐metal‐free anodes enable high energy density, yet high‐loading cathodes induce severe mechanical instability, leading to rapid cell failure. Herein, we identify stress accumulation caused by repetitive Li plating/stripping as a critical degradation origin in ASSBs and propose a mechanically adaptive Ag–carbon/carbon nanofiber (CNF) hybrid anode to address this challenge. Operando pressure analysis and mechanical modeling reveal that increasing cathode areal capacity substantially amplifies pressure fluctuations and dynamic mechanical instability, leading to interfacial disruption and short‐circuiting. To mitigate this behavior, the Ag–C interlayer and porous CNF framework were independently customized to provide complementary electrochemical regulation and mechanical buffering functions. The Ag–C layer promotes uniform Li nucleation through Ag–Li alloy‐assisted interfacial regulation, while the porous CNF host accommodates volumetric changes and dissipates stress. Phase‐field modeling and microstructural analyses reveal sequential Ag–Li alloying within the Ag–C interlayer, CNF lithiation and pore filling, and controlled interfacial Li deposition, thereby spatially redistributing volumetric expansion. Consequently, the Ag–C/CNF architecture significantly reduces pressure fluctuation and enables stable cycling over 250 cycles under high‐loading conditions (∼5 mAh cm−2). Furthermore, stable pouch‐cell operation is demonstrated under practical stack pressures of 1 and 2 MPa, highlighting a viable strategy for mechanically robust high‐energy‐density ASSBs.
n82f7cf236446: Lithium–metal batteries are widely regarded as a key direction for next-generation energy storage systems due to high energy density. However, LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2||Li battery systems face severe challenges in practical application, including lithium dendrite growth, interfacial side reactions and structural degradation of high-nickel cathodes. Here, we proposed a versatile modification strategy combining in-situ interfacial transformation with polymer phase regulation to fabricate self-healing solid polymer electrolyte with fast ion transport and stable interface. This strategy not only constructs fast ion channels and suppresses hydrofluoric acid production by in-situ converting Li2CO3 on the Li6.4La3Zr1.4Ta0.6O12 surface into Li2PO3F interfacial layer, but also induces the transition of PVDF from α-phase to high polarity β-phase using ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid to promote lithium salt dissolution and reduce Li+ migration resistance. The as-prepared electrolyte exhibits extended electrochemical voltage windows (5.13 V), high room-temperature ionic conductivity (1.694 mS cm− 1), excellent thermal stability (200°C), high elongation at break (422.6%), and superior cycling stability (89.4% retention after 500 cycles at 1 C). A non-destructive monitoring method based on dp/|dQ| and dT/|dQ| differential signals has been developed to track electrochemical-mechanical-thermal responses during battery operation. This work provides an effective strategy for designing solid polymer electrolytes with high ionic conductivity and interfacial stability.
n7078bb7dc390: Dual electrode‐free (DEF) Zn─MnO2 batteries based on dissolution‐deposition chemistry are promising candidates for large‐scale energy storage due to their lightweight architecture and high theoretical capacity (616 mAh g−1). However, poor interfacial reversibility and the accumulation of “dead manganese” significantly limit their lifespan. Here, we demonstrate a stable DEF battery enabled by an anion‐regulation strategy using a hybrid electrolyte (E‐OA) comprising trifluoromethanesulfonate (OTf−) and acetate (Ac−) ions. At the anode, OTf− facilitates the formation of a fluoride‐rich solid–electrolyte interphase (SEI), effectively suppressing dendrite growth and the hydrogen evolution reaction. At the cathode, the synergistic anionic environment elevates the MnO2 nucleation overpotential, shifting the electrocrystallization pathway to an instantaneous nucleation mode. The kinetically driven growth process traps abundant structural defects, identified as proton‐compensated manganese vacancies (Ruetschi defects). These vacancies lower the thermodynamic energy barrier for Mn─O bond cleavage, thereby ensuring highly reversible dissolution. Consequently, the E‐OA‐based DEF battery achieves exceptional stability for over 7500 cycles at 0.5 mAh cm−2 and sustains 600 cycles at 2 mAh cm−2 (10 mA cm−2), demonstrating superior rate capability and versatility in both flow and gel battery configurations. This work provides a transformative strategy for high‐energy aqueous batteries via tailored anion chemistry and kinetics‐driven defect engineering.
nd19116b8c808: Alkaline seawater electrolysis is a promising route for sustainable hydrogen production, yet its practical implementation is severely constrained by chloride‐induced corrosion and limited anode durability during the oxygen evolution reaction (OER). Here, we develop synergistic fluoride‐management, defect‐engineering, and polymer‐interfacial‐protection strategy for NiFe‐LDH anodes, enabling kilo‐hour‐scale operation at ampere‐level current densities in natural seawater. A custom‐designed microwave‐assisted method produces fluoride‐protected NiFe layered double hydroxide on nickel foam (F‑NiFe‑LDHMW/NF). The electrode is subsequently tailored through controlled Zn depletion to generate an evolving cation‐deficient environment, followed by electropolymerization of calmagite to construct a multifunctional poly(calmagite) (poly(CM)) interfacial layer. The optimized F‑NiFeZnvac‑LDHMW@CM/NF anode delivered exceptional stable operation for 1000 h in simulated seawater and 1650 h in natural seawater at a commercial‐scale current density of 1000 mA cm−2. Mechanistic analyses combining stage‐resolved characterization, electrolyte analysis, and DFT reveal complementary intrinsic and extrinsic stabilization mechanisms: F− regulation and the evolving cation‐defect environment modify the structural and electronic state of NiFe‐LDH, while poly(CM) suppresses Cl− access and adsorption and delays interfacial corrosion. During prolonged electrolysis, F− undergoes dynamic redistribution and gradual leaching, accompanied by controlled catalyst reconstruction rather than catastrophic structural degradation. This multilevel stabilization strategy can be a step forward toward practical seawater electrolysis.
na22b2c2f9f6a: Modulating the electronic structure and interfacial wettability of cathode catalysts is crucial for enhancing intrinsic activity and broadening triple‐phase interfaces for oxygen reduction reactions (ORR) in zinc−air batteries (ZABs), yet achieving their synergistic regulation faces a big challenge. Herein, an N/F source modulation strategy is proposed to synthesize porous carbon nanofibers anchored with MnF2 nanocrystals and N/F heteroatoms (MnF2/NF−CNF). The unique interconnected fibrous and hierarchical porous architecture, together with tailored MnF2 embedding and N/F doping, achieves an optimal balance between activity and wettability regulation. Excellent ORR performance with a high half‐wave potential of 0.87 V vs. RHE and limiting current density of 6.34 mA cm−2 is achieved, outperforming Pt/C and most previously reported Mn‐based/heteroatom‐doped systems. Theoretical and experimental analyses reveal surface N dopants as active sites, with MnF2 modulating p‐orbital configuration, refining ORR pathways. Meanwhile, surface F dopants, in synergy with the porous architecture, regulate wettability, equilibrate electrolyte/oxygen transport, and substantially extend triple‐phase reaction interfaces. The assembled ZAB delivers an exceptional peak power density of 181.5 mW cm−2 with high specific capacity, rate capability, and cycling stability. This work deciphers the regulatory mechanism balancing catalytic activity and interfacial wettability, proving a versatile strategy for developing advanced ORR electrocatalysts in ZABs.
ncb86ebd59219: Lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs) are central to modern energy storage, yet evaluating their internal states under extreme thermal fluctuations remains a critical challenge. Here we present a non‐destructive evaluation framework that leverages the quasi‐static component (QSC) of nonlinear ultrasonic guided waves. By integrating an operando electro‐acoustic‐thermal platform, we isolate temperature‐induced artefacts from intrinsic acoustic signals. This statistical compensation enables the precise, simultaneous prediction of state of charge (SOC) and state of charge relative to nominal capacity (SOCN) across a wide temperature span (−10°C to 40°C). Furthermore, in situ multidimensional characterization maps these ultrasonic signatures to temperature‐dependent mechanics and irreversible capacity fade mechanisms. Ultimately, this unified framework provides a scalable, quantitative diagnostic tool for reliable energy systems operating under extreme environments.
n70d8fc3949b3: Magnesium‐based hydrogen storage materials exhibit great application potential, but high operating temperature and slow kinetics hinder their large‐scale utilization. Here, the amorphous‐carbon‐stabilized Mg particles decorated with sub‐2 nm ZrO2 nanoclusters are reported, which were in situ fabricated via ball milling of commercial Mg powder, acetone (ACE), and zirconium acetylacetonate (Zr(acac)4). The optimized Mg‐ACE‐1 wt.% Zr composite achieves rapid hydrogen absorption of 4.25 wt.% at 30°C within 60 min and exhibits high cycling stability with nearly no H2 capacity fading after 40 cycles at 300°C under 30 bar H2. Notably, the Mg‐ACE‐1 wt.% Zr sample enables reversible hydrogenation at room temperature and dehydrogenation at high temperature, achieving better energy efficiency than conventional thermally driven MgH2 and showing promise for coupling with renewable hydrogen production. Interfacial characterizations and DFT calculations confirm that the in situ formed ZrO2/Mg interface accelerates H2 adsorption, dissociation, and diffusion.
n7b3bc9c257d4: Passive cooling textiles for buildings must do more than reflect sunlight; they must also buffer transient heat under real outdoor conditions. Here we report a continuous coaxial wet‐spinning strategy for fabricating a microencapsulated phase‐change material (mPCM)‐integrated radiative‐cooling meta‐fabric (MFRP), consisting of a thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU)/hexagonal boron nitride (h‐BN)/barium sulfate (BaSO4) photon‐regulating sheath and a TPU/mPCM latent‐heat core. The spatially separated architecture integrates broadband solar reflection, atmospheric‐window emission, and phase‐change thermal buffering within one fiber platform. The optimized meta‐fabric shows high solar reflectance (95.44%), strong atmospheric‐window emissivity (96.21%), and a melting enthalpy of 102.28 J/g. In a representative sunny‐day test, MFRP reduced the chamber temperature by up to 10.36°C relative to the blank control; three‐day cement‐panel measurements further yielded an average peak‐temperature reduction of 7.51°C ± 2.17°C relative to bare cement. Energy‐balance analysis and climate‐scale modelling further indicate promising cooling‐energy and carbon‐reduction potential in hot and cooling‐dominated regions. These results establish wet‐spun radiative cooling/phase‐change material meta‐fabrics as continuously processable exterior textile candidates for passive building thermal management.
n12d6e019c6b7: Bio‐based optical glasses exhibit great potential but remain elusive. This study presents a biodegradable glass derived from dehydroabietic acid (DA‐Glass) via a melt‐annealing process. The material transitions from crystalline to a stable amorphous state, exhibiting optical transparency, thermal stability, hydrophobicity and superior mechanical properties. Molecular simulations reveal that annealing enhances the hydrogen‐bonding network and introduces weak interactions, optimizing intermolecular forces and improving thermodynamic stability. DA‐Glass exhibits photoactivated room‐temperature phosphorescence (RTP), enabled by UV‐induced oxygen consumption and restricted molecular motion facilitated by cyclohexane units. The RTP is reversibly modulated by UV exposure and displays stability in water. Applications in smart anti‐counterfeiting, information encryption, and recyclable 3D printing are demonstrated, highlighting the potential for sustainable optical technologies.
n265cffc65082: Owing to poor lymphocyte infiltration, abundant immunosuppressive cells, and abnormal metabolism, the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (ITME) remains a primary challenge for effective cancer immunotherapy. A coordination engineering strategy was employed in this study to design an intramolecular junction polymer CuBr‐dptz‐CuCl‐dptz (dptz = 3,6‐di(pyridin‐4‐yl)‐1,2,4,5‐tetrazine), unlocking three synergistic antitumor cascades, IDO1 biobromination, cuproptosis, and apoptosis, within an integrated single material platform. The pyridinic nitrogen atoms of dptz coordinate to Cu(I) centers bridged by alternating Cu–Br and Cu─Cl chains. The intramolecular junction optimizes charge separation and d‐band centers, and together with electron‐withdrawing dptz stabilizes a high Cu+ fraction (∼80.33%). Density functional theory calculations identified low‐energy pathways for hydrogen peroxide dissociation to hydroxyl radical and its conversion to oxygen, accounting for the high catalytic efficiency. Released Cu+ potentiates cuproptosis by boosting cellular tricarboxylic acid cycle dependence and triggering dihydrolipoamide S‐acetyltransferase oligomerization and proteotoxic stress. Meanwhile, liberated Br− converts enzymatically to HBrO to realize functional IDO1 biobromination. Combined with apoptosis, the three‐pathway cascade synergy enhances lymphocyte infiltration, promotes anti‐tumor M1 macrophage polarization, and remodels ITME metabolism, ultimately activating robust systemic antitumor immunity. This work establishes intramolecular junction coordination polymers as a versatile single‐platform paradigm for multi‐mechanism synergistic cancer immunotherapy.
nf605c607dbd2: Conductive hydrogels are promising for wearable sensors in human motion detection owing to their skin-like softness, strain sensitivity, and biocompatibility. However, their practical application in aqueous environments is severely hindered by swelling-induced mechanical deterioration and electrical instability. Herein, a tough, anti-swelling conductive hydrogel for underwater sensing is reported, enabled by a “silk nanofiber-mediated controlled-swelling-locking” (SNF-CSL) strategy. In this approach, silk nanofibers (SNFs) are incorporated into a polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) matrix, followed by controlled swelling in a pyrrole solution to facilitate uniform monomer diffusion and adsorption onto SNFs. Subsequent ammonium persulfate-initiated oxidative polymerization induces in situ formation and structural locking of a continuous polypyrrole (PPy) network, effectively stabilizing the swollen hydrogel configuration. The resulting PVA/SNF/PPy hydrogel exhibits skin-matching Young's modulus (130.5 kPa), exceptional toughness (0.46 MJ m− 3), and excellent anti-swelling stability (equilibrium swelling ratio of 3.9%). As a strain sensor, the hydrogel demonstrates high sensitivity (gauge factor of 2.14), fast response (20 ms), and durable performance over 1000 cycles, while enabling Morse code communication under aquatic environments. This work establishes a simple and broadly applicable strategy for designing robust anti-swelling hydrogel sensors tailored for aquatic applications.
nb68235da8a11: Anode‐free lithium metal batteries promise high energy density. However, fluorinated electrolytes raise sustainability concerns. Herein, we develop a fully fluorine‐free interfacial strategy by coupling a cross‐linked vinylene carbonate‐N,N′‐methylenebisacrylamide artificial solid electrolyte interphase (ASEI) on Cu current collectors with a fluorine‐free electrolyte to regulate both lithium deposition and subsequent SEI formation. This combination offers an alternative to interfacial stabilization using fluorinated SEI‐forming components or alloy‐forming interlayers. The ASEI possesses strong Li‐ASEI interactions and enhanced lithiophilicity, thereby enabling homogeneous and compact Li deposition with reduced growth overpotential. Furthermore, the ASEI induces the formation of a conformal, mechanically robust, inorganic‐rich SEI containing Li2O and Li3N, leading to improved interfacial stability and the reversibility of Li plating/stripping. Consequently, the ASEI‐modified current collector delivers markedly improved full‐cell performance. The prelithiated LFP||ASEI‐Cu full cell achieves stable cycling over 350 cycles with a capacity retention of 84.5% at 25°C, while the prelithiated NCM811||ASEI‐Cu full cell delivers a reversible capacity of 146.8 mAh g−1 after 100 cycles with a capacity retention of 86.6% at 25°C. This work demonstrates the potential of fluorine‐free interfacial engineering for anode‐free lithium metal batteries, while further improvements in lithium‐inventory retention and high‐current‐density operation remain necessary for practical implementation.
n82a24e0698c5: The accurate detection of salt concentration and ionic composition is vital for chemical manufacturing and environmental monitoring. However, existing portable detectors are typically reliant on an external power supply and are unable to simultaneously measure a wide range of concentrations and provide reliable discrimination of key cations, including K+, Na+, Ca2+, and Mg2+. To address these challenges, we report a tribo-chemoelectric coupled nanogenerator (TCNG) for self-powered dual-modal sensing of salt solutions. Through a simple structural modification of a conventional droplet-based triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG), which involves exposing a 10 mm segment of the lower electrode at the bottom edge of the device, effective coupling between triboelectric and chemoelectric signals is realized within a single-structure, single-loop configuration. The resulting device enables highly sensitive and broad-range concentration detection (0–3500 mmol·L− 1) with a sensitivity of −500.76 µA·(mol·L− 1)− 1 below 0.5 mol·L− 1, while achieving 92.5% accuracy in multi-ion recognition. This work provides a feasible strategy for self-powered electrochemical sensing and offers a promising route for high-performance, on-site salt analysis within industrial and environmental settings.
n3a49ef08bb07: Chiral small‐molecule modification provides an interfacial route for functionalizing sliding ferroelectrics. Herein, we systematically investigate four chiral molecules adsorbed on h‐BN, 3R‐MoS2, and γ‐InSe. Across 48 adsorption configurations, the polarization changes range from −27.5% to +13.7%, with a median absolute variation of 10.0%, while 35 configurations show changes within ±15%. The polarization retains its original Up and Down sign in all relaxed configurations examined. The oppositely polarized states remain connected by finite‐energy sliding pathways, although molecular adsorption modifies the barrier heights and endpoint energy asymmetry. Bader charge and charge density difference analyses reveal limited net charge transfer and predominantly localized electronic redistribution near the interface. The relationship between the interfacial charge‐transfer dipole and the Berry‐phase polarization modulation depends on the substrate. These results demonstrate that stacking‐dependent polar states remain present in the investigated chiral‐molecule sliding‐ferroelectric interfaces, providing a microscopic basis for molecular functionalization of sliding ferroelectrics.
n372cab6c8118: We provide the first characterization of Magnesium–Vacancy (MgV) color centers under hydrostatic high‐pressure conditions. The luminescent defects were fabricated upon ion implantation into a diamond anvil, which was subsequently assembled into a Diamond Anvil Cell (DAC). The photoluminescence study, performed at 87 K, reveals a blueshift of the Zero‐Phonon Line (ZPL) induced by increasing compressive stress, with a slope of 2.1 meV/GPa. A theoretical model of the electronic level structure of the MgV−${\rm MgV}^-$ center has been developed to support the experimental findings, showing good compatibility with the measured shift. In addition, the optical response of MgV−${\rm MgV}^-$ centers was investigated upon temperature variations.The results obtained further confirm the previously reported temperature‐induced shift of the ZPL, which undergoes a redshift during cool down, in the opposite direction with respect to that observed in other color centers explored under changing temperature. The theoretical calculations reproduce this temperature dependence as well, complementing the characterization of MgV−${\rm MgV}^-$ centers as temperature sensors. These results are discussed in relation to existing studies on MgV−${\rm MgV}^-$ centers, expanding the understanding of this recently discovered quantum emitter and unlocking its employment as an all‐optical sensor of pressure and temperature.
n579ea35d2e6c: The von Neumann memory wall severely restricts the performance of traditional computing systems, and memristors have emerged as premier candidates for neuromorphic computing by virtue of their ability to integrate storage and computation functions. However, conventional HfOx memristors suffer from abrupt resistive switching and lack of intrinsic self‐protection, limiting their synaptic emulation performance. Herein, a novel nonvolatile HfOx/MoSx/HfOx trilayer heterostructure memristor with intrinsic self‐compliance and analog conductance modulation was constructed. The optimized device exhibits stable cycling endurance, multilevel retention stability and fast response speed, and achieves linear and symmetric conductance potentiation and depression. Furthermore, the proposed memristor successfully emulates diverse biological synaptic plasticities, including EPSC, IPSC, PPF, and PPD. A constructed neural network based on this device achieves a high handwritten digit recognition accuracy of 93.84% on the MNIST dataset, with excellent noise immunity and device variation robustness. Furthermore, the memristor acts as an irreplaceable physical entropy source for zero‐trust XOR‐based image encryption, generating ciphertext images with near‐optimal information entropy reaching 7.978 bits. This work presents a feasible MoSx interlayer modification strategy to optimize high‐performance artificial synapses on oxide memristors, enabling co‐integration of neuromorphic computing and hardware security.
n98ca32a16d38: Human skin encodes pressure and stretch through the motion of ions, a principle soft iontronics reproduce but rarely on sustainable terms. Additive manufacturing has lifted ionogels from cast slabs into architected sensors, yet this progress rests on fossil‐derived acrylates, because plant‐based networks expel the polar ionic liquids that carry charge. Here we print an ionogel whose matrix exceeds 80% bio‐based carbon while stably hosting a hydrophobic imidazolium ionic liquid, resolving a long‐standing compatibility barrier. A single monomer ratio tunes stiffness 30 fold (9 to 0.3 MPa) and nearly doubles ionic conductivity to 0.53 mS cm−1. Printed as gyroid lattices, the material senses pressure capacitively and strain resistively through separable channels: near‐incompressibility pins the gauge factor near 2 irrespective of geometry, whereas the lattice amplifies low‐pressure sensitivity eightfold and accelerates the strain response 4.6‐fold. On the body, both modes track joint motion with complementary signatures. Chemistry and printed architecture thus act as independent levers for renewable iontronic skin.
n350d8e1568fa: Aqueous zinc–iodine batteries have attracted considerable attention owing to their environmental friendliness and high theoretical capacity. However, the iodine cathode inevitably suffers from the formation of soluble polyiodides during charge/discharge processes, resulting in active material loss and heavy shuttle effects. In this manuscript, asymmetrically coordinated dysprosium (Dy‐N3O5) single atoms and clusters (DySA+C–NC) were designed and synthesized through high‐temperature annealing of its ZIF precursor. The optimized DySA+C–NC contains highly dispersed Dy‐N/O single atom sites together with Dy cluster sites, which collectively strengthen polyiodide confinement and accelerate reversible iodine conversion. In addition, the nitrogen‐doped carbon host offers continuous electron transport pathways and pore‐confined spaces, contributing to electrolyte wetting, ion diffusion and iodine utilization. In situ Raman, in situ UV–vis and DFT calculation support that the Dy single atoms/clusters effectively confines iodine species and promotes rapid polyiodide conversion. Particularly, PDOS analysis reveals that the overlap between I‐5p and Dy‐5d states enhances interfacial electronic coupling for iodine activation, while the localized Dy‐4f states regulate the electronic environment of Dy centers. The DySA+C–NC@I2 cathode delivers a high discharge capacity of 200.46 mAh g−1 at 5 A g−1 after 25 000 cycles. This work provides a strategy for the design of rare‐earth single atoms/cluster for long‐life aqueous zinc–iodine batteries.
n0ee4b9a1ea3e: Proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) is constrained by the sluggish oxygen evolution reaction (OER) kinetics and the intrinsic activity-stability trade-off of Ir-based anodes. In this work, an atomically Sm-doped Ir/IrO2 heterointerface catalyst is fabricated via a facile ligand-assisted foaming strategy. The optimized catalyst achieves overpotentials of 246 mV for OER and 19 mV for HER at 10 mA cm−2 in an acidic electrolyte, with a remarkable mass activity of 835.91 A gIr −1 at 1.53 V and long-term stability for 500 h. In PEM electrolyzer, the catalyst delivers 1 A cm−2 at 1.70 V and maintains stability for 325 h, demonstrating great promise for practical acidic water splitting. Combining in-situ spectroscopy and DFT calculations reveals that Sm, with its unique 4f electronic configuration, serves as an electron donor to downshift the d-band center of Ir and strengthen the Ir–O covalent bond. Such electronic modulation tends to the AEM pathway and optimizes the adsorption energetics of oxygenated intermediates. The rate-determining step shifts from *OOH formation to *OH dehydrogenation, thereby reducing the reaction free-energy and mitigating irreversible Ir overoxidation. This work establishes lanthanide doping at heterointerfaces as a powerful strategy to break the activity-stability trade-off in acidic water splitting.
n4fa45386f128: Hybrid ultramicroporous materials (HUMs) are comprised of combinations of inorganic and organic linker ligands as exemplified by the prototypal pcu topology variant [Zn(pyrazine)2(SiF6)]n, SIFSIX-3-Zn, and its recently reported first-generation derivatives [M(3,3’-bipyridine)2(SiF6)] n (M = Cu, Zn). Herein, we report the synthesis, structure, and sorption properties of a second-generation family of HUMs of general formula [M(3,3’-bipyridine)2(NbOF5)] n , NbOFFIVE-3,3'-bpy-M, M = Co, Ni, Cu, Zn. The four HUMs are structurally characterized by single crystal x-ray diffraction, revealing the expected pcu topology of the isostructural as-synthesized phases. All variants initially crystallized in large-pore (lp) phases with water molecules occupying 1D channels. Upon dehydration, Cu and Zn transformed from water-loaded lp phases into narrow-pore (np) guest-free phases, whereas Co and Ni retained their lp structures after desorption. Water vapor sorption isotherms (300 K) revealed stepped isotherms corresponding to structural transformations (np→lp) for Cu and Zn, and rare examples of induced-fit (lp→np→lp) from guest-free lp to np to water-loaded lp phases for Co and Ni. The NbOFFIVE-3,3'-bpy-M family exhibits uncommon examples of metal-dependent dynamic behavior in HUMs.
n2d3b283cea8a: Mechanically interlocked structures (MIS) provide a powerful platform for creating advanced materials with unprecedented topological architectures. Nevertheless, current related studies have predominantly focused on the construction of MIS with single topological motifs, and the integration of multiple topologies into a single MIS remains a grand challenge. Herein, we harness ligand conformational constraints to regulate the flexible coordination behavior of alkali metal ions, enabling the construction of a multi‐topologically superposed mechanically interlocked polymer (MIP) featuring the unprecedented incorporation of four distinct topological motifs. This incorporation imparts MIP with exceptional mechanical strength and efficient Na+ transport capability. As an artificial solid electrolyte interphase (ASEI) for sodium metal batteries, MIP delivers remarkable ultralong cycling stability, maintaining 87.8% capacity retention after 10 000 cycles at 20 C. This work breaks the boundaries of conventional MIS by enabling the creation of multi‐topologically superposed MIS, thereby unveiling new topological landscapes and opening unexplored opportunities for advanced functions.
nc29dbfd7623e: Potassium dihydrogen phosphate is well-known to exhibit ferroelectricity, while ammonium dihydrogen phosphate is an antiferroelectric material, with both of them exhibiting a phase transition to paraelectric phase below room temperature. In this work, we report the synthesis and room-temperature ferroelectric behavior of an aminophosphonium dihydrogen phosphate of formula, [{P(NHPh)4(H2PO4)·(CH3OH)0.5] (TAPDP·(CH3OH)0.5 ) that exhibits a three-dimensional pillared-layered hydrogen bonding network. (TAPDP·(CH3OH)0.5 crystallizes in the polar monoclinic P21 space group, and its non-centrosymmetric structure was confirmed by second-harmonic generation (SHG) measurements. The ferroelectric behavior was further verified through polarization–electric field (P–E) loop measurements, with a saturation polarization of 21.40 µC cm−2. Structural analysis combined with preliminary density functional theory calculations indicates a ferrielectric-type ordering in which the adjacent layers exhibit different polarization directions but with unequal dipole moments. Furthermore, the electromechanical energy-harvesting properties of TAPDP·(CH3OH)0.5 were explored in its composites with the polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) polymer. The 10 wt% TAPDP·(CH3OH)0.5–PDMS device exhibited a maximum peak-to-peak open-circuit voltage (𝑉oc) of 10.69 ± 0.04 V and the output work efficiency parameter (OWE) of 9.63%. Owing to the superior signal sensitivity of this device, a contact-type sensor was developed to measure a motor's revolutions per minute (RPM) at both low and high speeds.
n01c790c98d5d: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are appealing photocatalyst platforms because of their structural designability and tunable optoelectronic properties. However, the traditional strategy of extending π‐conjugation to improve light absorption often increases exciton binding energy and suppresses charge separation, creating a trade‐off that limits catalytic performance. Here, we introduce a conjugation‐interruption strategy for the first time to construct efficient COF‐based photocatalysts, where methylene (sp3) bridges are incorporated into one‐dimensional (1D) framework backbones to moderately disrupt long‐range conjugation, localize electrons and reduce exciton binding energy. Schiff base condensation of the 4‐connected thiadiazole‐containing tetra‐aldehyde with 2‐connected angular diamine precursors consisting of naphthyl, phenyl, and methylene bridges afforded BT‐NDA‐COF, BT‐TDA‐COF, and BT‐MDA‐COF, respectively. BT‐MDA‐COF with the weakest conjugation, exhibits the longest fluorescence lifetime (1.57 ns) and the lowest exciton binding energy (63.21 meV), clearly outperforming its fully conjugated counterparts (BT‐TDA‐COF and BT‐NDA‐COF). Combined experimental and theoretical analyses reveal that the methylene bridges induce structural distortion and weaken exciton confinement, thereby promoting charge separation. This superior charge separation enables gram‐scale photocatalytic synthesis of bioactive 2,3‐dihydrobenzofurans with 98% yield, demonstrating the practical potential of conjugation interruption in COFs for green, high‐efficiency photocatalytic organic synthesis.
na6eaf5124441: Improving the durability of platinum (Pt)-based catalysts for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) remains a central challenge in the commercialization of proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs), yet simple and effective indicators to guide the rational design of highly stable Pt-based catalysts are still lacking. Herein, we identify initial electrochemically active surface area (ECSA) and dry proton accessibility (DPA) as two key indicators for unraveling cathodic Pt/C catalyst degradation. Systematic studies on a library of Pt/C catalysts with a wide range of initial ECSA (49–114 m2 gPt −1) and DPA (27%–91%) reveal clear relationships between these two indicators and ECSA loss: at a comparable DPA, ECSA loss decreases significantly with the reduction in initial ECSA; at a similar initial ECSA, lower DPA effectively mitigates ECSA loss; and the influence of DPA on ECSA loss becomes increasingly prominent as initial ECSA decreases. Regression analysis further clarifies the respective roles of these two indicators: initial ECSA is the dominant factor associated with ECSA loss within the catalyst library, while DPA further modulates degradation depending on the initial ECSA level. These findings suggest that catalyst durability can be improved by prioritizing the reduction of initial ECSA, with further benefits achieved by lowering DPA.
n7a729d381b09: The green and facile protocol for the tunable transformation of alicyclic amines is meaningful due to the immense importance of the functionalized azaheterocycles in pharmaceuticals. In this work, electrochemically selective synthesis of α‐cyano amines and cyclic amidines from the reaction of saturated cyclic amines with TMSN3 is developed. Using thiomorpholines as amine substrates, the regioselective cleavage of C(sp3)─S bond, followed by recombination and cyanation, enables the construction of α‐cyano thiazolidines via a ring contraction process. In the presence of sodium sulfinate, alicyclic amines undergo cycloaddition, N2 extrusion, hydride transfer, and sulfonylation to give sulfonyl amidines. Notable features of the methods developed herein include simple and broad tertiary/secondary cyclic amine substrates, diverse novel transformations, catalyst‐free and external oxidant‐free conditions. Importantly, these reaction systems are amenable to the late‐stage functionalization of complex targets containing basic N‐heterocyclic moieties that are prevalent in medicinally active agents. In addition, electrolysis of the N‐aryl sulfonyl amidine triggers further cleavage of the N─S bond and coupling of C(sp2)─N bond to provide fused amines.
n8d1df99a8d34: The precise control of liquid motion with light is fundamental to advancing next‐generation microfluidic devices and microreactors. Fluoroalkylated photoswitches that combine low surface tension with photoinduced reversible solid‑to‑liquid transitions would be ideal for this purpose, yet they have remained unrealized because fluoroalkyl chains typically suppress solid‑state photoisomerization. Here, we overcome this limitation by designing fluoroalkylated azobenzenes that exhibit low surface tension and photoinduced reversible solid‑to‑liquid transitions. This dual functionality stems from tailored molecular and crystalline structures that enable efficient trans‐cis photoisomerization in the solid state. The fluoroalkylated azobenzenes function as non‑lubricating solids in their trans form and become liquid lubricants upon photoconversion to their cis form. By infusing them into microstructured substrates, we create surfaces that can be optically switched between a liquid‐pinning state and a slippery state. This photoswitching capability enables the on‑demand creation and reconfiguration of guiding pathways to control the sliding of various liquids. This work establishes spatiotemporally controlled lubrication via photoinduced reversible solid‑to‐liquid transitions as a new mechanism for designing microfluidics, microreactors, and adaptive surfaces.
n3ccbfea61cbf: Integrating the “magic methyl” effect and deuterium kinetic isotope effect, trideuteromethyl (CD3) modification is a robust strategy for pharmaceutical development. Accordingly, the development of cost‐effective and practical methods to install CD3 moieties into drug‐like molecules is highly desirable. Herein, we develop a reusable heterogeneous Pd‐catalyzed trideuteromethylation of arylboron esters, with D2O serving as the sole deuterium source. Methylthianthrenium salts (TT‐Me) act as key precursors, undergoing facile H/D exchange to in situ produce CD3 synthons for efficient one‐pot cross‐coupling with arylboron esters. This protocol features outstanding functional group compatibility and an extraordinarily broad substrate applicability. It enables the trideuteromethylation of diverse biologically relevant scaffolds, as well as the modular two‐step synthesis of aryl‐CD3 skeletons starting from commercially available aryl chlorides, phenols, anilines, and benzoic acids. It also facilely affords 13CH3/13CD3 dual‐labeled analogs for pharmaceutical and analytical use. Combined with C─H borylation, this one‐pot platform achieves direct trideuteromethylation of inert aryl C─H bonds, allowing divergent installation of two site‐specific CD3 moieties into lidocaine isotopologues. Mechanistic investigations reveal a surface‐mediated heterogeneous pathway, where K2CO3 dually activates TT‐Me and arylboron esters. This work offers a practical, scalable and sustainable route for constructing aryl–CD3 isotopic architectures.
nb14dc5d7663c: Achieving high selectivity in photocatalytic CO2 reduction remains a fundamental challenge, as competing pathways share similar thermodynamic potentials but differ in their intermediate adsorption behavior. Here we introduce a heterometallic polarization strategy based on bimetallic metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), where asymmetric charge redistribution between distinct metal centers tailors the local electronic structure and modulates CO* binding energetics. Taking MIL‐88A(Fe/Ni) as a model system, the incorporation of Ni induces intermetallic electronic coupling, creating polarized Fe─Ni sites that synergistically enhance CO2 activation and charge transfer. As a result, MIL‐88A(Fe/Ni2.5) achieves a CO production rate of 1517.4 µmol g−1 h−1—10.8 times higher than MIL‐88A(Fe/Ni0)—with a selectivity of 97.9%. Increasing the Ni content strengthens CO* adsorption, thereby steering the reaction from CO evolution to deep hydrogenation toward CH4. MIL‐88A(Fe/Ni7.5) delivers a CH4 production rate of 255.0 µmol g−1 h−1—28.3 and 14.5 times that of MIL‐88A(Fe/Ni0) and MIL‐88A(Fe/Ni2.5), respectively—with an electron selectivity of 81.3%. These results demonstrate that heterometallic polarization provides a powerful design principle for regulating intermediates and achieving tunable product selectivity in photocatalytic CO2 conversion.
n813f89113899: Photocatalytic CO2 reduction to hydrocarbon fuels represents a sustainable route toward carbon neutrality, yet selective and efficient C2 production remains a formidable challenging due to the high thermodynamic barrier and sluggish C–C coupling kinetics. In this study, we report a hydroxyl (–OH)‐rich TiO2 photocatalyst decorated with Cu single atoms (SAs) (Cu/HTO) that addresses this challenge through synergistic active site—surface group engineering. The electronic interplay between surface –OH groups and Cu SAs promotes charge separation and strengthens CO2 chemisorption/activation at Cu sites, facilitating *CO intermediates formation and subsequent protonation for selective C2H5OH and CO prodution. Under sacrificial agent free conditions, Cu/HTO delivers CO at 90.1 µmol g−1 h−1 with 88.3% yield‐based selectivity in a gas–solid (GS) system. Notably, in a gas–liquid–solid (GLS) system with water supplying abundant protons, Cu/HTO efficiently yields C2H5OH at 361.5 µmol g−1 h−1 with 99.4% yield‐based selectivity, which is related to Cu2+ sites stabilized *CO intermediates thermodynamically favoring C–C coupling and the surface –OH groups mediated proton transfer kinetically facilitating multistep protonation. This work not only establishes a high‐performance and low‐cost photocatalyst for CO2‐to‐C2 conversion but also provides a rational design paradigm for engineering single‐atom–surface‐group synergy in solar fuel synthesis.
nf8711d26f986: Pre-catalyst reconstruction fundamentally governs the local structure and solid–liquid interface of the derived phase, significantly influencing water electrolysis performance. However, fully unlocking the intrinsic potential of pre-catalysts remain a persistent bottleneck, as conventional electrolytes cannot functionalize the interface during reconstruction. Herein, we propose an interfacial carbonate-dominated activation strategy to simultaneously tune the derived NiOOH structure and its interface, enabling efficient oxygen evolution reaction (OER). Using Ca-Ni3S2 as the model pre-catalyst and K2CO3 to replace KOH as the reconstruction electrolyte, the carbonate-dominated interface kinetically and thermodynamically impedes the transformation of Ni3S2 into NiOOH, enabling surface-confined reconstruction at elevated potential that preserves the interior Ni3S2 while forming the functionalized NiOOH phase on the surface. This functionalized surface, induced by the retained CO3 2− from reconstruction, optimizes the electron distribution, interface water framework, and establishes a stable buffer layer, facilitating water oxidation and suppressing NiOOH deactivation. Resultantly, the reconstructed catalyst (Ca-Ni3S2-RC) shows an overpotential of only 261 mV at 100 mA cm−2, a remarkable reduction of 198 mV compared to its KOH-reconstructed counterpart. Integrated into an alkaline water electrolyzer (AWE), Ca-Ni3S2-RC presents a competitive energy consumption of 4.21 kWh m−3 H2 to deliver 4000 A m−2 over 900 h, highlighting its promise for industrial applicability.
nf60439f5c6d8: Rapid advances in A-DA'D-A fused-ring electron acceptors have significantly boosted organic solar cells (OSCs), yet non-radiative energy loss (ΔE 3) remains a persistent bottleneck, and reliance on single electron-deficient cores limits further molecular diversification. Herein, we report CBT-4F, a novel acceptor featuring a double electron-deficient bis([1,2,5]thiadiazolo)[3,4-c:3′,4′-g]carbazole (CBT) core constructed via stepwise intramolecular Cadogan reductive cyclization. This synthetic strategy circumvents the challenges of carrying multiple nitro groups through key cross-coupling steps and offers an extensible route to multi-electron-deficient-core acceptors. Compared with the benchmark acceptor Y6, CBT-4F exhibits extended π-conjugation, increased backbone curvature, a lower average molecular electrostatic potential, and a distinct packing motif. These coupled molecular and solid-state characteristics, together with optimized blend morphology and recombination behavior, are associated with significantly suppressed ΔE 3 in PM6:CBT-4F devices (0.220 vs. 0.262 eV for PM6:Y6). Benefiting from a wider photovoltaic bandgap and reduced ΔE 3, PM6:CBT-4F achieves a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 19.02% with a high open-circuit voltage (V OC) of 0.923 V, substantially outperforming the PM6:Y6 counterpart (17.63%, 0.834 V). Furthermore, incorporating CBT-4F as a third component into the PM6:BTP-eC9 system boosts the ternary PCE to 20.57%. This work establishes CBT-4F as a high-performance molecular platform and expands synthetic accessibility to multi-electron-deficient-core acceptors.
n55cf9bfa3ed3: Metabolic reprogramming in malignant cells drives tumor progression and impairs immunotherapy efficacy, highlighting the urgent need for synergistic metabolic‐immunotherapy. However, the pharmacokinetic disparity and systemic toxicities pose significant challenges on this synergy. We develop a tumor‐preferential, multifunctional DNA nano‐regulator assembled on a DNA origami‐based framework with two functional layers for the integration of immune cues and metabolic modulation at the tumor‐immune interface. The inner layer is precisely functionalized with anti‐CD3/CD28/PD‐L1 antibodies and glutamine synthetase, enabling in situ T‐cell engagement, PD‐L1 blockade, and metabolic environment improvement. The outer layer combines albumin‐binding domains with pH‐responsive i‐motif switches to form a pH‐sensitive albumin coating in vivo, which shields the inner antibodies during systemic circulation and specifically exposes them within the tumoral acidic microenvironment. In the xenograft and syngeneic mouse models, the regulator‐mediated broad remodeling of the intratumoral immune and metabolic landscapes results in enhanced T‑cell infiltration and activation, potent tumor‐growth suppression, and a favorable safety profile. This study combines metabolic intervention with immunotherapy by integrating the synergism and tumor preference of therapies.
n0d88162674b5: In a rhenium‐doped SrZrxIr1−xO3 perovskite, high‐valent Re stabilizes low‐valent iridium active sites against overoxidation during acidic oxygen evolution. n396dfd82ce10: Gaining control over chromophore-functionalized multicomponent architectures sets the stage to construct modular libraries of tunable emitters, light-harvesting complexes, and photo-redox catalysts. Computations suggest that different extents of vibrational relaxation of the donors’ S1 states enable excitation back-transfer in only one of the two cages and propose a Förster-type mechanism for it, indicating that the energy-transfer pathway can be selected through the choice of the co-ligand. Hence, the encapsulation of a chiral guest bestows both cages with circular dichroism (CD) and circularly polarized luminescence (CPL).

n8da6a96460eb: Solid-state batteries pairing lithium metal anodes with inorganic solid electrolytes promise a step change in energy density, but during charging at practical rates lithium dendrites penetrate the solid electrolyte, short-circuiting the cell. Our current understanding of dendrite propagation derives largely from symmetric Li−Li cells with millimetre-thick electrolyte pellets, whereas practical cells will employ solid electrolyte separators less than 100 μm in thickness. In this work, we use in situ synchrotron X-ray computed tomography to show that dendrites in a thin Li6PS5Cl separator, which generally propagate from the lithium anode to the cathode, can be made to propagate laterally by the cathode. Volume contraction of the NMC cathode during charge places the thin separator under lateral compressive stress, deflecting dendritic cracks to propagate laterally (parallel to the electrodes) rather than transversely (across the separator). The result is that the cell resists short circuit even after passing 3 mA h cm−2 capacity at a rate of 3 mA cm−2. Replacing NMC with zero-volume-change pre-lithiated Li4Ti5O12 removes this compressive stress, and the cell rapidly fails by transverse cracking. Chemomechanical modelling rationalises both behaviours, with cathode volume change emerging as a design parameter that can suppress or accelerate failure, with direct implications for cathode selection and cathode/separator interface engineering in practical solid-state batteries.
n2216855ec587: Rare-earth hybrid nitrate double perovskites (REHNDPs) have recently emerged as an intriguing subclass of functional materials, combining structural diversity with rich intrinsic optoelectronic, magnetic, piezoelectric, and ferroelectric properties. Although notable progress has been made in three-dimensional (3D) and 2D REHNDPs, 1D counterparts have yet to be discovered. Herein, by introducing the bulky organic cation 1-adamantyltrimethylammonium (TMAA+), we report a family of 1D REHNDPs with the general formula (TMAA)2LnCs(NO3)6 (Ln = La3+, Ce3+, Pr3+, Nd3+, Sm3+, and Eu3+). Distinct from the μ2-κ3(O,O′,O″) mode characteristic of 2D and 3D REHNDPs, the bridging NO3− ligands adopt a μ2-κ3(O,O′) coordination mode in 1D counterparts. Strikingly, (TMAA)2SmCs(NO3)6 possesses a step-like high-temperature dielectric switch at 431.7 K. (TMAA)2EuCs(NO3)6 shows brilliant photoluminescence with a quantum yield of 65.46% and a lifetime of 5.21 ms. The X-ray detector based on (TMAA)2EuCs(NO3)6 demonstrates high X-ray sensitivity of 560 μC Gyair−1 cm−2 and a low detection limit of 153 nGyair s−1 under a bias of 25 V. This work bridges a critical dimensional gap and significantly expands the structural and functional portfolio of the REHNDPs.
n986a0e2cfb8f: Rechargeable Zn−air batteries (ZABs) have attracted considerable attention as promising energy storage systems owing to their high theoretical energy density and environmental compatibility. However, their practical application is hindered by the sluggish ORR/OER kinetics at the air cathode. This study investigates low Pt-modified Fe- and Ni-doped hexagonal perovskites (BaTi0.8M0.2O3−δ, M = Fe and Ni) as robust bifunctional oxygen electrocatalysts, focusing on the modulation of their participating metal and electronic structures. Structural analysis confirms the formation of stable hexagonal phases, while Pt deposition induces distinct electronic reconstruction depending on the dopant species. With a higher ORR catalytic behavior than the Pt/BTO-Ni catalyst, the Pt/BTO-Fe catalyst demonstrates remarkable bifunctionality driven through dopant-dependent surface interaction modulation by Pt with optimized surface/lattice oxygen distribution. Notably, in full-cell ZAB tests, the optimized Pt/BTO-Fe catalyst achieved a comparable peak power density of 124.8 mW cm−2 with a remarkably low round-trip efficiency decay rate of 0.41%/h under stable operation for 60 h, compared to the commercial IrO2 + Pt/C benchmark (125.2 mW cm−2 and 1.39%/h) even at lower Pt content. These findings highlight the critical role of Pt2+-mediated interfacial interactions in governing catalytic durability, providing a rational strategy for designing highly durable bifunctional electrocatalysts for next-generation energy storage systems.
n774c976db3fb: The number of possible crystal structures vastly exceeds the number realized among thermodynamically stable inorganic materials, suggesting that experimentally accessible structure space is organized around a limited set of preferred structural frameworks. Analysis of 23,160 structures on the thermodynamic convex hull identifies 6820 distinct structural frameworks, of which 2382 recur across multiple chemically distinct materials and are therefore classified as structural prototypes. Within a filtered dataset, metallic systems exhibit particularly strong structural recurrence, with 6270 materials grouped into 535 frameworks and 327 prototypes, while 5557 ionic compounds occupy 1704 frameworks and 696 prototypes. These results demonstrate that stable inorganic materials naturally coalesce into recurrent structural prototypes and do not require any a priori definition through manual curation. The resulting recurrence-based catalog also provides an empirical measure of framework prevalence, enabling the relative likelihood of structural frameworks in future materials to be estimated from their recurrence among known compounds.
n70e42d8e642f: To understand the nature of multicenter interactions in periodic solids and their associated materials (transport) properties, we investigate and quantify multicenter bonding on the basis of the underlying wave function, namely by a combination of quantum-chemical tools for a diverse series of functional materials. First, we probe all compounds by projected force constants based on plane-wave phonon calculations, followed by a projection from plane waves onto a local-orbital framework and its thorough quantum-chemical analysis. While the three-center crystal orbital bond index is used to quantify multicenter bonding between atomic orbitals, the linear combination of fragment orbitals provides a molecular-orbital lens. Eventually, both approaches are fused into the molecular orbital contribution index that directly attributes the contributions of a single molecular orbital to a multicenter bond.
n185e0085945e: SAPO-34 is an excellent catalyst for methanol-to-olefins (MTO) reaction. Simultaneously alleviating the diffusion limitations and optimizing the acidity of SAPO-34 is extremely challenging. Herein, a three-dimensional hollow square array SAPO-34 (SAPO-34-HSA) with a sinusoidal-like distribution of silicon was synthesized in a simple way. The role of triethylamine (TEA) switches between the etchant and structure-directing agent according to the reaction temperature. In the heating stage, the seed with high silicon content was etched by TEA; during the crystallization process, TEA guides the epitaxial growth of raw materials on the seed crystal, forming a hollow core−shell structure; after crystallization, the shell was partly leached to form a hollow square array structure. The sinusoidal-like distribution of silicon is conducive to promoting olefin cycling in the hydrocarbon pool mechanism and significantly improving the selectivity of ethylene. So the SAPO-34-HSA catalyst exhibits 70%−400% longer catalytic lifetime in MTO reaction compared with the seed under different reaction conditions.
na923104221b9: Amid escalating energy demand and severe environmental effects, green hydrogen production via water electrolysis has emerged as a cornerstone technology. Conventional alkaline water electrolysis (AWE) generally suffers from low hydrogen purity and current density, while proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) relies on high-cost noble-metal catalysts and harsh acidic conditions. To mitigate these limitations, researchers have turned to anion exchange membrane water electrolysis (AEMWE) as a promising alternative, offering an intermediate pathway that pairs the non-noble metal-based catalysts of AWE with the high purity and compact architecture of PEMWE. However, AEMWE technology remains comparatively underdeveloped. Herein, we have summarized transition metal chalcogenides (TMCs) as a low-cost catalyst platform for AEMWE devices. The current review focuses on a comparative analysis across the chalcogen family and discusses how variations in their physicochemical properties influence the overall catalytic performance of anion exchange membrane devices. In addition, the underlying mechanisms of AEMWE, the membrane-electrode assembly, and cell configurations have also been explored in detail. The review critically examines the intrinsic activity of the transition metal chalcogenide-based catalyst layer against device-level performance metrics and further highlights emerging future directions. The review aims to provide a clear roadmap toward the development of highly efficient and commercially competitive AEMWE systems for next-generation green hydrogen production.
n09b6b63883fd: Seawater electrolysis for green hydrogen production urgently demands high-performance electrocatalysts that simultaneously deliver fast reaction kinetics with robust chloride ion (Cl−) resistance. Herein, we report an ultralow Pt-loaded (<1 wt %) Pt/Fe2O3 catalyst rich in Pt−Fe atomic pairs synthesized via a photoreduction synthetic strategy. Photogenerated electrons drive the selective reduction of Pt precursors at low-coordinate Fe3+ sites on α-Fe2O3 (012) facets, constructing Pt−Fe pair interfaces that enable directional electron transfer from Fe-dz2 to Pt-dz2 orbitals. This electronic modulation optimizes the Gibbs free energy of hydrogen adsorption, weakens the intrinsic affinity of active sites toward Cl−, and accelerates water dissociation. The as-synthesized catalyst achieves ultralow overpotentials of 9 and 51 mV at 10 and 100 mA cm−2 respectively in alkaline simulated seawater, with a slight potential decay of only 0.08 mV h−1 over 1000 h of continuous operation, outperforming most state-of-the-art electrocatalysts. When integrated into an anion exchange membrane electrolyzer, it delivers a low cell voltage of 2.0 V at 500 mA cm−2 and maintains stable operation for 200 h at 100 mA cm−2.
